The year was around 60 AD. The Apostle Paul had been apprehended and almost killed in the Temple at Jerusalem by a mob of angry Jews.

A few days later, he had been whisked off to the Roman Procurator Felix because of danger from a group of Jewish plotters. Felix had heard his case and though there was no evidence to convict Paul, Felix had kept him in prison for the next two years until the new Procurator, Festus, took his place.

King Herod Agrippa II came to visit Festus and the two of them listened to Paul speak. During the hearing Paul …reasoned of righteousness, temperance, and judgment to come, [until finally] Felix trembled, and answered, Go thy way for this time; when I have a convenient season, I will call for thee –Acts 24:25. Then towards the end of Paul’s oration …Festus said with a loud voice, Paul, thou art beside thyself; much learning doth make thee mad –Acts 26:24.

Festus was not speaking of scientific knowledge, but of the fact that Paul was well-studied. Worse yet, Paul was making the governor uncomfortable with his sinful life and his reasoning made clear that the only solution for both Festus and Agrippa was to follow the Scriptures of the Hebrews.

Paul was well educated. He made clear in his letters and sermons, quoting not only from the Jewish Bible, but also from a variety of Greek and Cretan philosophers and poets.

In more modern times, it seems as though science is not a friend to faith. Many scientists claim that the idea of an intelligent designer of the Universe is ludicrous. Further, many of them would say that those who believe such things are the next thing to savages.

It certainly turns many Christians away from science entirely. They do not see something so antagonistic to the fundamental Christian faith as being useful.

I can understand this point of view, but I think that we should not give up learning simply because some of those who claim to be so knowledgeable are, in actuality, quite foolish.

Creation

When I think about the subject of science, I often begin with the subject of creation. This is the beginning of everything and is the first place where “science” and the Bible first come into conflict.

Science is simply unable to accept that there could have been a Creator God who set in motion everything that we see.

There are many books delving into the subject of intelligent design and seeing God’s fingerprints throughout creation. It takes a lot more faith to believe that the universe happened by chance, than to believe in a Creator.

The Bible makes it clear that God was not only present at the time of Creation, but it was also He who began it (John 1:1-3). Paul says For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse –Romans 1:20.

People should be able to discern that there is a Creator God involved in our world and the universe from the time of Creation. They should be able to understand a few other things about Him as well. Perhaps most important for our discussion here, we can tell by looking at creation that God is an orderly God and that He created the world to function with a specific structure and laws that govern it.

This is one of the big differences between the Creation account found in Genesis and the myths of creation found in other cultures of the time. The Bible makes it clear that God intentionally created the world, that He did so in an orderly fashion, and that He made certain that every part of it meshed with all the other parts. There is no magic or mystical thinking in the Genesis account.

The Laws of the Universe Still Stand

There are many people who believe that they can alter the way that the universe functions, that they can behave in immoral ways and not suffer the rewards of sin, and that they can do foolish things and not suffer the consequences of their behavior.

The Prophet Jeremiah tells us that there are laws which are in place that will not cease to function. Thus saith the LORD, which giveth the sun for a light by day, and the ordinances of the moon and of the stars for a light by night, which divideth the sea when the waves thereof roar; The LORD of hosts is his name: If those ordinances depart from before me, saith the LORD, then the seed of Israel also shall cease from being a nation before me for ever –Jeremiah 31:35-36.

There is a whole set of laws that governs the way that the earth rotates on its axis and orbits the sun. Everything from the speed of light to the way that gravity pulls things towards large bodies of mass was instituted at the time of Creation—…all things continue as they were from the beginning of the creation –2 Peter 3:4.

Since those laws continue and do not fluctuate, we are able to understand them—at least in part. This is what science is—the study of the natural world that we see and an attempt to comprehend the ways in which it works. God created our world in such a way that if you do an experiment the same way every time, you will get the same results every time.

Science Will Never Understand Everything

The Prophet Isaiah says, For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways, saith the LORD. For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts –Isaiah 55:8-9.

Even the smartest quantum physicists will admit that they don’t understand everything. In fact, the number of questions that they have is greater than the whole storehouse of knowledge that has been accumulated.

Most of us will have far less understanding of the universe than that. We won’t understand all the details of how the atom functions. We won’t be able to do the calculus necessary to put a satellite into orbit. That’s all right. The important thing is that we learn what we can in order to understand what an amazing and orderly God we serve.

Presuppositions are a Problem

The biggest problem that we see in science is not the science itself, rather it is the biases of the people performing the science. The fool hath said in his heart, There is no God… –Psalm 14:1. By this definition, many scientists are fools.

I don’t say this lightly. Atheists observe the universe and since they believe that there cannot be a God, they must then explain how it exists without the presence of an actual Creator. This is the heart of foolishness.

When they come to gaps in their knowledge, they are silent and yet the Christian can explain them in a few simple words. As I said before, when we look at the complexity of the universe, from the tiniest things to the largest galaxies, we can see the hands of God at work.

When I consider thy heavens, the work of thy fingers, the moon and the stars, which thou hast ordained; What is man, that thou art mindful of him? and the son of man, that thou visitest him? –Psalm 8:3-4. When we think about the world around us, when we read what scientists write, it is crucial that we come to it with a knowledge that God is behind all of this. For in him we live, and move, and have our being… – Acts 17:28, and nothing that science can discern will change that.

Science should be like a detective, uncovering God’s fingerprints on the universe, not someone bound and determined to discredit His very real presence.

Many Scientists Believe in God

Looking into the past, many scientists were men who believed in the God of the Bible. Isaac Newton, Francis Bacon, Nicholas Copernicus and many others believed in the Bible and were forthright in their expression of this faith to others.

In more modern days, there are many men and women of science who believe in the God of the Bible. Just because one is working in science doesn’t mean that they are unable to have a life of faith.

Many people have co-opted scientific discoveries to push messages that are against Christian belief and teaching.

We need to remember that when there is a set of facts, there are usually different explanations that can account for their presence. Creation and evolution examine the same facts of nature, yet from a different perspective or bias, thus they end up with vastly different conclusions. Perhaps it is a little like a Sherlock Holmes story, where Dr. Watson routinely takes the facts and gives an inaccurate explanation of them, while the detective takes the same information and gives the right explanation.

Science and Medicine

It is not against Scripture to research how things work in our universe, as long as we do so within a Biblical framework and understanding that there is a Creator God who is ordering it all.

Modern medicine is an application of many various fields, including anatomy, microanatomy, genetics, and biochemistry. The point, in this case, is to observe the human body the best that we can and then to fix the things that go wrong with it. Doctors can be scientists, but most of them are simply applying knowledge which has been passed down to them through their training.

Observation is where things start. Let’s consider diabetes as an example. Aretaeus of Cappadocia in the second century AD was the first person to give a complete description of diabetes and actually gave the disease the name diabetes. The problem was that while he was able to diagnose people with this illness, he had no treatment to help his patients. Observation had only taken him so far.

Over time, other work was done that demonstrated that the problem was an issue in the pancreas and that something was specifically wrong with the islet cells. Even into the early 1900s, there was no cure for Diabetes Mellitus and the only solution that doctors had to offer was an extremely low glycemic diet with severe calorie limits—attempting to keep patients at 500 or 600 calories a day. As can be imagined, this wasn’t an ideal treatment.

It wasn’t until the 1920s that a couple of researchers in Canada discovered a way to extract insulin from dogs and administered it to a 14-year-old who was dying of diabetes. The extract saved his life and began a new era for people with diabetes.

This is the way that things work. We begin by observing a disease and various medications that seem to be effective for it, then over time and through meticulous testing we can assess what treatments are most effective for that illness.

Studies in which half of the participants with a disease are given a medication or treatment and half are given a placebo (a pill without medical efficacy) are still the most effective way of telling whether something really works.

Why Treatments Need to be Studied

There is a real tendency to believe that the things that you have been taught are effective. We know that George Washington died of pneumonia. His doctors probably damaged his chances of recovery by bleeding him four times for a total of close to 40 percent of his blood volume. They probably would have bled him a fifth time, but he wasn’t thought to be strong enough to survive the procedure.

Doctors bled patients because they believed that there were toxic build ups in the blood stream that had to be let out. Most of the people who died after bloodletting would probably have died anyway, but bleeding people who are really sick certainly doesn’t help them recover.

Maybe the doctors simply wanted to be doing something. Patients expected bloodletting and so they met those expectations, even though it harmed the patients.

Experience is what lets you make the same mistakes with a lot more confidence.

What Makes a Good Study

Good studies—have plenty of patients in them, have a control group (that either receives an inactive pill called a placebo, or the current best treatment for that disease), and have the test group getting the new treatment. It is also important for the control group and the test group to be matched as closely as possible. Finally, the size of the groups in the study is vital to the conclusions of the study. If there are only ten or twenty patients in the study, it is not a large enough group to really sort out if something works or doesn’t.

For many diseases there is something called a placebo effect. This placebo effect is when people get better from an illness even though they are not receiving something that should be effective at treating the malady. Interestingly, in studies, many people get side effects from the inert pills. If 20 percent of the people getting the placebo get better and 45 percent of the people getting the treatment get better, that would indicate that the treatment is effective. If the difference is minimal—say 20 percent of the placebo group and 23 percent of the treatment group improve—then the treatment isn’t effective.

Problems

The biggest problem with many treatments is that they simply aren’t studied. Vitamin supplements and herbal compounds may work, but many of them have never actually been studied in a trial comparing them with a control group. Most of the information is anecdotal. The fact that someone’s grandmother or uncle benefited from something is possibly an indication that it is effective, but it doesn’t tell us how effective this treatment is or what dosage level is ideal.

Another issue is when studies simply don’t have enough participants to really give accurate information. Many studies only include ten or twenty patients. That is simply not enough to identify how well a treatment works or what side effects can be expected. For a drug to be approved by the FDA, it will typically have been studied on between 1,000 to 3,000 patients with the disease.

A final issue with studies is when they show that a medication is effective, but the effect isn’t clinically significant. As an example, a new injectable medication for dementia (aducanumab) was recently approved by the FDA. It is very expensive, and the benefit seemed to be small. Patients who were on it got an average of 1.5 more test questions right on an 85-question mental status questionnaire after 18 months compared to the control group.

One can rightly question if the benefits shown by this medication are worth the 50,000 dollar-per-year cost. More than that, how much of a meaningful improvement in someone’s everyday activities would come from using such a medicine? It seems unlikely that it would make very much of a difference.

It is unfortunate, but drug companies will always try to make it seem like their medicine is the best, even if the studies do not show significant benefit over existing, cheaper options.

Conclusion

Christians are faced with a world which does not love them or their beliefs. Many would try to use science as a way to bludgeon them into giving up their faith. I hope that does not lead us to give up on the scientific method or to give up attempting to understand the laws behind the universe that God created.

The scientific method is valid, even if many of the people who use it are atheists or agnostics. If a treatment works, it should be observable, testable, and repeatable.

Even as we approach it, we have a basic understanding of the universe that atheists don’t have. Knowing that there is a Creator God who loves us makes a major difference as we interpret the results of all the different observations that are being made in the fields of medicine and other places.

Those who do not know God are bound to be ever learning, and never able to come to the knowledge of the truth –2 Timothy 3:7. On the other hand, if we begin with a Biblical understanding, we can use science as a tool to help us to understand the creation that He has placed around us.

L’anno era circa il 60 d.C. L’apostolo Paolo era stato arrestato e quasi ucciso nel Tempio di Gerusalemme da una folla di ebrei inferociti.

Pochi giorni dopo era stato portato dal procuratore romano Felice a causa del pericolo rappresentato da un gruppo di cospiratori ebrei. Felice aveva ascoltato il suo caso e, benché non ci fosse alcuna prova per condannare Paolo, lo aveva tenuto in prigione per i due anni successivi, fino a quando il nuovo procuratore, Festo, non prese il suo posto.

Il re Agrippa II venne a far visita a Festo e i due ascoltarono Paolo parlare. Durante l’udienza Paolo …discuteva di giustizia, di autocontrollo e del giudizio che deve venire, [fino a quando] Felice tremò e disse: Vattene per ora; quando avrò tempo ti chiamerò – Atti 24:25. Poi, verso la fine dell’orazione di Paolo, …Festo, con voce forte, disse: Paolo, sei fuori di te; molto sapere ti fa impazzire – Atti 26:24.

Festo non parlava di conoscenze scientifiche, ma del fatto che Paolo era ben istruito. Peggio ancora, Paolo stava mettendo a disagio il governatore riguardo alla sua vita peccaminosa e il suo ragionamento rendeva chiaro che l’unica soluzione per Festo e per Agrippa era seguire le Scritture degli Ebrei.

Paolo era ben istruito. Lo chiarisce nelle sue lettere e nei suoi sermoni, citando non solo la Bibbia ebraica, ma anche una varietà di filosofi e poeti greci e cretesi.

In tempi più moderni, sembra che la scienza non sia amica della fede. Molti scienziati affermano che l’idea di un progettista intelligente dell’Universo sia ridicola. Inoltre, molti di loro direbbero che coloro che credono a tali cose sono quasi dei selvaggi.

Questo certamente allontana molti cristiani dalla scienza del tutto. Non vedono qualcosa di così antagonista alla fede cristiana fondamentale come utile.

Posso comprendere questo punto di vista, ma penso che non dovremmo rinunciare all’apprendimento semplicemente perché alcuni di coloro che si dichiarano tanto competenti sono, in realtà, piuttosto stolti.

Creazione

Quando penso al tema della scienza, spesso comincio con il soggetto della creazione. Questo è l’inizio di tutto ed è il primo luogo in cui “scienza” e Bibbia vengono in conflitto.

La scienza è semplicemente incapace di accettare che possa esserci stato un Dio Creatore che ha messo in moto tutto ciò che vediamo.

Esistono molti libri che trattano il tema del disegno intelligente e del vedere le impronte digitali di Dio nella creazione. Ci vuole molta più fede per credere che l’universo sia avvenuto per caso, che per credere in un Creatore.

La Bibbia chiarisce che Dio non solo era presente al momento della Creazione, ma che fu egli a iniziarla (Giovanni 1:1-3). Paolo dice Poiché le cose invisibili di lui, fin dalla creazione del mondo, si intendono per mezzo delle opere; così che essi sono inescusabili: avendo mostrato la sua eterna potenza e divinità – Romani 1:20.

Le persone dovrebbero essere in grado di discernere che c’è un Dio Creatore coinvolto nel nostro mondo e nell’universo fin dal tempo della Creazione. Dovrebbero anche poter comprendere alcune altre cose su di lui. Forse la più importante per la nostra discussione qui è che, osservando la creazione, possiamo dire che Dio è un Dio ordinato e che ha creato il mondo per funzionare con una struttura specifica e leggi che lo governano.

Questa è una delle grandi differenze tra il racconto della Creazione trovato in Genesi e i miti della creazione presenti in altre culture dell’epoca. La Bibbia rende chiaro che Dio ha creato intenzionalmente il mondo, che lo fece in modo ordinato e che fece in modo che ogni sua parte si integrasse con tutte le altre parti. Non c’è magia né pensiero mistico nel racconto della Genesi.

Le leggi dell’universo restano valide

Ci sono molte persone che credono di poter alterare il modo in cui l’universo funziona, di poter comportarsi in modi immorali senza subirne le conseguenze, e di poter fare sciocchezze senza pagare il prezzo del loro comportamento.

Il profeta Geremia ci dice che ci sono leggi in vigore che non cesseranno di funzionare. Così parla il SIGNORE, che dà il sole per luce del giorno, e le leggi della luna e delle stelle per luce della notte, che divide il mare quando le sue onde brontolano; il SIGNORE degli eserciti è il suo nome: Se quelle leggi venissero meno davanti a me, dice il SIGNORE, allora anche la stirpe d’Israele cesserebbe per sempre d’essere una nazione davanti a me – Geremia 31:35-36.

Esiste tutto un insieme di leggi che governa il modo in cui la terra ruota sul suo asse e orbita intorno al sole. Tutto, dalla velocità della luce al modo in cui la gravità attrae le cose verso grandi masse, fu istituito al momento della Creazione—…tutte le cose continuano come fin dall’inizio della creazione – 2 Pietro 3:4.

Poiché quelle leggi continuano e non fluttuano, siamo in grado di comprenderle—almeno in parte. Questo è ciò che è la scienza: lo studio del mondo naturale che vediamo e un tentativo di comprendere i modi in cui funziona. Dio ha creato il nostro mondo in modo tale che se fai un esperimento nello stesso modo ogni volta, otterrai gli stessi risultati ogni volta.

La scienza non comprenderà mai tutto

Il profeta Isaia dice, Poiché i miei pensieri non sono i vostri pensieri, né le vostre vie le mie vie, dice il SIGNORE. Come sono più alti i cieli della terra, così sono più alte le mie vie delle vostre vie e i miei pensieri dei vostri pensieri – Isaia 55:8-9.

Anche i più intelligenti fisici quantistici ammetteranno di non comprendere tutto. Infatti, il numero delle domande che hanno è maggiore dell’intero magazzino di conoscenza accumulato.

La maggior parte di noi avrà una comprensione dell’universo molto inferiore. Non capiremo tutti i dettagli di come funziona l’atomo. Non saremo in grado di fare il calcolo necessario per mettere in orbita un satellite. Va bene così. La cosa importante è che apprendiamo ciò che possiamo per comprendere che Dio che serviamo è stupendo e ordinato.

Le presupposizioni sono un problema

Il problema più grande che vediamo nella scienza non è la scienza stessa, ma i pregiudizi delle persone che la praticano. Il pazzo ha detto nel suo cuore: Non c’è Dio… – Salmo 14:1. Per questa definizione, molti scienziati sono stolti.

Non lo dico a cuor leggero. Gli atei osservano l’universo e, dato che credono che non possa esistere un Dio, devono allora spiegare come esso esista senza la presenza di un vero Creatore. Questo è il cuore della stoltezza.

Quando arrivano a buchi nella loro conoscenza, stanno zitti, mentre il cristiano può spiegarli con poche parole semplici. Come ho detto prima, quando guardiamo alla complessità dell’universo, dalle cose più piccole alle galassie più grandi, possiamo vedere le mani di Dio all’opera.

Quando considero i tuoi cieli, opera delle tue dita, la luna e le stelle che tu hai fissate; che cos’è l’uomo perché te ne ricordi? e il figlio dell’uomo perché te ne curi? – Salmo 8:3-4. Quando pensiamo al mondo intorno a noi, quando leggiamo ciò che gli scienziati scrivono, è cruciale avvicinarsi con la consapevolezza che Dio è dietro tutto questo. Perché in lui viviamo, ci muoviamo e siamo – Atti 17:28, e nulla di ciò che la scienza può discernere cambierà questo.

La scienza dovrebbe essere come un detective, che scopre le impronte digitali di Dio nell’universo, non qualcuno deciso a smentire la Sua presenza molto reale.

Molti scienziati credono in Dio

Guardando al passato, molti scienziati erano uomini che credevano nel Dio della Bibbia. Isaac Newton, Francis Bacon, Niccolò Copernico e molti altri credevano nella Bibbia e lo esprimevano apertamente.

In tempi più moderni, ci sono molti uomini e donne di scienza che credono nel Dio della Bibbia. Il fatto di lavorare nella scienza non significa che non si possa avere una vita di fede.

Molte persone hanno strumentalizzato le scoperte scientifiche per promuovere messaggi contrari alla fede e all’insegnamento cristiano.

Dobbiamo ricordare che di fronte a un insieme di fatti, di solito esistono diverse spiegazioni che possono rendere conto della loro presenza. Creazione ed evoluzione esaminano gli stessi fatti della natura, ma da prospettive o pregiudizi diversi, e finiscono così per arrivare a conclusioni molto differenti. Forse è un po’ come una storia di Sherlock Holmes, dove il dottor Watson prende i fatti e fornisce regolarmente una spiegazione inaccurata, mentre il detective prende le stesse informazioni e fornisce la spiegazione giusta.

Scienza e medicina

Non è contrario alle Scritture ricercare come funzionano le cose nel nostro universo, purché lo si faccia all’interno di un quadro biblico e con la comprensione che esiste un Dio Creatore che lo ordina tutto.

La medicina moderna è un’applicazione di molti campi diversi, compresa l’anatomia, la microanatomia, la genetica e la biochimica. Lo scopo, in questo caso, è osservare il corpo umano al meglio possibile e poi riparare le cose che vanno storte. I medici possono essere scienziati, ma la maggior parte di loro applica semplicemente conoscenze tramandate attraverso la loro formazione.

L’osservazione è il punto di partenza. Consideriamo il diabete come esempio. Areteo di Cappadocia nel II secolo d.C. fu il primo a dare una descrizione completa del diabete e a dare alla malattia il nome di diabete. Il problema era che, pur essendo in grado di diagnosticare le persone con questa malattia, non aveva alcun trattamento per aiutare i suoi pazienti. L’osservazione lo aveva portato solo fino a un certo punto.

Col tempo, altri studi dimostrarono che il problema era un’anomalia nel pancreas e che c’era qualcosa di specificamente sbagliato nelle cellule delle isole. Anche nei primi anni del 1900 non esisteva una cura per il diabete mellito e l’unica soluzione che i medici potevano offrire era una dieta a bassissimo indice glicemico con limiti calorici severi—cercando di mantenere i pazienti a 500 o 600 calorie al giorno. Come si può immaginare, non era un trattamento ideale.

Fu solo negli anni ’20 che un paio di ricercatori in Canada scoprirono un modo per estrarre l’insulina dai cani e la somministrarono a un quattordicenne che stava morendo di diabete. L’estratto gli salvò la vita e iniziò una nuova era per le persone con diabete.

Questo è il modo in cui funzionano le cose. Si comincia osservando una malattia e vari farmaci che sembrano efficaci, poi col tempo e con test meticolosi si può valutare quali trattamenti sono più efficaci per quella malattia.

Gli studi in cui metà dei partecipanti affetti da una malattia ricevono un farmaco o un trattamento e l’altra metà riceve un placebo (una pillola senza efficacia medica) sono ancora il modo più efficace per stabilire se qualcosa funziona davvero.

Perché i trattamenti devono essere studiati

Esiste una reale tendenza a credere che le cose che ti sono state insegnate siano efficaci. Sappiamo che George Washington morì di polmonite. I suoi medici probabilmente danneggiarono le sue possibilità di recupero emorragizzandolo quattro volte per un totale di quasi il 40 percento del suo volume di sangue. Probabilmente lo avrebbero emorragizzato una quinta volta, ma non si ritenne che fosse abbastanza forte da sopravvivere alla procedura.

I medici emorragizzavano i pazienti perché ritenevano che vi fossero accumuli tossici nel flusso sanguigno che dovevano essere eliminati. La maggior parte delle persone che morivano dopo la salassazione probabilmente sarebbe morte comunque, ma praticare la salassazione su persone gravemente malate sicuramente non aiuta la loro guarigione.

Forse i medici semplicemente volevano fare qualcosa. I pazienti si aspettavano la salassazione e quindi si soddisfacevano quelle aspettative, anche se ciò danneggiava i pazienti.

L’esperienza è ciò che ti permette di commettere gli stessi errori con molta più fiducia.

Cosa rende uno studio valido

I buoni studi—hanno molti pazienti, hanno un gruppo di controllo (che riceve o una pillola inattiva chiamata placebo, o il miglior trattamento attuale per quella malattia), e il gruppo di test riceve il nuovo trattamento. È anche importante che il gruppo di controllo e il gruppo di test siano abbinati il più possibile. Infine, la dimensione dei gruppi nello studio è vitale per le conclusioni dello studio. Se ci sono solo dieci o venti pazienti nello studio, non è un gruppo abbastanza numeroso per capire davvero se qualcosa funziona o no.

Per molte malattie esiste un effetto placebo. Questo effetto placebo è quando le persone guariscono da una malattia anche se non stanno ricevendo qualcosa che dovrebbe essere efficace per curare il male. È interessante che, negli studi, molte persone riportino effetti collaterali anche dalle pillole inattive. Se il 20 percento delle persone che prendono il placebo migliora e il 45 percento delle persone che prendono il trattamento migliora, ciò indicherebbe che il trattamento è efficace. Se la differenza è minima—per esempio il 20 percento del gruppo placebo e il 23 percento del gruppo in trattamento migliorano—allora il trattamento non è efficace.

Problemi

Il problema più grande con molti trattamenti è che semplicemente non sono studiati. Integratori vitaminici e composti erboristici possono funzionare, ma molti di essi non sono mai stati effettivamente studiati in una prova che li confronti con un gruppo di controllo. La maggior parte delle informazioni è aneddotica. Il fatto che la nonna o lo zio di qualcuno abbia tratto beneficio da qualcosa è forse un’indicazione che è efficace, ma non ci dice quanto sia efficace questo trattamento o quale livello di dosaggio sia ideale.

Un altro problema è quando gli studi semplicemente non hanno abbastanza partecipanti per fornire informazioni accurate. Molti studi includono solo dieci o venti pazienti. Questo non è sufficiente per identificare quanto bene funzioni un trattamento o quali effetti collaterali ci si possa aspettare. Perché un farmaco sia approvato dalla FDA, di solito è stato studiato su tra 1.000 e 3.000 pazienti affetti dalla malattia.

Un ultimo problema con gli studi è quando mostrano che un farmaco è efficace, ma l’effetto non è clinicamente significativo. Ad esempio, un nuovo farmaco iniettabile per la demenza (aducanumab) è stato recentemente approvato dalla FDA. È molto costoso e il beneficio sembra essere limitato. I pazienti che lo assumevano rispondevano in media a 1,5 domande in più su un questionario di stato mentale di 85 domande dopo 18 mesi rispetto al gruppo di controllo.

Ci si può giustamente chiedere se i benefici mostrati da questo farmaco valgano il costo di 50.000 dollari all’anno. Ancora di più, quanto miglioramento significativo nelle attività quotidiane di una persona deriverebbe dall’uso di un tale medicinale? Sembra improbabile che faccia molta differenza.

È sfortunato, ma le compagnie farmaceutiche cercheranno sempre di far sembrare il loro medicinale il migliore, anche se gli studi non mostrano un beneficio significativo rispetto alle opzioni esistenti e più economiche.

Conclusione

I cristiani si trovano di fronte a un mondo che non li ama né ama le loro convinzioni. Molti cercherebbero di usare la scienza per costringerli a rinunciare alla fede. Spero che questo non ci porti a rinunciare al metodo scientifico o a rinunciare a tentare di capire le leggi dietro l’universo che Dio ha creato.

Il metodo scientifico è valido, anche se molte delle persone che lo usano sono atei o agnostici. Se un trattamento funziona, dovrebbe essere osservabile, testabile e ripetibile.

Anche nell’approcciarlo, abbiamo una comprensione di base dell’universo che gli atei non hanno. Sapere che esiste un Dio Creatore che ci ama fa una grande differenza quando interpretiamo i risultati delle diverse osservazioni compiute nei campi della medicina e in altri ambiti.

Coloro che non conoscono Dio sono destinati a essere sempre intenti ad imparare, e mai in grado di giungere alla conoscenza della verità – 2 Timoteo 3:7. D’altra parte, se cominciamo con una comprensione biblica, possiamo usare la scienza come uno strumento per aiutarci a comprendere la creazione che Egli ha posto intorno a noi.

The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised, To preach the acceptable year of the Lord –Luke 4:18-19.

Jesus was in His hometown of Nazareth. It was on the Sabbath, and He stood to read the scripture as He had in the past. This Sabbath He read from Isaiah 61. When He finished, He said, …This day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears –Luke 4:21.

This marked the beginning of Jesus’ earthly ministry. In this first sermon He described the nature of His ministry. Notice the many references in this passage to healing: healing to the brokenhearted, deliverance to the captives, recovering of sight to the blind, and liberty to the bruised. Jesus came to provide a remedy for our brokenness. He came to repair the damage that sin has brought into humanity.

In this article we will look at the possibility for healing that is found in Jesus. Healing is a process that requires inner restoration with outside remediation. Physical healing begins at the cellular level and restores physical function. Spiritual healing begins at the heart level and restores us to fullness of life. Jesus said, …I am come that they might have life, and that they might have it more abundantly – John 10:10.

As Jesus walked the dusty paths of Judea, He encountered many who needed physical healing. It was His ability to heal that drew many to seek Him out and to follow him. Many brought their friends and family to Him for healing. There is in all of us a desire for healing and wholeness. In the garden of Eden, mankind was created to be whole. When we are not whole, we seek every possible cure. So, crowds gathered around Jesus hoping for healing.

One day as Jesus was journeying through Jericho, a blind man, Bartimaeus, heard that He was approaching. Hope sprang up in his breast. He began to call out to Jesus, “Jesus, thou son of David, have mercy on me.” They tried to silence him, but he called the louder, “Jesus, thou son of David, have mercy on me.”

He cast his coat aside and blindly rushed into the street. Jesus said to him, “What wilt thou that I should do unto thee?” He said, “Lord, that I might receive my sight.” Jesus’ response to this simple faith was, “Go thy way; thy faith hath made thee whole.” Immediately, he received his sight, and followed Jesus. This is just one example of Jesus’ healing ministry. The examples are many. He healed lepers. He healed paralytics. He healed men and women of unclean spirits.

Does Jesus still heal in our day? I would like to answer that question by sharing my own journey of healing. I realize that not all are healed. Even in Jesus’ day, not all were healed. But I want to share my journey of healing to demonstrate the interconnectedness of the physical and the spiritual.

I was diagnosed with cancer in May of 2020. Hearing a doctor say, “You have millions of cancer cells in your body”, brought me face to face with my mortality like never before. Oh, I knew that someday I would die, but that was always somewhere in the far distant future. Now I needed to face the fact that I had a disease growing within me which had the potential to destroy my body.

Is any sick among you? let him call for the elders of the church; and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord: And the prayer of faith shall save the sick, and the Lord shall raise him up; and if he have committed sins, they shall be forgiven him. Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed. The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much –James 5:14-16.

I have always been a strong advocate of anointing with oil. Just like we are taught in the book of James, I called for the elders of the church and asked them to anoint me with oil. In the biblical teaching of God healing through the anointing with oil there are a number of things that are expected of those seeking the healing. There is: call[ing] for the elders of the church, the prayer of faith, pray[ing] one for another, Confess[ing] your faults one to another, the effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man… and the list goes on. So, one of the necessities to seek healing through the anointing with oil is the clearing of the heart of any known, unconfessed sin. Hence, I searched my heart and cleansed my heart of anything that would hinder God’s healing of my body.

Notice the close correlation in this passage between the physical and the spiritual. I found in my journey of healing that the one affects the other. Physical healing begins with spiritual healing. A few drops of oil have no therapeutic benefit. This anointing with oil is primarily a spiritual exercise. If we practice this ordinance as James offered it, we cleanse our hearts inwardly and then we ask God for physical healing.

This was my first step to healing, but a long journey lay ahead. We consulted with multiple doctors and eventually we chose a treatment protocol that included radiation and hormone therapy. This treatment weakened me physically and made me feel my humanity. It made me more dependent on God and others and less confident in my own abilities. Living with weakness caused me to draw my strength from my Heavenly Father Who is the source of strength. I relied heavily on the encouragement and support that my wife and family offered.

There are some lessons that can only be learned through human weakness. It was for this reason that Paul was given a thorn in the flesh. He sought the Lord three times for healing. God’s answer came back always the same, “My grace is sufficient for you, for my strength is made perfect in your weakness.” I can testify that that is true.

I had multiple radiation treatments in January of 2021. I had scheduled a series of meetings for the month of February thinking that my treatments would be over, and I would be back to normal. What I did not realize was the delayed effect of radiation. I breezed through the treatments, but in February I experienced a lot of digestive issues and a lot of physical weakness.

I was expected to deliver a series of four sermons on four consecutive evenings. We prayed and although I could not get through the day without napping God provided supernatural strength for those evening messages. I praise God that His strength was made perfect in my weakness.

My doctors have plied their trade. I am grateful for the professional medical care that I received. I have done what I could with herbs and supplements and God has been merciful. My last bloodwork came back “undetectable”. May God be praised!

I am sharing my experience to show the correlation between the physical and the spiritual. Physical illness in my experience had a sanctifying effect on my spirit and spiritual renewal conditioned my body for healing. I will be forever grateful for the professional care given by my doctors, but even they realize the limits of their profession. On my last visit to my Medical Oncologist, he said to me, “Now we are going to trust the Lord.” Thank God for God-fearing doctors!

There are several examples in scripture that demonstrate this correlation between physical and spiritual healing. In Mark 2 when they let the paralytic down through the roof into the presence of Jesus, He said to the paralytic, “Thy sins be forgiven thee.” Then He said, “Rise up and walk.” When He was challenged by the Pharisees for forgiving sins, He said to them, “Which is easier to say rise up and walk or thy sins be forgiven”, demonstrating that He had the power to do both. If we believe that Jesus has the power to forgive our sins, do we also believe that He has the power to heal our bodies? I do!

In John 5, Jesus healed a man who lay by the pool of Bethesda. He had this infirmity for thirty-eight years. Jesus came by and healed him. Later when He met him in the temple He said to him, “Behold, thou art made whole: sin no more, lest a worse thing come unto thee.” Note the correlation between the physical and the spiritual.

Physical infirmity has a tremendous potential to open our hearts to spiritual realities if we allow it to. The Psalmist said: Before I was afflicted I went astray: but now have I kept thy word –Psalm 119:67. Jesus said: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised, To preach the acceptable year of the Lord –Luke 4:18-19.

Take a fresh look at our proof text for this article and notice that Jesus is offering more than physical healing. He promises healing to the brokenhearted, deliverance to the captives, and liberty to the bruised. These promises are of emotional healing—healing for the hurt that we receive as a result of living in a broken, sin-cursed world.

I am sure that there are many people reading this article who have experienced trauma that I know nothing about. But I want to assure you that you can be healed. Do you believe that? Do you believe that the pain can go away? Do you believe that you can be delivered from fear, anxiety, anger, and bitterness?

We addressed the correlation between spiritual and physical healing. There is also a correlation between spiritual and emotional healing. If you are experiencing a broken heart, Jesus wants to heal your broken heart. If you are a captive—if you are bound to a past or to an addiction that prevents your freedom—Jesus will set you free. If you have been bruised Jesus will heal you.

My wife and I are appalled at the large number of people in our Anabaptist churches that are turning to psych drugs (mind medication) and secular counseling to find solutions for emotional disorders. The Bible addresses most emotional disorders:

Fear

  • There is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear –1 John 4:18.
  • What time I am afraid, I will trust in thee –Psalm 56:3.
  • “Fear not” is found 63 times in the Bible

Anxiety

  • Be careful [anxious] for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God –Philippians 4:6.

Anger

  • Let all bitterness, and wrath, and anger, and clamour, and evil speaking, be put away from you, with all malice –Ephesians 4:31.

This is just a sampling of emotional disorders that we encounter in life, and I realize that behind these emotions there is often deep-seated trauma. Your trauma is not an astonishment to Jesus. He may not have experienced your exact trauma, but he has gone to the depth of your pain, and he has come through it in victory.

For we have not an high priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities; but was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin. Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need –Hebrews 4:15-16.

The gospel provides a holistic remedy to man’s sin problem. Our Anabaptist heritage has emphasized the fact that faith in Jesus affects every area of our lives. This faith motivates us to follow Jesus in very practical ways in our daily lives. This results in a life of radical nonconformity to the world around us.

This radical discipleship should also affect our emotional responses to difficult people and circumstances. Or have we become so emotionally fragile that if life does not give us exactly what we want it upsets our emotional equilibrium? Or maybe the gospel that we preach has become a litany of words that appeases the mind but has no effect on our soul.

Let us therefore fear, lest, a promise being left us of entering into his rest, any of you should seem to come short of it. For unto us was the gospel preached, as well as unto them: but the word preached did not profit them, not being mixed with faith in them that heard it –Hebrews 4:1-2. Is our faith in God so weak (remember that in the Biblical accounts of healing, it was their faith that enabled the healing) that we have more faith in medication or in a board-certified secular counselor than we have in God and His Word?

This is a discipleship series. Come with me to the mountain where Jesus is teaching. Yes, there is a large crowd, but follow me closely, we will try to get close enough to hear. I hear His voice—He is saying something about “salt of the earth” and “light of the world.” Here is an empty space—just room for two. Let’s sit on the grass and listen:

“Ye have heard that it hath been said, An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth: But I say unto you, That ye resist not evil: but whosoever shall smite thee on thy right cheek, turn to him the other also.

And if any man will sue thee at the law, and take away thy coat, let him have thy cloak also. And whosoever shall compel thee to go a mile, go with him twain. Give to him that asketh thee, and from him that would borrow of thee turn not thou away.

Ye have heard that it hath been said, Thou shalt love thy neighbour, and hate thine enemy. But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you; That ye may be the children of your Father which is in heaven: for he maketh his sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and sendeth rain on the just and on the unjust.”

These are radical teachings. Radical in that they are so opposite from our natural inclinations, and yet, this is the way of peace. Most of our negative emotions such as anger, fear, and anxiety can be remedied by applying these teachings of Jesus to our situations. This may sound overly simplistic, but that is the nature of the gospel and millions of people have found life and freedom through faith in Christ.

Bless the LORD, O my soul: and all that is within me, bless his holy name. Bless the LORD, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits: Who forgiveth all thine iniquities; who healeth all thy diseases; Who redeemeth thy life from destruction; who crowneth thee with lovingkindness and tender mercies; Who satisfieth thy mouth with good things; so that thy youth is renewed like the eagle’s –Psalm 103:1-5.

De Geest des Heren is op mij, omdat Hij mij gezalfd heeft om het evangelie te prediken voor de armen; Hij heeft mij gezonden om de gebrokenen van hart te genezen, om vrijspraak te prediken aan de gevangenen, en het zien te herstellen aan de blinden, om vrijlating te brengen aan de gekneuvelden, To preach the acceptable year of the Lord – Lukas 4:18-19.

Jezus was in Zijn geboorteplaats Nazareth. Het was op de sabbat, en Hij stond op om de Schrift te lezen zoals Hij dat vroeger deed. Deze sabbat las Hij uit Jesaja 61. Toen Hij klaar was, zei Hij, …Deze dag is deze Schrift in uw oren vervuld – Lukas 4:21.

Dit markeerde het begin van Jezus’ aardse bediening. In deze eerste prediking beschreef Hij de aard van Zijn bediening. Let op de vele verwijzingen in deze passage naar genezing: genezing voor de gebrokenen van hart, bevrijding voor de gevangenen, het teruggeven van het zicht aan de blinden, en bevrijding voor de gekneuvelden. Jezus kwam om een remedie te bieden voor onze gebrokenheid. Hij kwam om de schade te herstellen die de zonde in de mensheid heeft gebracht.

In dit artikel zullen we kijken naar de mogelijkheid van genezing die in Jezus wordt gevonden. Genezing is een proces dat innerlijke herstelwerkzaamheden met uiterlijke remediëring vereist. Fysieke genezing begint op cellulair niveau en herstelt lichamelijke functie. Geestelijke genezing begint op hartniveau en herstelt ons tot volheid van leven. Jezus zei, …Ik ben gekomen opdat zij het leven zouden hebben, en het te meer in overvloed – Johannes 10:10.

Terwijl Jezus over de stoffige paden van Judea liep, ontmoette Hij velen die lichamelijke genezing nodig hadden. Het was Zijn vermogen om te genezen dat velen ertoe bracht Hem te zoeken en Hem te volgen. Velen brachten hun vrienden en familie naar Hem voor genezing. In ons allemaal is er een verlangen naar genezing en heelheid. In de tuin van Eden werd de mens geschapen om heel te zijn. Wanneer we niet heel zijn, zoeken we elk mogelijk geneesmiddel. Zo verzamelden zich mensenmassa’s rond Jezus in de hoop op genezing.

Op een dag, terwijl Jezus door Jericho trok, hoorde een blinde man, Bartimeüs, dat Hij naderde. Hoop steeg op in zijn hart. Hij begon Jezus toe te roepen: “Jezus, Zoon van David, ontferm U over mij.” Zij probeerden hem het zwijgen op te leggen, maar hij riep luider: “Jezus, Zoon van David, ontferm U over mij.”

Hij wierp zijn jas af en snelde blindelings de straat op. Jezus zei tegen hem: “Wat wilt u dat Ik u doe?” Hij zei: “Heer, opdat ik mijn gezichtsvermogen mag ontvangen.” Jezus’ antwoord op dit eenvoudige geloof was: “Ga heen; uw geloof heeft u verlost.” Meteen ontving hij zijn gezicht en volgde Jezus. Dit is slechts één voorbeeld van Jezus’ genezende bediening. De voorbeelden zijn talrijk. Hij genas melaatsen. Hij genas verlamden. Hij genas mannen en vrouwen van onreine geesten.

Heet Jezus vandaag de dag nog steeds genezen? Ik wil die vraag beantwoorden door mijn eigen genezingsweg te delen. Ik besef dat niet allen genezen worden. Zelfs ten tijde van Jezus werden niet allen genezen. Maar ik wil mijn genezingsweg delen om de onderlinge verbondenheid van het fysieke en het geestelijke aan te tonen.

In mei 2020 werd bij mij kanker vastgesteld. Een arts horen zeggen: “U heeft miljoenen kankercellen in uw lichaam” bracht mij als nooit tevoren oog in oog met mijn sterfelijkheid. O, ik wist dat ik op een dag zou sterven, maar dat was altijd ergens ver in de toekomst. Nu moest ik onder ogen zien dat ik een ziekte in mij had die de potentie had mijn lichaam te vernietigen.

Is iemand van u ziek? Laat hij de ouderlingen van de gemeente roepen; en laat zij over hem bidden en hem zalven met olie in de naam des Heren: En het gebed des geloofs zal de zieke behouden, en de Here zal hem oprichten; en indien hij zonden heeft gedaan, zullen zij hem vergeven worden. Biecht elkanders fouten, en bidt voor elkander, opdat gij gezond moogt worden. Het krachtige verzoek des rechtvaardigen baat veel – Jakobus 5:14-16.

Ik ben altijd een groot voorstander geweest van zalving met olie. Net zoals we in het boek Jakobus geleerd worden, riep ik de ouderlingen van de gemeente en vroeg hen mij te zalven met olie. In de Bijbelse leer dat God geneest door de zalving met olie worden er een aantal dingen van degenen verwacht die genezing zoeken. Er is: het roepen van de ouderlingen der gemeente, het gebed des geloofs, voor elkander bidden, elkaars fouten belijden, het krachtige verzoek van een rechtvaardige… en de lijst gaat door. Dus een van de noodzakelijkheden om genezing te zoeken door de zalving met olie is het reinigen van het hart van enige bekende, niet-belijden zonde. Daarom doorzocht ik mijn hart en reinigde ik mijn hart van alles wat Gods genezing van mijn lichaam zou belemmeren.

Merk op de nauwe samenhang in deze passage tussen het lichamelijke en het geestelijke. Ik ontdekte in mijn genezingsweg dat het een het ander beïnvloedt. Lichamelijke genezing begint met geestelijke genezing. Een paar druppels olie hebben geen therapeutisch voordeel. Deze zalving met olie is primair een geestelijke oefening. Als we dit sacrament beoefenen zoals Jakobus het aanbiedt, reinigen we van binnenuit onze harten en vragen we vervolgens God om lichamelijke genezing.

Dit was mijn eerste stap naar genezing, maar er lag een lange weg voor ons. We raadpleegden meerdere artsen en uiteindelijk kozen we een behandelingsprotocol dat bestraling en hormoontherapie omvatte. Deze behandeling verzwakte mij lichamelijk en deed mij mijn menselijkheid voelen. Het maakte mij afhankelijker van God en anderen en minder zeker van mijn eigen vermogen. Leven in zwakte deed mij kracht putten uit mijn hemelse Vader Die de bron van kracht is. Ik vertrouwde zwaar op de bemoediging en steun die mijn vrouw en familie boden.

Er zijn lessen die alleen door menselijke zwakte geleerd kunnen worden. Om die reden kreeg Paulus een doorn in het vlees. Hij zocht driemaal de Heer om genezing. Gods antwoord kwam telkens hetzelfde terug: “Mijn genade is u voldoende, want Mijn kracht wordt in zwakheid volmaakt.” Ik kan getuigen dat dat waar is.

In januari 2021 onderging ik meerdere bestralingsbehandelingen. Ik had voor de maand februari een reeks samenkomsten gepland, in de veronderstelling dat mijn behandelingen voorbij zouden zijn en ik weer normaal zou zijn. Wat ik niet had gerealiseerd, was het vertraagde effect van bestraling. Ik ging gemakkelijk door de behandelingen heen, maar in februari ervoer ik veel spijsverteringsproblemen en veel lichamelijke zwakte.

Er werd van mij verwacht dat ik een reeks van vier preken op vier opeenvolgende avonden zou houden. We baden en hoewel ik de dag niet door kon komen zonder te slapen, gaf God bovennatuurlijke kracht voor die avondboodschappen. Ik loof God dat Zijn kracht in mijn zwakheid volmaakt werd.

Mijn artsen hebben hun vak uitgeoefend. Ik ben dankbaar voor de professionele medische zorg die ik ontving. Ik heb gedaan wat ik kon met kruiden en supplementen en God is barmhartig geweest. Mijn laatste bloedonderzoek was niet aantoonbaar. God zij geprezen!

Ik deel mijn ervaring om de correlatie tussen het lichamelijke en het geestelijke te laten zien. Lichamelijke ziekte had in mijn ervaring een heiligend effect op mijn geest en geestelijke vernieuwing konditioneerde mijn lichaam voor genezing. Ik zal altijd dankbaar zijn voor de professionele zorg van mijn artsen, maar ook zij realiseren zich de grenzen van hun professie. Bij mijn laatste bezoek aan mijn medisch oncoloog zei hij tegen mij: “Nu gaan we de Heer vertrouwen.” Dank God voor Godvrezende artsen!

Er zijn verschillende voorbeelden in de Schrift die deze samenhang tussen lichamelijke en geestelijke genezing aantonen. In Marcus 2, toen zij de verlamde naar beneden lieten door het dak in de aanwezigheid van Jezus, zei Hij tegen de verlamde: “Uw zonden zijn u vergeven.” Vervolgens zei Hij: “Sta op en wandel.” Toen Hij door de Farizeeën werd uitgedaagd omdat Hij zonden vergaf, zei Hij tegen hen: “Wat is gemakkelijker te zeggen, Sta op en wandel of Uw zonden zijn u vergeven,” waarmee Hij aantoonde dat Hij de macht had om beide te doen. Als wij geloven dat Jezus de macht heeft onze zonden te vergeven, geloven wij dan ook dat Hij de macht heeft onze lichamen te genezen? Ik wel!

In Johannes 5 genas Jezus een man die bij de vijver van Bethesda lag. Hij had deze kwaal achtendertig jaar. Jezus kwam langs en genas hem. Later, toen Hij hem in de tempel ontmoette, zei Hij tegen hem: “Zie, gij zijt gezond gemaakt; zondig niet meer, opdat u niet iets noch ergers geschiede.” Let op de samenhang tussen het lichamelijke en het geestelijke.

Lichamelijke gebreken hebben een enorme potentie om ons hart te openen voor geestelijke realiteiten, als wij het toelaten. De psalmist zei: Voor ik bengekwetst, ging ik verkeerd; maar nu heb ik Uw woord bewaard – Psalm 119:67. Jezus zei: De Geest des Heren is op mij, omdat Hij mij gezalfd heeft om het evangelie te prediken voor de armen; Hij heeft mij gezonden om de gebrokenen van hart te genezen, om vrijspraak te prediken aan de gevangenen, en het zien te herstellen aan de blinden, om vrijlating te brengen aan de gekneuvelden, om het aanvaardbare jaar des Heren te prediken – Lukas 4:18-19.

Neem nogmaals een frisse blik op onze tekst voor dit artikel en merk op dat Jezus meer dan lichamelijke genezing aanbiedt. Hij belooft genezing voor de gebrokenen van hart, bevrijding voor de gevangenen, en bevrijding voor de gekneuvelden. Deze beloften betreffen emotionele genezing — genezing voor de pijn die we ontvangen als gevolg van het leven in een gebroken, door zonde vervloekte wereld.

Ik weet zeker dat er velen dit artikel lezen die trauma hebben meegemaakt waarvan ik niets weet. Maar ik wil u verzekeren dat u genezen kunt worden. Gelooft u dat? Gelooft u dat de pijn kan verdwijnen? Gelooft u dat u bevrijd kunt worden van angst, bezorgdheid, woede en bitterheid?

We bespraken de correlatie tussen geestelijke en lichamelijke genezing. Er is ook een correlatie tussen geestelijke en emotionele genezing. Als u een gebroken hart ervaart, wil Jezus uw gebroken hart genezen. Als u een gevangene bent — als u gebonden bent aan een verleden of aan een verslaving die uw vrijheid verhindert — zal Jezus u vrijmaken. Als u gekneusd bent, zal Jezus u genezen.

Mijn vrouw en ik zijn onthutst over het grote aantal mensen in onze anabaptistische kerken dat zich tot psychofarmaca (geestmedicatie) en seculiere counseling wendt om oplossingen te vinden voor emotionele stoornissen. De Bijbel behandelt de meeste emotionele stoornissen:

Vrees

  • Er is geen vrees in de liefde; maar de volmaakte liefde drijft de vrees uit – 1 Johannes 4:18.
  • Als ik bang ben, zal ik op U vertrouwen – Psalm 56:3.
  • “Wees niet bevreesd” komt 63 keer in de Bijbel voor

Zorg/Bezorgdheid

  • Weest in geen ding bezorgd; maar in alles, door bidden en smeken met dankzegging, laat uw bede bekend worden bij God – Filipenzen 4:6.

Woede

  • Alle bitterheid, en woede, en toorn, en geschreeuw, en smadelijk spreken zij van u weggenomen met alle boosheid – Efeziërs 4:31.

Dit is slechts een greep uit emotionele stoornissen die we in het leven tegenkomen, en ik besef dat er achter deze emoties vaak diepgeworteld trauma schuilt. Uw trauma is geen verrassing voor Jezus. Hij heeft misschien uw exacte trauma niet ervaren, maar Hij is tot in de diepte van uw pijn gegaan en Hij is er als Overwinnaar uitgekomen.

Want wij hebben niet een hogepriester, die niet kan innemen medelijden met onze zwakheden; maar die in alle dingen verzocht is gelijk als wij, doch zonder zonde. Laten wij dan vrijmoedig toegaan tot de troon der genade, opdat wij barmhartigheid verkrijgen en genade vinden tot hulp in den tijd van aangelegenheid – Hebreeën 4:15-16.

Het evangelie biedt een holistische remedie voor het zondeprobleem van de mens. Onze anabaptistische erfenis heeft benadrukt dat geloof in Jezus elk gebied van ons leven beïnvloedt. Dit geloof motiveert ons Jezus op zeer praktische manieren in ons dagelijks leven te volgen. Dit resulteert in een leven van radicale niet-aanpassing aan de wereld om ons heen.

Dit radicale discipelschap zou ook onze emotionele reacties op moeilijke mensen en omstandigheden moeten beïnvloeden. Of zijn we zo emotioneel fragiel geworden dat, als het leven ons niet precies geeft wat we willen, ons emotionele evenwicht verstoord raakt? Of is het evangelie dat we prediken misschien een opeenvolging van woorden geworden die de geest sussen maar geen effect heeft op onze ziel?

Laten wij dan vreezen, opdat niet, dat een belofte overblijvende ons te geven om in Zijn rust in te gaan, iemand van u schijnbaar daaraan tekort zou doen komen. Want ook tot ons is het evangelie verkondigd gelijk ook tot hen; maar het woord verkondigd nuttigde hun niet, niet gemengd met geloof in hen die het hoorden – Hebreeën 4:1-2. Is ons geloof in God zo zwak (denk eraan dat in de Bijbelse verhalen van genezing het hun geloof was dat de genezing mogelijk maakte) dat wij meer geloof hebben in medicatie of in een gecertificeerde seculiere counselor dan in God en Zijn Woord?

Dit is een discipelschapreeks. Kom met mij op de berg waar Jezus onderwijst. Ja, er is een grote menigte, maar volg mij nauwgezet, we zullen proberen dicht genoeg te komen om te horen. Ik hoor Zijn stem — Hij zegt iets over “het zout der aarde” en “het licht der wereld.” Hier is een lege plaats — precies ruimte voor twee. Laten we op het gras zitten en luisteren:

“Gij hebt gehoord dat gezegd is: Oog om oog en tand om tand. Maar Ik zeg u: Weert u niet tegen de boze; doch zoudt een iegelijk die u een tik op de rechterwang geeft, ook de andere wenden.

En indien iemand u dagvaardt om uw kleed, laat hem ook uw mantel hebben. En zo iemand u dwingt een mijl te gaan, ga met hem twee. Geeft aan hem die u vraagt, en keert u niet af van hem die van u wil lenen.

Gij hebt gehoord dat gezegd is: Gij zult uw naaste liefhebben en uw vijand haten. Maar Ik zeg u: Bemint uw vijanden, zegenet die u vervloeken, doet goed aan die u haten, en bidt voor die u onrecht aandoen en vervolgen; opdat gij kinderen moogt zijn van uw Vader die in de hemelen is: want Hij doet Zijn zon opgaan over bozen en goeden, en doet regenen over rechtvaardigen en onrechtvaardigen.”

Dit zijn radicale leerstellingen. Radicaal doordat ze zo tegenovergesteld zijn aan onze natuurlijke neigingen, en toch is dit de weg van de vrede. De meeste van onze negatieve emoties zoals woede, vrees en bezorgdheid kunnen opgelost worden door deze leerstellingen van Jezus op onze situaties toe te passen. Dit kan wellicht te simplistisch klinken, maar dat is de aard van het evangelie en miljoenen mensen hebben leven en vrijheid gevonden door geloof in Christus.

Loof de HEERE, o mijn ziel; en al wat binnen in mij is, loof Zijn heilige naam. Loof de HEERE, o mijn ziel, en vergeet niet al Zijn weldaden: Die al uw ongerechtigheden vergeeft; die al uw ziekten geneest; Die uw leven verlost van het verderf; Die u kroont met goedertierenheid en barmhartigheden; Die uw mond verzadigt met het goede, zodat uw jeugd vernieuwd wordt als van den arend – Psalm 103:1-5.

Lunchtime was over and it was that delightful hour of the day when mom said it was time for a break. Since Ellie was ten, she wasn’t required to take a daily nap anymore, so she set about trying to decide just how she would spend this free time. She loved being outdoors, so the sunny skies and fresh air of this particularly lovely summer day fairly pulled her outside.

“I know!” she thought to herself. “This would be a perfect time to try some whittling with that knife Paul gave me.”

She had spent a week with her aunt and uncle who lived several counties over from hers and while there, her cousin Paul had given her a knife that he had made. It had a short, round handle and he had inserted a small piece of steel into one end. He then honed the blade to a nice sharp edge. He could carve the funniest little faces on small blocks of wood and Ellie was always eager to see what he would create next. She tried to copy him, but it didn’t seem as if she would be turning out anything very exciting any time soon. Still, it was fun to try, so she got the knife from her drawer in her bedroom and headed outside.

The large maple tree in front of their old stone farmhouse beckoned to her. Its low hanging branches seemed like the perfect place to perch and try out that knife again. Ellie selected a few large twigs and then hoisted herself up into the cool shade of the tree. Once situated, she began cutting and picking away at her pieces of wood. She still couldn’t make eyes and a nose appear, but she had fun carving notches and shaving off small pieces of bark. It was a relaxing thing with which to be occupied while enjoying the quietness of the afternoon. She was so glad this tree was in their yard, and she was so glad that Paul had given her that whittling knife.

After a time, the branch Ellie was sitting on began to feel rough and hard, and the twigs she was whittling had nearly disappeared. “I should go see what the boys are doing,” she thought. She shifted to the lowest branch and sat poised, ready to jump down like she always did to get out of the tree.

She paused, looking at the knife in her hand. “Never jump down from anywhere while holding a knife in your hand!” her mother’s voice rang in her memory. “It is a very dangerous thing to do. You could get cut very badly.” Ellie sat thinking about that for a little.

“Yes, I know that’s probably true,” she told herself. “But I think if I am very careful, I could jump down and it will be fine,” she reasoned.

She firmly grasped the knife in her right hand, then quickly jumped the distance to the ground. Just as she landed, her ankle turned and gave way under her. She fell awkwardly onto her left leg. And, oh no! That little knife had plunged into her left wrist as she was trying to keep her balance. She quickly pulled it out and watched, with her heart beating rapidly, as the blood welled up, dark and warm. It was a small cut, only about one quarter of an inch long, but it had gone in rather deeply.

What should she do now? Yes, there was no doubt about it, her mom had been right after all! In her heart, she knew the right thing to do would be to go directly to her mother and tell her what she had done. But she felt guilty and ashamed. She had known better than to jump down with that knife, yet she had gone ahead and done it anyway. Guiltily, she quickly pressed her thumb on top of the wound and slipped into the house. The bleeding soon stopped, and after finding a little bandage and placing it on her cut, she quietly put her knife away and found a book to read. She never told her mom what she had done until many years later when she was a grown woman.

Today, as she looks at that scar, which is still visible from 40 years ago, she wonders why God had protected her. She had been a foolish little girl to not go immediately to her mother and confess what she had done. She could have gotten a severe infection from getting cut with a dirty, slightly rusty knife. Even though she acted foolishly, she is grateful that God protected her, but she still wishes she had confessed her disobedience to her mother.

It is never wise to hide anything from your parents. They need to know those wrong things you do, no matter how embarrassed or ashamed you might feel. Parents need to know all the things that happen to their children It is God’s design for fathers and mothers to be there for their children, to help you when you get hurt, and to guide and teach you as you learn how to be good, obedient children. God’s way is always the best.

दोपहर का खाना समाप्त हो चुका था और वह सुखद समय आ गया था जब माँ कहती थीं कि अब आराम करने का समय है। चूँकि एली दस साल की थी, उसे रोज़ाना झपकी लेने की ज़रूरत नहीं रहती थी, इसलिए उसने तय करने की कोशिश की कि वह इस खाली समय को कैसे बिताएगी। उसे बाहर रहना बहुत पसंद था, इसलिए इस ख़ास सुंदर गर्मियों के दिन की धूप और ताज़ा हवा उसे बाहर खींच लाई।

“मुझे पता है!” उसने खुद से सोचा। “यह पॉल ने दिया हुआ वो चाकू आज आज़माने का एकदम सही समय होगा।”

वह अपने चाचा-चाची के यहाँ एक हफ्ता रही थी जो उसके काउंटी से कई काउंटियों दूर रहते थे और वहीं उसके चचेरे भाई पॉल ने उसे एक चाकू दिया था जो उसने खुद बनाया था। उस चाकू का हैंडल छोटा और गोल था और उसने एक सिरे में स्टील का एक छोटा टुकड़ा डाला था। फिर उसने ब्लेड को तेज़ धार दे दी थी। वह लकड़ी के छोटे-छोटे टुकड़ों पर बहुत विचित्र चेहरे काट लेता था और एली हमेशा उत्सुक रहती थी कि वह अगला क्या बनाएगा। उसने उसकी नक़ल करने की कोशिश की, पर ऐसा लगता था कि वह जल्द ही कुछ बहुत रोमांचक नहीं बनाएगी। फिर भी, कोशिश करना मज़ेदार था, तो वह अपने कमरे के दराज से चाकू लेकर बाहर चली गई।

उनके पुराने पत्थर के फार्महाउस के सामने बड़ा मेपल का पेड़ उसे बुला रहा था। इसकी नीचे झुकती शाखाएँ जैसे चढ़कर उस चाकू की कोशिश करने के लिए एकदम सही जगह थीं। एली ने कुछ मोटे टहनी चुनीं और फिर खुद को पेड़ की ठंडी छाया में चढ़ा लिया। एक बार बैठ जाने के बाद उसने लकड़ी के टुकड़ों को काटना और छीलना शुरू किया। वह अभी भी आँखें और नाक जैसा कुछ नहीं बना पाई थी, लेकिन उसे चीरे काटना और छाल के छोटे-छोटे टुकड़े शेव करना मज़ेदार लग रहा था। यह दोपहर की शांति का आनंद लेते हुए लगे रहने के लिए एक शांत काम था। उसे बहुत अच्छा लग रहा था कि यह पेड़ उनके आंगन में है, और वह बहुत खुश थी कि पॉल ने उसे वह चाकू दिया था।

कुछ समय बाद, जिस शाखा पर एली बैठी थी वह खुरदरी और कठोर महसूस होने लगी और जिन टहनियों को वह काट रही थी वे लगभग नष्ट हो चुकी थीं। “मुझे जाकर देखना चाहिए कि लड़के क्या कर रहे हैं,” उसने सोचा। वह सबसे नीचे वाली टहनी पर सरकी और झट से नीचे कूदने के लिए तैयार बैठी, जैसे वह हमेशा करती थी, पेड़ से उतरने के लिए।

वह रुकी और अपने हाथ में चाकू को देखा। “कहीं से भी चाकू हाथ में लेकर कूदना कभी नहीं!” उसकी माँ की आवाज़ उसकी याद में गूंज उठी। “यह बहुत ख़तरनाक होता है। तुम बहुत बुरी तरह कट सकती हो।” एली ने थोड़ी देर के लिए उस पर विचार किया।

“हाँ, मुझे पता है कि शायद यह सच है,” उसने खुद से कहा। “पर मुझे लगता है कि अगर मैं बहुत सावधान रहूँ तो मैं कूद सकती हूँ और ठीक रहूँगी,” उसने तर्क किया।

उसने अपने दाहिने हाथ में चाकू को मजबूती से पकड़ा और फिर जल्दी से जमीन तक कूद पड़ी। जैसे ही वह उतरती, उसका टखना मोड़ा और वह असंतुलित होकर गिर पड़ी। वह अनमना ढंग से अपनी बायीँ टांग पर गिरी। और, ओह नहीं! उस छोटे चाकू से वह उसकी बायीँ कलाई में घुस गया जब वह संतुलन बनाए रखने की कोशिश कर रही थी। उसने उसे जल्दी से निकाल लिया और अपने हृदय की तेज़ धड़कन के साथ देखा कि खून बाहर आ रहा है, गहरा और गर्म। यह एक छोटी सी कट थी, केवल लगभग एक चौथाई इंच लंबी, पर यह काफी गहराई तक चली गई थी।

अब उसे क्या करना चाहिए था? हाँ, इसमें कोई संदेह नहीं था, उसकी माँ आखिरकार सही थीं! उसके भीतर, वह जानती थी कि सही काम यही होगा कि वह सीधे अपनी माँ के पास जाए और जो हुआ बता दे। पर वह दोषी और शर्मिंदा महसूस कर रही थी। उसे पता था कि चाकू हाथ में लेकर कूदना गलत था, फिर भी उसने ऐसा कर दिया था। दोषी होकर उसने जल्दी से अपने अंगूठे को घाव के ऊपर दबा दिया और घर में चली गई। खून जल्द ही रुक गया, और एक छोटा पट्टी मिली तो उसने उसे काट पर लगाकर चुपचाप अपना चाकू वापस रखा और एक किताब ढूँढकर पढ़ने लगी। उसने कई साल बाद जब वह बड़ी महिला बनी तब तक अपनी माँ को कभी नहीं बताया कि उसने ऐसा किया था।

आज, जब वह उस निशान को देखती है, जो अभी भी 40 साल पहले का दिखता है, वह आश्चर्य करती है कि परमेश्वर ने उसकी रक्षा क्यों की। वह अपनी माँ के पास तुरंत जाकर जो कुछ उसने किया था कबूल न करने पर खुद को मूर्ख समझती थी। वह गंदे, हल्के जंग लगे चाकू से कटने पर गंभीर संक्रमण भी पा सकती थी। यद्यपि उसने मूर्खतापूर्ण व्यवहार किया, वह आभारी है कि परमेश्वर ने उसकी रक्षा की, पर वह अभी भी चाहती है कि उसने अपनी अवज्ञा अपनी माँ के सामने स्वीकार कर दी होती।

अपने माता-पिता से कुछ भी छिपाना कभी बुद्धिमानी नहीं है। उन्हें उन गलत चीज़ों के बारे में जानने की ज़रूरत है जो तुम करते हो, चाहे तुम कितने ही शर्मिंदा या लज्जित क्यों न महसूस करो। माता-पिता को अपने बच्चों के साथ जो कुछ भी होता है वह जानना आवश्यक है। पिता और माता का यह डिजाइन है कि वे अपने बच्चों के लिए वहाँ रहें, जब आप चोट खाते हैं तो आपकी मदद करें, और आपको मार्गदर्शन और शिक्षा दें जैसे आप अच्छे, आज्ञाकारी बच्चे बनना सीखते हैं। परमेश्वर का तरीका हमेशा सबसे अच्छा है।
