Denn Christus hat mich nicht gesandt, zu taufen, sondern zu predigen das Evangelium; nicht mit Klugheit der Rede, damit nicht das Kreuz Christi gemacht werde zu nichts. Denn die Predigt vom Kreuz ist denen, die verloren gehen, Torheit; uns aber, die wir selig werden, ist sie Gottes Kraft. …es gefiel Gott, durch die Torheit der Predigt selig zu machen, die glauben –1 Korinther –1:17-21.

Die moderne christliche Welt hat viele der demütigen Mittel, die Gott benutzt hat, um das Reich einzuführen, gebührend übernommen. Die jungfräuliche Geburt, die grob geschnitzte Krippe und die Windeln sind zu herrschenden Denkmalen geworden, auf die wir kaum verzichten könnten. Sogar der schlichte Esel wird am Karfreitag gewürdigt und das alte, robuste Kreuz ist zu einem geistlichen Emblem geworden, das nominell an Halsketten und in kunstvollen Kanzelschnitzereien gezeigt wird. Während der Mensch weiterhin von den traditionellen Symbolen des Evangeliums fasziniert bleibt, gibt es doch einen absurden Weg, den Gott wählte und der zunehmend verachtet wird.

Jahrhunderte lang wurde das Evangelium von törichten und ungelehrten Männern verkündigt (so sagten zumindest ihre elitären und intellektuellen Gegenüber). Die biblische Wahrheit, in Schlichtheit gesprochen, war an sich ausreichend, damit Gottes Heiliger Geist sie gebrauchen konnte, um den Sünder zu bekehren. Zwar mangelt es heute nicht an Predigt, doch scheint vieles davon eine andere Art zu sein als die ursprüngliche Form, die Christus vorlebte. Wenn jemand fähig gewesen wäre, eine kunstvolle Rede in einer präzisen philosophischen Sprache zu formulieren, dann wäre es der Apostel Paulus gewesen. Doch weigerte er sich, das Evangelium auf diese Weise zu predigen, …damit nicht das Kreuz Christi gemacht werde zu nichts –1 Korinther 1:17. Er predigte mit Bedacht, damit der Erfolg nicht der Kraft der Kunst, sondern der Wahrheit selbst zugeschrieben würde.

Paulus war an den Füßen Gamaliels in jüdischer Gelehrsamkeit geprägt worden und verstand sowohl Hebräisch als auch Griechisch, doch beim Predigen vom Kreuz Christi legte er sein Wissen beiseite. Er sprach die Worte des Evangeliums in einer Sprache frei von menschlicher Macht, damit die Ehre, die Christus gebührt, nicht von seiner eigenen persönlichen Kraft überstrahlt werde. Denn seine Briefe, sagen sie, sind schwer und kräftig; aber seine Gegenwart ist schwach, und seine Rede verächtlich –2 Korinther 10:10. Hier hat die moderne Kirche die einfachen Mittel, die Christus und die Apostel wählten, verworfen und ist auf einen Weg ausgewichen, der in unserer Zeit als annehmbarer gilt. Die Effizienz der Moderne verlangt einen direkteren Weg zum Ziel, und wenn die Bibel es nicht verbietet, halten wir es für unser Vorrecht, ihn zu benutzen.

Zwar könnten evangelikale Filme, Musikkonzerte und eine Reihe anderer fragwürdiger Formen des Dienstes genannt werden, doch möchte ich mich vor allem dem modernen Einladungssystem widmen, das als „Altaraufruf“ bekannt ist. Obwohl es gemeinhin mit den „altmodischen Versammlungen“ der letzten zwei Jahrhunderte assoziiert wird, ist es tatsächlich modern, weil fast neunzehn Jahrhunderte lang niemand von dieser Praxis gehört hatte. Evangelisten wie George Whitefield, Jonathan Edwards und sogar John Wesley kannten eine solche Gewohnheit nicht. Selbst Charles Spurgeon (gerühmt als der „Fürst der Prediger“) kritisierte sie heftig und weigerte sich, sie zu übernehmen.*

So sehen wir, dass die Praxis nicht in der apostolischen Kirche geboren wurde. Sie ist nicht im Dienst Jesu, seiner Apostel oder sogar der Kirche der nachapostolischen Zeit zu finden. Wir sehen zwar, dass Jesus und die Apostel Männer und Frauen einluden, zu Christus zu kommen und gerettet zu werden, doch niemals durch dieses besondere Verfahren. Warum aber ist diese Praxis heute in den meisten evangelikalen und in vielen anabaptistischen Kirchen zu einem so wesentlichen Werkzeug geworden? Die Antwort lautet – pragmatische Ergebnisse. Unmittelbar nach der Predigt singt die Gemeinde ein Lied, während der Prediger die Menschen aufruft, nach vorn in die Aula (zum „Altar“) zu gehen, um eine öffentliche Entscheidung für Christus zu treffen. Das Heil wird allen angeboten, die nach vorn kommen und es empfangen. Diejenigen, die kommen, erhalten oft die persönliche Betreuung eines Beraters, der mit ihnen betet und sie durch das Bekenntnis führt.

Diese Praxis wurde entwickelt, um Entscheidungen zu fördern und Ergebnisse zu erzielen. Und das tat sie. Mit leichten Variationen verbreitete sich die neue Methode zunehmend durch Charles Finney, später Dwight L. Moody und schließlich praktisch durch das ganze evangelikal geprägte 19. und 20. Jahrhundert. Peter Cartwright, Sam Jones, R. A. Torrey, Billy Sunday, Bob Jones, Gipsy Smith, John R. Rice, Billy Graham und George Brunk verwendeten alle diese Methode mit beeindruckendem Erfolg. So wurde das Einladungssystem zur akzeptierten Normalpraxis, und diejenigen, die es hinterfragen, gelten oft als geistlich exzentrisch.

Warum sollten wir die Praxis beanstanden, wenn die Schrift sie nicht verbietet? Die Antwort liegt in der Frage nach der Angemessenheit des Altaraufrufs. Zunächst sei angemerkt, dass die Schriften reich an Einladungen zur Rettung sind. Solche Angebote wie Kommt zu mir, … so will ich euch Ruhe geben –Matthäus 11:28, und …Wenn jemand dürstet, der komme zu mir und trinke –Johannes 7:37, sind wunderbare Lebensangebote für die, die Christus vertrauen. Die Apostel zögerten auch nicht, Christus als Retter allen zu zeigen, die ihre Botschaft hören wollten.

Sie predigten ohne Unterschied: So tut Buße und bekehret euch, dass eure Sünden ausgetilget würden… –Apostelgeschichte 3:19, und …wir ermahnen euch an Christi Statt, dass ihr euch versöhnet mit Gott –2 Korinther 5:20. Und sie zeugten …den Juden und auch den Griechen, Buße gegen Gott und den Glauben an unsern Herrn Jesus Christus –Apostelgeschichte 20:21. Bei alldem sollte jeder Christ nicht nur zustimmen, sondern sich auch freuen.

Schließlich …zwingt sie zu kommen, dass mein Haus voll werde –Lukas 14:23, ist ein weiterer Bibelvers, der zur Unterstützung der Altaraufruf-Methode herangezogen werden könnte. Dennoch sagt auch dieser nichts zur Richtigkeit des Altaraufrufs. Wenn wir die Praxis an ihren Wurzeln untersuchen, können wir nicht umhin, einige Mängel zu beobachten:

…außerbiblisch

Dies soll kein Vorwurf gegen die Vielen sein, die bei einer solchen Veranstaltung Rettung gefunden haben. Die Engel im Himmel freuen sich über die Buße jedes Sünders, egal wie er dorthin gelangt ist. Wir möchten lediglich die Schlichtheit der Torheit der Predigt hervorheben, durch die Glaubende selig werden. Der Altaraufruf wird als eine spezielle Ergänzung zur Predigt verwendet, um zu dem zu gelangen, was die Torheit der Predigt allein nicht zustande brachte.

Der Altaraufruf gewann in den 1830er Jahren mit der Predigt von Charles G. Finney an Popularität, der schrieb: „Eine Erweckung ist kein Wunder, noch in irgendeinem Sinne von einem Wunder abhängig. Sie ist ein rein philosophisches Ergebnis des richtigen Gebrauchs der eingerichteten Mittel." ** Wir können nicht allen, die den Altaraufruf praktizieren, vorwerfen, dies zu glauben, doch ist es doch aufschlussreich, dass der Prediger, der ihn populär machte, ihn eher einer mathematischen Gleichung als einem göttlichen Eingreifen gleichstellte.

Wenn die Wahrheit auf den Boden eines guten und ehrlichen Herzens fällt, nimmt der Same wahrhaft Wurzel und bringt Frucht. Dieser Wahrheits-Samen braucht keine künstliche Kleidung. Er leuchtet in seiner größten Majestät in seinem eigenen Licht und beherrscht die Welt durch seine göttliche Autorität. Es ist eine Demonstration des Geistes, ohne menschliche Erfindung oder Intervention. Die einfache Predigt eines gekreuzigten Christus ist mächtiger als alle Rhetorik, Philosophien und emotional aufwühlenden Methoden der Welt.

…emotionaler Antrieb

Der Altaraufruf verlangt von einem Suchenden, seinen Platz zu verlassen und nach vorn zu gehen, um Vergebung zu empfangen. Solche Einladungen werden oft von erschütternden Berichten, traurigen Geschichten oder Zeugnissen begleitet, die die Gefühle zu Furcht, Schuld oder Reue erregen. Umrahmt von einem sanften Gemeindelied sind die Emotionen reif, vorwärts zu gehen. Diejenigen, die ohne körperliche Antwort von ihrem Platz aus bereuen, werden oft als jemanden angesehen, der eine „Gelegenheit verpasst“ hat.

Und diese sind gleich denen, die auf steinigen Boden gesät sind; welche, nachdem sie das Wort gehört haben, es eilends mit Freuden annehmen; und haben keine Wurzel in sich, und währen doch nur eine Zeit; darnach, wenn Bedrängnis oder Verfolgung um des Wortes willen kommt, werden sie sogleich veranlasst –Markus 4:16-17. Wir weigern uns, daraus zu schließen, dass alle, die durch diese Art von Dienst bekehrt wurden, Zuhörer auf steinigem Boden seien. Doch die große Mehrheit derer, die es in einer derart aufgeladenen emotionalen Umgebung annehmen, wird oft eine weniger aufrichtige Bekehrung haben.

Einmal hatte ich einen überschwänglichen Kunden in meiner Werkstatt, der mir berichtete, dass ihre Kirche einen nationalen evangelistischen Dienst gesponsert habe, der an der öffentlichen Highschool predigte. „Es gab über 400 Entscheidungen für Christus!“ Während wir uns alle mit den Engeln freuen wollen, kann man nicht umhin zu fragen, wie viele von ihnen ein Jahr später noch in der Kirche waren. Auch wenn das Fehlen echten Engagements nicht allein dem Gebrauch des Altaraufrufs zuzuschreiben ist, dürfen wir sicher sein, dass der Same, der so schnell aufspringt, sich an den Pfählen einer emotionalen Einladung zeigen wird. Diejenigen, die keine Wurzel haben, wären besser dran, nie voreilig geantwortet zu haben.

Bekehrungen, die durch emotionale Kanäle herbeigeführt werden, sind oft fragwürdig und vergänglich. Die Regungen des Heiligen Geistes benötigen keine menschliche Stärke, Weisheit oder Anstrengungen, um sie zu vermitteln. Erweckungsmethoden wie Schreien, offenes Weinen, emotional aufrührende Musik und das Erzählen sentimentaler Geschichten sind die menschengemachte Kunst des Predigens. Sie finden sich auch in vielen anderen öffentlichen Foren, die darauf ausgelegt sind, eine bestimmte vorherbestimmte Reaktion des Hörers hervorzurufen. Jede dieser Dimensionen ist dem menschlichen Verhalten ganz natürlich, und manchmal gibt es eine schmale Grenze zwischen dem, was in der Predigt akzeptabel und nicht akzeptabel ist. Große Sorgfalt ist geboten, damit wir nicht einen emotionalen Höhepunkt schaffen und die Botschaft in ungebührlicher Weise in den Schatten stellen, damit die Kraft nicht der Menschen, sondern Christi ist.

…Eingriff in elterliche und örtliche Gemeindebefugnis

Kinder sind bei solchen Gelegenheiten oft ein Ziel. Sie mögen sich wegen irgendeines kindlichen Fehlverhaltens schuldig fühlen, doch eine feurige Botschaft, gefolgt von emotionalem Flehen, kann sehr beunruhigend sein. Dies sind Zeiten, in denen ein Elternteil zum Herzen seines Kindes sprechen und sich auf geistliche Weise verbinden sollte. Stattdessen wird das Kind oft nach vorn bewegt und einem Gemeindebetreuer übergeben, damit es dort sein Bekenntnis ausschütten kann.

Ich kenne eine Frau, deren Vater ein wandernder evangelikaler Prediger war. Sie behauptet, sie habe „hundertfach“ auf den Altaraufruf reagiert. Eine lockere und ehrliche Einschätzung würde zeigen, dass der Altaraufruf zwar vielen aufrichtigen Bekehrungen den Anfang geben mag, sich aber ebenso einer Vielzahl voreiliger Entscheidungen und druckbedingter Verpflichtungen bedient. Das lässt oft viele instabile Seelen in geistlicher Unsicherheit dahintreiben und jahrelang mit einem Mangel an Gewissheit über die Erlösung kämpfen.

Denn obgleich ihr zehntausend Lehrmeister in Christo habet, so habt ihr doch nicht viele Väter: denn in Christo Jesu habe ich euch durch das Evangelium gezeugt. Darum flehe ich euch an, seid meine Nachahmer –1 Korinther 4:15-16. Gott hat Väter und Mütter bestimmt, ihre Kinder sowohl leiblich als auch geistlich zur Welt zu bringen.

Seid meine Nachahmer, gleichwie ich Christi bin –1 Korinther 11:1. Der gewandte wandernde Evangelist hat nicht die Absicht, geistliche Kinder zu zeugen und Anhänger von sich selbst zu machen. Das überlässt er anderen, denn er hat seine Gabe darin gefunden, Menschen zu Entscheidungen zu drängen.

Und wir ermahnen euch, Brüder, wisst, welche unter euch arbeiten und euch vorstehen im Herrn und euch zurechtweisen; und schätzt sie sehr in der Liebe um ihrer Arbeit willen… –1 Thessalonicher 5:13. Es soll jedoch eine von Gott gegebene Treue zu jenen geistlichen Vätern geben, die über uns arbeiten und uns über das viele Lehren auf dem Lebensweg hinaus zur Geburt bringen. Das zeitgenössische Auftreten von Tausenden von „Hau-Ruck“-Diensten sollte uns Sorge bereiten.

Während das öffentliche Bekenntnis der Sünde offensichtlich eine wichtige Lehre Christi zur Begleitung der Rettung ist, gehören diese Bekenntnisse in die Hände der geistlichen Autoritäten, die die Situation einschätzen und die Seele weiter durch die Versuchungen von morgen hindurchführen können. Wenn diejenigen, die den Bekehrten kennen, persönlich eingebunden sind, kann eine gründlichere und ehrlichere Untersuchung vorgenommen werden, um eine aufrichtige Bekehrung herbeizuführen. Das legt das Fundament für das tiefe Graben, das erforderlich ist, um den Grund auf den Felsen zu legen und die Seele sowohl im Haus als auch in der Gemeinde zu festigen.

…künstlich herbeigeführter Glaube

Wenn Menschen ständig Erweckungsszenen ausgesetzt sind, besteht oft unausprochene Erwartung, dass die Versammlungen der Ort sind, um Geschäfte mit Gott zu machen. Das neigt dazu, „rettenden Glauben“ mit einer „rettenden Handlung“ zu verwechseln. Die Betonung auf „nach vorn kommen, um Christus zu empfangen“ verwässert die Bedeutung des Glaubens. Christus ist der starke Trost, zu dem wir …als zu einer Zuflucht geflohen sind, um festzuhalten an der vorgestellten Hoffnung: welche wir haben als einen Anker der Seele, fest und sicher… –Hebräer 6:18-19. (Hervorhebung von mir)

Die Einladung Christi zu …Kommt zu mir… Matthäus 11:28, darf niemals mit dem „zum Altar kommen“ (nach vorn gehen) verwechselt werden. Die Torheit der Predigt ist die Einladung, und „Christus“ ist das Ziel. Die Kraft der Rede soll nicht in der Dynamik des Predigers liegen, sondern in der Wahrheit der Botschaft. Wir werden wie Papierfiguren, die gar keine Kraft in sich haben. Alle Kraft muss von oben kommen; alle benutzten Methoden müssen auch von oben kommen. –Watchman Nee ***

Der Wind weht, wo er will… Johannes 3:8, ebenso der Heilige Geist, und der Prediger muss damit zufrieden sein. Ich vertraue darauf, dass viele, die Altaraufrufe geben, die besten Absichten haben und nicht den Geist umgehen wollen. Aber die meisten Werke, die auf dem Gipfel der Emotion vollbracht werden, neigen stark dazu, trügerisch zu sein. So kommt der Glaube aus dem Hören, das Hören aber durch das Wort Gottes –Römer 10:17.

Endnoten:

* „Charles Spurgeon, bekannt für seine evangelistischen Fähigkeiten, weigerte sich entschieden, die Praxis der Altaraufrufe zu übernehmen, und kritisierte sie scharf. Er betrachtete den Altaraufruf als eine Methode, Entscheidungen als Ergebnisse zu erzwingen, erkannte jedoch sein Missbrauchs- und Gefährdungspotenzial.“ Altar Calls – Bill Brenner

‚Ich möchte gerne in das Anfragenzimmer gehen.‘ Ich wage zu sagen, das würdet ihr gern, aber wir sind nicht bereit, der Volksaberglaube zu frönen. Wir fürchten, dass in diesen Räumen Menschen zu einer falschen Zuversicht erwärmt werden. Sehr wenige der vermeintlichen Bekehrten aus den Anfragenräumen erweisen sich als dauerhaft gut. Geht sogleich zu eurem Gott, sogar wo ihr jetzt seid. Werft euch auf Christus, sofort, ehe ihr einen Zoll rührt!’ - Pleading and Encouragement – Charles Haddon Spurgeon – 17. Aug. 1841

** What A Revival Of Religion Is – Charles Grandison Finney – The Belknap Press Of Harvard University Ein „Wiederaufleben der Religion“ setzt einen Niedergang voraus. Fast alle Religion in der Welt ist durch Erweckungen hervorgebracht worden. Gott hat es für notwendig befunden, die Erregbarkeit der Menschheit auszunutzen, um mächtige Erregungen unter ihnen zu erzeugen, bevor er sie zum Gehorsam führen kann. Die Menschen sind so träge, es gibt so viele Dinge, die ihren Geist von der Religion ablenken und dem Einfluss des Evangeliums entgegenstehen, dass es notwendig ist, eine Erregung unter ihnen zu wecken, bis die Flut so hoch ansteigt, dass sie die entgegenstehenden Hindernisse hinwegspült. Sie müssen so erregt werden, dass sie über diese entgegenwirkenden Einflüsse hinwegbrechen, bevor sie Gott gehorchen.

*** Spirit Force vs. Psychic Force – Watchman Nee

This hymn is generally thought to be one of the most loved hymns written during the latter part of the 19th century. The writing of this thoughtful and beautifully constructed text is even more amazing when we consider that its author was one who was almost completely blind and who describes the writing of this hymn as the “fruit of much mental suffering,” and “the quickest bit of work I ever did in my life.”

Born in Glasgow, Scotland, March 27, 1842, George Matheson had only partial vision as a boy, and, after entering Glasgow University, his eyesight continued to fail rapidly. Except for “moments of shadowy eyesight”, he was totally blind by the age of 18. This affliction of blindness seemed to be a tragedy since he was an eager and avid scholar, yet it caused him to trust in the Lord, and it strengthened his walk with God.

He entered the university at the early age of 15 and graduated with high honors in 1861 at the age of 19. He was a brilliant scholar, even spending four more years after graduation in more theological studies, all the while remaining single. After his graduation he became entirely dependent on others, relying much upon his two sisters, who were so dedicated that they learned Latin, Greek, and Hebrew since they thought it might aid him in his theological studies. One of them continued to be his faithful co-worker and helper throughout his life, assisting in his calling of being a pastor and other ministerial duties.

After completing his theological course, he became assistant pastor to the renowned Dr. Macduff, in whose church of thousands of members he had been brought up. Soon, however, he was chosen minister of the Church of Scotland in the seaport summer resort of Innellan. Here he stayed for eighteen years. Many families came to spend the summer there chiefly to be inspired by his preaching ministry.

Whenever he preached, the open Bible was before him as he stood in the pulpit, and to the congregation, he seemed to be reading from it. During the messages, his eyes looked straight at the congregation, and many went away with no clue that they just listened to a blind preacher. It was during this time that he made a practice of memorizing his sermons, as well as the passages of Scripture he used in his messages. His memory was so sharp that if someone read one of his prepared sermons to him twice, or whatever else he wanted to memorize, he could from then on repeat it perfectly. One Sunday, however, after doing this for 12 years, when in the middle of a powerful sermon his memory completely collapsed, and the topic on which he was preaching vanished from his mind. He sat down and commenced to request a psalm to be sung, and, after the song, with perfect calmness told the audience what had happened. With this done, he stood to his feet, gave out a new text, and preached an impromptu sermon of great power. After that experience George wrote little of his sermons, and finally prepared only an outline from which to preach.

Dr. Matheson’s final pastorate was taken up in 1886 at the age of 44 where he became pastor of the large St. Bernard’s Parish Church in Edinburgh, where his eloquent preaching consistently attracted large throngs of people to the services. Here he remained for 13 years, his church growing from 1,494 members to 1,703 in the first 5 years. He continued faithfully preaching the gospel and became well known as one of Scotland’s outstanding preachers and pastors and was greatly esteemed in Edinburgh where he resided.

Many speculations have been made regarding the cause of the mental distress which prompted the author to write this text. A very popular account, although never verified, is that this text was a result of the severe trial Matheson faced after his soon-to-be bride left him just before their marriage when she learned of his impending total blindness. Although this story cannot be documented, there are many significant hints in this hymn reflecting a saddened heart, such as the “flickering torch” and the “borrowed ray” in the second verse, the tracing of the “rainbow through the rain” in the third stanza, as well as the “cross” in the last verse.

Fortunately, Dr. Matheson did relate an account of his writing of this hymn:

“My hymn was composed in the manse of Innellan on the evening of June 6, 1882. I was at that time alone. It was the day of my sister’s wedding, and the rest of the family were staying overnight in Glasgow. Something happened to me, which was known only to myself, and which caused me the most severe mental suffering. The hymn was the fruit of that suffering and was the quickest bit of work I ever did in my life. A genuine inspiration, I had the impression rather of having it dictated to me by some inward voice than of working it out myself. I am quite sure that the whole work was completed in five minutes and equally sure it never received at my hands any retouching or correction. I have no natural gift of rhythm. All the other verses I have ever written are manufactured articles; this came like a dayspring from on high. I have never been able to gain once more the same fervor in verse.”

The hymn first appeared in the Church of Scotland monthly magazine, Life and Work, in January 1883. The tune was composed one year later by a prominent Scotch organist of his day, Albert L. Peace, who was asked to write a tune especially for Matheson’s text.

Peace’s own account of the writing of this fine tune is as follows, “After reading it over carefully, I wrote the music straight off, and may say that the ink of the first note was hardly dry when I had finished the tune.” The origin or the tune name, St. Margaret, is unknown except that it is a name much revered in Scotland, and certainly because of the beloved Queen Margaret of Scotland.

The later years of Matheson’s life from the age of 57 to his death at age 64 were spent in writing some of the finest devotional writings in the English tongue, including Moments on the Mount, Voice of the Spirit, and Rests by the River. Although this is his only hymn found in most hymnals, he did write a few other fine hymns, including “Make Me A Captive Lord”, and “Then I Shall Be Free.”

The four key words of “O Love, That Wilt Not Let Me Go” are: love, light, joy, and cross. These words have been described as the complete satisfaction for any believer whose life is totally surrendered to the will of God. It could take the rest of one’s life to completely discover the personal significance of these four expressions.

Ce cantique est généralement considéré comme l’un des plus aimés composés durant la seconde partie du 19th siècle. L’écriture de ce texte réfléchi et magnifiquement construit est d’autant plus remarquable si l’on considère que son auteur était presque complètement aveugle et qu’il décrit la composition de ce cantique comme le « fruit de grandes souffrances mentales » et « le travail le plus rapide que j’aie jamais fait de ma vie ».

Né à Glasgow, en Écosse, le 27 mars 1842, George Matheson n’avait qu’une vision partielle dans son enfance, et, après être entré à l’université de Glasgow, sa vue continua de décliner rapidement. À l’exception de « moments de vue ombragée », il était totalement aveugle à l’âge de 18 ans. Cette affliction de cécité semblait être une tragédie étant donné qu’il était un étudiant zélé et avide, mais elle le poussa à se confier en le Seigneur et renforça sa marche avec Dieu.

Il entra à l’université à l’âge précoce de 15 ans et en sortit diplômé avec les plus grands honneurs en 1861 à l’âge de 19 ans. Il fut un brillant érudit, passant même quatre années supplémentaires après l’obtention de son diplôme à des études théologiques, tout en restant célibataire. Après sa diplomation, il devint entièrement dépendant des autres, s’appuyant beaucoup sur ses deux sœurs, qui étaient si dévouées qu’elles apprirent le latin, le grec et l’hébreu car elles pensaient que cela pourrait l’aider dans ses études théologiques. L’une d’elles continua d’être sa fidèle collaboratrice et aide tout au long de sa vie, assistant dans son ministère pastoral et autres fonctions ministérielles.

Après avoir terminé son cursus théologique, il devint pasteur assistant auprès du célèbre Dr. Macduff, dans l’église duquel il avait grandi et qui comptait des milliers de membres. Bientôt cependant, il fut choisi comme ministre de l’Église d’Écosse dans la station balnéaire portuaire d’Innellan. Il y resta dix-huit ans. De nombreuses familles venaient y passer l’été principalement pour être inspirées par son ministère de prédication.

Chaque fois qu’il prêchait, la Bible ouverte était devant lui alors qu’il se tenait en chaire, et pour la congrégation, il semblait en lire les paroles. Pendant les messages, ses yeux regardaient droit la congrégation, et beaucoup s’en allaient sans avoir la moindre idée qu’ils venaient d’écouter un prédicateur aveugle. C’est durant cette période qu’il prit l’habitude de mémoriser ses sermons, ainsi que les passages de l’Écriture qu’il utilisait dans ses messages. Sa mémoire était si vive que si quelqu’un lui lisait un de ses sermons préparés deux fois, ou tout autre texte qu’il souhaitait mémoriser, il pouvait dès lors le répéter parfaitement. Un dimanche, toutefois, après avoir agi ainsi pendant 12 ans, alors qu’il prononçait un sermon puissant, sa mémoire s’effondra complètement et le sujet qu’il traitait disparut de son esprit. Il s’assit et demanda qu’un psaume soit chanté, et, après le chant, avec un calme parfait, raconta à l’auditoire ce qui s’était passé. Cela accompli, il se leva, donna un nouveau texte et prêcha un sermon improvisé d’une grande puissance. Après cette expérience, George écrivit peu de ses sermons, et finit par ne préparer qu’un simple plan à partir duquel prêcher.

Le dernier pastorat du Dr Matheson débuta en 1886 à l’âge de 44 ans lorsqu’il devint pasteur de la grande paroisse de St. Bernard’s à Édimbourg, où sa prédication éloquente attirait sans cesse de grandes foules aux offices. Il demeura là treize ans, son église passant de 1 494 membres à 1 703 au cours des cinq premières années. Il continua à prêcher fidèlement l’évangile et devint bien connu comme l’un des prédicateurs et pasteurs éminents d’Écosse, et il était grandement estimé à Édimbourg où il résidait.

Beaucoup de spéculations ont été émises concernant la cause du tourment mental qui poussa l’auteur à écrire ce texte. Un récit très populaire, bien que jamais vérifié, affirme que ce texte résulta de l’épreuve sévère que Matheson affronta après que sa future épouse l’eut quitté peu avant leur mariage lorsqu’elle apprit qu’il deviendrait totalement aveugle. Bien que cette histoire ne puisse être documentée, il existe dans ce cantique de nombreux indices significatifs reflétant un cœur attristé, tels que la « torche vacillante » et le « rayon emprunté » dans le deuxième couplet, le fait de « tracer l’arc-en-ciel à travers la pluie » dans la troisième strophe, ainsi que la « croix » dans le dernier verset.

Heureusement, le Dr Matheson relata un épisode de la composition de ce cantique :

« Mon cantique a été composé dans la maison du pasteur d’Innellan le soir du 6 juin 1882. J’étais à ce moment-là seul. C’était le jour du mariage de ma sœur, et le reste de la famille passait la nuit à Glasgow. Quelque chose m’est arrivé, connu seulement de moi-même, et qui me causa les plus vives souffrances mentales. Le cantique fut le fruit de cette souffrance et fut le travail le plus rapide que j’aie jamais fait de ma vie. Une véritable inspiration, j’eus plutôt l’impression de l’avoir entendu me dicté par quelque voix intérieure que de l’avoir élaboré moi-même. Je suis tout à fait certain que l’œuvre entière fut achevée en cinq minutes et également sûr qu’elle ne reçut de moi aucune retouche ni correction. Je n’ai aucun don naturel pour le rythme. Tous les autres vers que j’ai jamais écrits sont des articles manufacturés ; celui-ci est venu comme une aube d’en-haut. Je n’ai jamais pu retrouver la même ferveur dans un vers. »

Le cantique parut pour la première fois dans le magazine mensuel de l’Église d’Écosse, Life and Work, en janvier 1883. La mélodie fut composée un an plus tard par un organiste écossais en vue de son époque, Albert L. Peace, à qui l’on demanda d’écrire une mélodie spécialement pour le texte de Matheson.

Le propre récit de Peace sur la composition de cette belle mélodie est le suivant : « Après l’avoir lu attentivement, j’écrivis la musique d’un trait, et je puis dire que l’encre de la première note n’était guère sèche quand j’eus fini la mélodie. » L’origine du nom de la mélodie, St. Margaret, est inconnue sauf qu’il s’agit d’un nom très vénéré en Écosse, et certainement en référence à la bien-aimée reine Margaret d’Écosse.

Les dernières années de la vie de Matheson, de 57 ans jusqu’à sa mort à 64 ans, furent consacrées à l’écriture de quelques-uns des meilleurs ouvrages dévotionnels en langue anglaise, notamment Moments on the Mount, Voice of the Spirit et Rests by the River. Bien qu’il s’agisse de son seul cantique qu’on trouve dans la plupart des recueils, il écrivit quelques autres beaux cantiques, dont « Make Me A Captive Lord » et « Then I Shall Be Free. »

Les quatre mots clés de « O Love, That Wilt Not Let Me Go » sont : amour, lumière, joie et croix. Ces mots ont été décrits comme la satisfaction complète pour tout croyant dont la vie est totalement abandonnée à la volonté de Dieu. Il pourrait falloir le reste de sa vie pour découvrir pleinement la signification personnelle de ces quatre expressions.

The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised, To preach the acceptable year of the Lord –Luke 4:18-19.

Jesus was in His hometown of Nazareth. It was on the Sabbath, and He stood to read the scripture as He had in the past. This Sabbath He read from Isaiah 61. When He finished, He said, …This day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears –Luke 4:21.

This marked the beginning of Jesus’ earthly ministry. In this first sermon He described the nature of His ministry. Notice the many references in this passage to healing: healing to the brokenhearted, deliverance to the captives, recovering of sight to the blind, and liberty to the bruised. Jesus came to provide a remedy for our brokenness. He came to repair the damage that sin has brought into humanity.

In this article we will look at the possibility for healing that is found in Jesus. Healing is a process that requires inner restoration with outside remediation. Physical healing begins at the cellular level and restores physical function. Spiritual healing begins at the heart level and restores us to fullness of life. Jesus said, …I am come that they might have life, and that they might have it more abundantly – John 10:10.

As Jesus walked the dusty paths of Judea, He encountered many who needed physical healing. It was His ability to heal that drew many to seek Him out and to follow him. Many brought their friends and family to Him for healing. There is in all of us a desire for healing and wholeness. In the garden of Eden, mankind was created to be whole. When we are not whole, we seek every possible cure. So, crowds gathered around Jesus hoping for healing.

One day as Jesus was journeying through Jericho, a blind man, Bartimaeus, heard that He was approaching. Hope sprang up in his breast. He began to call out to Jesus, “Jesus, thou son of David, have mercy on me.” They tried to silence him, but he called the louder, “Jesus, thou son of David, have mercy on me.”

He cast his coat aside and blindly rushed into the street. Jesus said to him, “What wilt thou that I should do unto thee?” He said, “Lord, that I might receive my sight.” Jesus’ response to this simple faith was, “Go thy way; thy faith hath made thee whole.” Immediately, he received his sight, and followed Jesus. This is just one example of Jesus’ healing ministry. The examples are many. He healed lepers. He healed paralytics. He healed men and women of unclean spirits.

Does Jesus still heal in our day? I would like to answer that question by sharing my own journey of healing. I realize that not all are healed. Even in Jesus’ day, not all were healed. But I want to share my journey of healing to demonstrate the interconnectedness of the physical and the spiritual.

I was diagnosed with cancer in May of 2020. Hearing a doctor say, “You have millions of cancer cells in your body”, brought me face to face with my mortality like never before. Oh, I knew that someday I would die, but that was always somewhere in the far distant future. Now I needed to face the fact that I had a disease growing within me which had the potential to destroy my body.

Is any sick among you? let him call for the elders of the church; and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord: And the prayer of faith shall save the sick, and the Lord shall raise him up; and if he have committed sins, they shall be forgiven him. Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed. The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much –James 5:14-16.

I have always been a strong advocate of anointing with oil. Just like we are taught in the book of James, I called for the elders of the church and asked them to anoint me with oil. In the biblical teaching of God healing through the anointing with oil there are a number of things that are expected of those seeking the healing. There is: call[ing] for the elders of the church, the prayer of faith, pray[ing] one for another, Confess[ing] your faults one to another, the effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man… and the list goes on. So, one of the necessities to seek healing through the anointing with oil is the clearing of the heart of any known, unconfessed sin. Hence, I searched my heart and cleansed my heart of anything that would hinder God’s healing of my body.

Notice the close correlation in this passage between the physical and the spiritual. I found in my journey of healing that the one affects the other. Physical healing begins with spiritual healing. A few drops of oil have no therapeutic benefit. This anointing with oil is primarily a spiritual exercise. If we practice this ordinance as James offered it, we cleanse our hearts inwardly and then we ask God for physical healing.

This was my first step to healing, but a long journey lay ahead. We consulted with multiple doctors and eventually we chose a treatment protocol that included radiation and hormone therapy. This treatment weakened me physically and made me feel my humanity. It made me more dependent on God and others and less confident in my own abilities. Living with weakness caused me to draw my strength from my Heavenly Father Who is the source of strength. I relied heavily on the encouragement and support that my wife and family offered.

There are some lessons that can only be learned through human weakness. It was for this reason that Paul was given a thorn in the flesh. He sought the Lord three times for healing. God’s answer came back always the same, “My grace is sufficient for you, for my strength is made perfect in your weakness.” I can testify that that is true.

I had multiple radiation treatments in January of 2021. I had scheduled a series of meetings for the month of February thinking that my treatments would be over, and I would be back to normal. What I did not realize was the delayed effect of radiation. I breezed through the treatments, but in February I experienced a lot of digestive issues and a lot of physical weakness.

I was expected to deliver a series of four sermons on four consecutive evenings. We prayed and although I could not get through the day without napping God provided supernatural strength for those evening messages. I praise God that His strength was made perfect in my weakness.

My doctors have plied their trade. I am grateful for the professional medical care that I received. I have done what I could with herbs and supplements and God has been merciful. My last bloodwork came back “undetectable”. May God be praised!

I am sharing my experience to show the correlation between the physical and the spiritual. Physical illness in my experience had a sanctifying effect on my spirit and spiritual renewal conditioned my body for healing. I will be forever grateful for the professional care given by my doctors, but even they realize the limits of their profession. On my last visit to my Medical Oncologist, he said to me, “Now we are going to trust the Lord.” Thank God for God-fearing doctors!

There are several examples in scripture that demonstrate this correlation between physical and spiritual healing. In Mark 2 when they let the paralytic down through the roof into the presence of Jesus, He said to the paralytic, “Thy sins be forgiven thee.” Then He said, “Rise up and walk.” When He was challenged by the Pharisees for forgiving sins, He said to them, “Which is easier to say rise up and walk or thy sins be forgiven”, demonstrating that He had the power to do both. If we believe that Jesus has the power to forgive our sins, do we also believe that He has the power to heal our bodies? I do!

In John 5, Jesus healed a man who lay by the pool of Bethesda. He had this infirmity for thirty-eight years. Jesus came by and healed him. Later when He met him in the temple He said to him, “Behold, thou art made whole: sin no more, lest a worse thing come unto thee.” Note the correlation between the physical and the spiritual.

Physical infirmity has a tremendous potential to open our hearts to spiritual realities if we allow it to. The Psalmist said: Before I was afflicted I went astray: but now have I kept thy word –Psalm 119:67. Jesus said: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised, To preach the acceptable year of the Lord –Luke 4:18-19.

Take a fresh look at our proof text for this article and notice that Jesus is offering more than physical healing. He promises healing to the brokenhearted, deliverance to the captives, and liberty to the bruised. These promises are of emotional healing—healing for the hurt that we receive as a result of living in a broken, sin-cursed world.

I am sure that there are many people reading this article who have experienced trauma that I know nothing about. But I want to assure you that you can be healed. Do you believe that? Do you believe that the pain can go away? Do you believe that you can be delivered from fear, anxiety, anger, and bitterness?

We addressed the correlation between spiritual and physical healing. There is also a correlation between spiritual and emotional healing. If you are experiencing a broken heart, Jesus wants to heal your broken heart. If you are a captive—if you are bound to a past or to an addiction that prevents your freedom—Jesus will set you free. If you have been bruised Jesus will heal you.

My wife and I are appalled at the large number of people in our Anabaptist churches that are turning to psych drugs (mind medication) and secular counseling to find solutions for emotional disorders. The Bible addresses most emotional disorders:

Fear

  • There is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear –1 John 4:18.
  • What time I am afraid, I will trust in thee –Psalm 56:3.
  • “Fear not” is found 63 times in the Bible

Anxiety

  • Be careful [anxious] for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God –Philippians 4:6.

Anger

  • Let all bitterness, and wrath, and anger, and clamour, and evil speaking, be put away from you, with all malice –Ephesians 4:31.

This is just a sampling of emotional disorders that we encounter in life, and I realize that behind these emotions there is often deep-seated trauma. Your trauma is not an astonishment to Jesus. He may not have experienced your exact trauma, but he has gone to the depth of your pain, and he has come through it in victory.

For we have not an high priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities; but was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin. Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need –Hebrews 4:15-16.

The gospel provides a holistic remedy to man’s sin problem. Our Anabaptist heritage has emphasized the fact that faith in Jesus affects every area of our lives. This faith motivates us to follow Jesus in very practical ways in our daily lives. This results in a life of radical nonconformity to the world around us.

This radical discipleship should also affect our emotional responses to difficult people and circumstances. Or have we become so emotionally fragile that if life does not give us exactly what we want it upsets our emotional equilibrium? Or maybe the gospel that we preach has become a litany of words that appeases the mind but has no effect on our soul.

Let us therefore fear, lest, a promise being left us of entering into his rest, any of you should seem to come short of it. For unto us was the gospel preached, as well as unto them: but the word preached did not profit them, not being mixed with faith in them that heard it –Hebrews 4:1-2. Is our faith in God so weak (remember that in the Biblical accounts of healing, it was their faith that enabled the healing) that we have more faith in medication or in a board-certified secular counselor than we have in God and His Word?

This is a discipleship series. Come with me to the mountain where Jesus is teaching. Yes, there is a large crowd, but follow me closely, we will try to get close enough to hear. I hear His voice—He is saying something about “salt of the earth” and “light of the world.” Here is an empty space—just room for two. Let’s sit on the grass and listen:

“Ye have heard that it hath been said, An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth: But I say unto you, That ye resist not evil: but whosoever shall smite thee on thy right cheek, turn to him the other also.

And if any man will sue thee at the law, and take away thy coat, let him have thy cloak also. And whosoever shall compel thee to go a mile, go with him twain. Give to him that asketh thee, and from him that would borrow of thee turn not thou away.

Ye have heard that it hath been said, Thou shalt love thy neighbour, and hate thine enemy. But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you; That ye may be the children of your Father which is in heaven: for he maketh his sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and sendeth rain on the just and on the unjust.”

These are radical teachings. Radical in that they are so opposite from our natural inclinations, and yet, this is the way of peace. Most of our negative emotions such as anger, fear, and anxiety can be remedied by applying these teachings of Jesus to our situations. This may sound overly simplistic, but that is the nature of the gospel and millions of people have found life and freedom through faith in Christ.

Bless the LORD, O my soul: and all that is within me, bless his holy name. Bless the LORD, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits: Who forgiveth all thine iniquities; who healeth all thy diseases; Who redeemeth thy life from destruction; who crowneth thee with lovingkindness and tender mercies; Who satisfieth thy mouth with good things; so that thy youth is renewed like the eagle’s –Psalm 103:1-5.

Herrens Ånd er over meg, for han har salvet meg til å forkynne gode nyheter for de fattige; han har sendt meg for å lege dem som har et knust hjerte, for å forkynne frihet for fangene og syn for de blinde, for å sette de knuste fri, for å forkynne Herrens nådeår – Lukas 4:18-19.

Jesus var i sin hjemby Nasaret. Det var sabbat, og han reiste seg for å lese Skriften som han hadde gjort tidligere. Denne sabbaten leste han fra Jesaja 61. Da han var ferdig, sa han, …I dag er denne skriften oppfylt i deres ører – Lukas 4:21.

Dette markerte begynnelsen på Jesu jordiske tjeneste. I denne første prekenen beskrev han tjenestens natur. Legg merke til de mange henvisningene i dette avsnittet til helbredelse: helbredelse for de knuste i hjertet, frihet for fangene, gjenvunnet syn for de blinde og frihet for de som er påført skader. Jesus kom for å gi en remedie for vår brutthet. Han kom for å reparere skaden som synden har påført menneskeheten.

I denne artikkelen vil vi se på muligheten for helbredelse som finnes i Jesus. Helbredelse er en prosess som krever indre restaurering sammen med ytre utbedring. Fysisk helbredelse begynner på cellenivå og gjenoppretter fysisk funksjon. Åndelig helbredelse begynner i hjertet og gjenoppretter oss til livets fylde. Jesus sa, …Jeg er kommet for at de skal ha liv, og ha det i overflod – Johannes 10:10.

Mens Jesus vandret på de støvete stier i Judea, møtte han mange som trengte fysisk helbredelse. Det var hans evne til å helbrede som fikk mange til å søke ham og følge ham. Mange tok med venner og familie til ham for helbredelse. Det ligger i oss alle et ønske om helbredelse og å være hele. I Edens hage ble mennesket skapt for å være helt. Når vi ikke er hele, søker vi enhver mulig kur. Så samlet folkemengder seg rundt Jesus i håp om helbredelse.

En dag, mens Jesus var på vei gjennom Jeriko, hørte en blind mann, Bartimeus, at han nærmet seg. Håpet våknet i hans bryst. Han begynte å rope til Jesus: «Jesus, Davids sønn, forbarm deg over meg.» De forsøkte å tie ham, men han ropte høyere: «Jesus, Davids sønn, forbarm deg over meg.»

Han kastet kåpen til side og stormet blint ut i gaten. Jesus sa til ham: «Hva vil du at jeg skal gjøre for deg?» Han svarte: «Herre, at jeg får synet mitt.» Jesu svar på denne enkle troen var: «Gå bort; din tro har gjort deg frisk.» Øyeblikkelig fikk han synet tilbake og fulgte Jesus. Dette er bare ett eksempel på Jesu helbredelsestjeneste. Eksemplene er mange. Han helbredet spedalske. Han helbredet lamme. Han helbredet menn og kvinner fra urene ånder.

Helbreder Jesus fortsatt i vår tid? Jeg vil gjerne svare på det spørsmålet ved å dele min egen helbredelsesreise. Jeg innser at ikke alle blir helbredet. Selv i Jesu tid ble ikke alle helbredet. Men jeg ønsker å dele min helbredelsesreise for å vise sammenhengen mellom det fysiske og det åndelige.

Jeg fikk diagnosen kreft i mai 2020. Å høre en lege si: «Du har millioner av kreftceller i kroppen din», tvang meg til å møte min dødelighet som aldri før. Å, jeg visste at jeg en dag skulle dø, men det hadde alltid vært et sted langt der fremme i framtiden. Nå måtte jeg innse at jeg hadde en sykdom i meg som kunne ødelegge kroppen min.

Er noen blant dere syke? Han skal kalle til seg menighetens eldste, og disse skal be over ham og salve ham med olje i Herrens navn. Og troens bønner skal frelse den syke, og Herren skal reise ham opp. Og om han har gjort synder, skal han få dem tilgitt. Bekjenn deres synder for hverandre og be for hverandre, så dere kan bli helbredet. Den rettferdiges virksomme, inderlige bønn har stor kraft og virker mye – Jakob 5:14-16.

Jeg har alltid vært en sterk forkjemper for salving med olje. Akkurat som vi blir lært i Jakobs brev, kalte jeg på menighetens eldste og ba dem salve meg med olje. I den bibelske undervisningen om at Gud helbreder gjennom salving med olje er det flere ting som forventes av dem som søker helbredelse. Det er: å kalle på menighetens eldste, troens bønn, å be for hverandre, å bekjenne sine feil for hverandre, den effektive inderlige bønnen fra en rettferdig mann… og listen fortsetter. Så en av nødvendighetene for å søke helbredelse gjennom salving med olje er å rense hjertet for enhver kjent synd som ikke er bekjent. Derfor søkte jeg mitt hjerte og renset det for alt som kunne hindre Guds helbredelse av min kropp.

Legg merke til den nære sammenhengen i dette avsnittet mellom det fysiske og det åndelige. Jeg fant i min helbredelsesreise at det ene påvirker det andre. Fysisk helbredelse begynner med åndelig helbredelse. Noen dråper olje har ingen terapeutisk nytte. Denne salving med olje er først og fremst en åndelig øvelse. Hvis vi praktiserer denne ordningen som Jakob beskriver, renser vi våre hjerter innvendig og så ber vi Gud om fysisk helbredelse.

Dette var mitt første skritt mot helbredelse, men en lang reise lå foran meg. Vi konsulterte flere leger, og til slutt valgte vi en behandlingsprotokoll som inkluderte strålebehandling og hormonbehandling. Denne behandlingen svekket meg fysisk og fikk meg til å føle min menneskelighet. Den gjorde meg mer avhengig av Gud og andre og mindre selvsikker i mine egne evner. Å leve med svakhet førte til at jeg hentet min styrke fra min Himmelske Far som er styrkens kilde. Jeg var sterkt avhengig av oppmuntringen og støtten min kone og familie ga meg.

Det finnes noen lærepenge som bare kan læres gjennom menneskelig svakhet. Det var av denne grunn Paulus fikk en torn i kjødet. Han ba tre ganger til Herren om helbredelse. Guds svar var alltid det samme: «Min nåde er nok for deg, for min kraft fullendes i svakhet.» Jeg kan vitne om at det er sant.

Jeg fikk flere strålebehandlinger i januar 2021. Jeg hadde planlagt en serie møter i februar i troen på at behandlingene ville være over og at jeg var tilbake til det normale. Det jeg ikke hadde innsett var strålingenes forsinkede virkning. Jeg kom meg greit gjennom selve behandlingene, men i februar opplevde jeg mange fordøyelsesproblemer og stor fysisk svakhet.

Jeg skulle holde en serie på fire prekener fire kvelder på rad. Vi ba, og selv om jeg ikke kunne komme meg gjennom dagen uten en lur, skaffet Gud overnaturlig styrke for disse kveldsbudskapene. Jeg priser Gud for at hans styrke ble fullendt i min svakhet.

Legene mine hadde gjort sin del. Jeg er takknemlig for den profesjonelle medisinske behandlingen jeg mottok. Jeg har gjort det jeg kunne med urter og kosttilskudd, og Gud har vært barmhjertig. Mine siste blodprøver kom tilbake «ikke påvisbar». Må Gud være priset!

Jeg deler min erfaring for å vise sammenhengen mellom det fysiske og det åndelige. Fysisk sykdom hadde i min erfaring en santgjørende effekt på min ånd, og åndelig fornyelse forberedte kroppen min til helbredelse. Jeg vil være evig takknemlig for den profesjonelle omsorg mine leger ga, men selv de erkjenner begrensningene i sitt fag. Ved mitt siste besøk hos min onkolog sa han til meg: «Nå skal vi stole på Herren.» Takk Gud for gudfryktige leger!

Det finnes flere eksempler i Skriften som viser denne sammenhengen mellom fysisk og åndelig helbredelse. I Markus 2, da de lot den lamme ned gjennom taket foran Jesus, sa han til den lamme: «Dine synder er tilgitt deg.» Så sa han: «Reis deg, ta din seng og gå hjem.» Da fariseerne motsatte seg ham for å tilgi synder, sa han til dem: «Hva er lettere å si reis deg og gå eller dine synder er tilgitt», og viste at han hadde makt til begge deler. Hvis vi tror at Jesus har makt til å tilgi våre synder, tror vi da også at han har makt til å helbrede våre kropper? Det gjør jeg!

I Johannes 5 helbredet Jesus en mann som lå ved Betesda-dammen. Han hadde vært syk i trettiåtte år. Jesus kom forbi og helbredet ham. Senere, da han møtte ham i templet, sa han til ham: «Se, du er blitt frisk. Synd ikke mer, for at ikke noe verre skal hende deg.» Legg merke til sammenhengen mellom det fysiske og det åndelige.

Fysisk sykdom har et enormt potensial til å åpne våre hjerter for åndelige realiteter, hvis vi tillater det. Salmisten sa: Før jeg ble tynget, villedet jeg; men nå holder jeg din lov – Salme 119:67. Jesus sa: Herrens Ånd er over meg, for han har salvet meg til å forkynne de gode nyhetene for de fattige; han har sendt meg for å lege dem som har et knust hjerte, for å forkynne frihet for fangene og syn for de blinde, for å sette de knuste fri, for å forkynne Herrens nådeår – Lukas 4:18-19.

Se en ny gang på vårt bevissted for denne artikkelen og merk at Jesus tilbyr mer enn fysisk helbredelse. Han lover helbredelse for de knuste i hjertet, frihet for fangene og frihet for de som er påført skader. Disse løftene gjelder emosjonell helbredelse—helbredelse for den smerte vi får som følge av å leve i en brutt, syndsforbannet verden.

Jeg er sikker på at mange som leser denne artikkelen har opplevd traumer jeg ikke vet noe om. Men jeg vil forsikre deg om at du kan bli helbredet. Tror du det? Tror du at smerten kan forsvinne? Tror du at du kan bli frigjort fra frykt, angst, sinne og bitterhet?

Vi har berørt sammenhengen mellom åndelig og fysisk helbredelse. Det finnes også en sammenheng mellom åndelig og emosjonell helbredelse. Hvis du opplever et knust hjerte, vil Jesus helbrede ditt knuste hjerte. Hvis du er en fange—om du er bundet til en fortid eller avhengighet som hindrer din frihet—vil Jesus sette deg fri. Hvis du har blitt såret, vil Jesus helbrede deg.

Min kone og jeg er forferdet over det store antallet mennesker i våre anabaptistiske kirker som vender seg til psykofarmaka (hjernemedisin) og sekulær rådgivning for å finne løsninger på emosjonelle lidelser. Bibelen tar opp de fleste emosjonelle lidelser:

Frykt

  • Det er ikke frykt i kjærligheten; men fullkommen kjærlighet driver frykten ut – 1 Johannes 4:18.
  • Når jeg er redd, stoler jeg på deg – Salme 56:3.
  • «Frykt ikke» finnes 63 ganger i Bibelen

Angst

  • Vær ikke bekymret for noe; men i alle ting la deres bønner og påkallelser med takk være kjent for Gud – Filipperne 4:6.

Sinne

  • La all bitterhet og vrede og harme og skrål og spott forsvinne fra dere, med all ondskap – Efeserne 4:31.

Dette er bare et utvalg av emosjonelle lidelser vi møter i livet, og jeg innser at bak disse følelsene ligger det ofte dyp forankret traume. Ditt traume er ikke en overraskelse for Jesus. Han har kanskje ikke opplevd nøyaktig det samme som deg, men han har gått ned i djupet av din smerte, og han har seiret over den.

For vi har ikke en øversteprest som ikke kan ha noen medfølelse med våre svakheter; han ble fristet i alt liksom vi, dog uten synd. La oss derfor frimodig tre fram for nådens trone, så vi kan få miskunn og finne nåde til hjelp i rette tid – Hebreerne 4:15-16.

Evangeliet gir en helhetlig løsning på menneskets syndproblem. Vår anabaptistiske arv har understreket at troen på Jesus berører alle områder av livet vårt. Denne troen motiverer oss til å følge Jesus på svært praktiske måter i vårt daglige liv. Dette resulterer i et liv med radikal ikke-tilpasning til verden rundt oss.

Denne radikale disippelskap bør også påvirke våre emosjonelle reaksjoner på vanskelige mennesker og omstendigheter. Eller har vi blitt så emosjonelt skjøre at hvis livet ikke gir oss nøyaktig det vi ønsker, blir vår emosjonelle likevekt forstyrret? Eller kanskje evangeliet vi forkynner har blitt en litani av ord som får sinnet til å roe seg, men som ikke berører sjelen.

La oss derfor frykte, for at det løfte som er igjen om at vi skal gå inn i hans hvile, ikke skal skje slik at noen av dere synes å komme kort derav. For evangeliet ble også forkynt for oss liksom for dem; men det ord som ble forkynt tjenet dem ikke, fordi det ikke var blandet med tro hos dem som hørte det – Hebreerne 4:1-2. Er vår tro på Gud så svak (husk at i de bibelske beretningene om helbredelse var det deres tro som muliggjorde helbredelsen) at vi har mer tro på medisinering eller på en sertifisert sekulær rådgiver enn vi har på Gud og hans Ord?

Dette er en disippelkapsserie. Kom med meg opp på fjellet hvor Jesus underviser. Ja, det er en stor folkemengde, men følg meg tett, vi skal prøve å komme så nær at vi kan høre. Jeg hører hans stemme—han sier noe om «jordens salt» og «verdens lys». Her er et tomt sted—bare plass til to. La oss sitte på gresset og lytte:

«Dere har hørt det er sagt: Øye for øye og tann for tann. Men jeg sier dere: Motstå ikke den onde. Men hvis noen slår deg på din høyre kinn, vend også det andre til.

Og om noen vil gå i retten med deg og ta din kappe, så la ham få kappen også. Og hvem som helst tvinger deg til å gå en mil, gå med ham to. Gi til den som ber deg, og vend deg ikke bort fra den som vil låne av deg.

Dere har hørt det er sagt: Du skal elske din neste og hate din fiende. Men jeg sier dere: Elsk deres fiender, velsign dem som forbanner dere, gjør godt mot dem som hater dere, og be for dem som misbruker og forfølger dere; så kan dere være Farens barn i himmelen; for han lar sin sol gå opp over onde og gode og lar det regne over rettferdige og urettferdige.»

Dette er radikale læresetninger. Radikale i det at de er så motsatt av våre naturlige tilbøyeligheter, og likevel er dette fredens vei. De fleste av våre negative følelser som sinne, frykt og angst kan helbredes ved å anvende disse Jesu læresetningene på våre situasjoner. Dette kan høres altfor enkelt ut, men slik er evangeliets natur, og millioner av mennesker har funnet liv og frihet gjennom tro på Kristus.

Lovet være Herren, min sjel. Alt som er i meg, lov hans hellige navn. Lovet være Herren, min sjel, og glem ikke alle hans goder: Han som tilgir alle dine misgjerninger, som leger alle dine sykdommer; han som frir ditt liv fra undergang; han som kroner deg med miskunn og barmhjertighet; han som metter ditt ønske med gode gaver, så ditt ungdoms styrke blir fornyet som ørnenes – Salme 103:1-5.

The year was around 60 AD. The Apostle Paul had been apprehended and almost killed in the Temple at Jerusalem by a mob of angry Jews.

A few days later, he had been whisked off to the Roman Procurator Felix because of danger from a group of Jewish plotters. Felix had heard his case and though there was no evidence to convict Paul, Felix had kept him in prison for the next two years until the new Procurator, Festus, took his place.

King Herod Agrippa II came to visit Festus and the two of them listened to Paul speak. During the hearing Paul …reasoned of righteousness, temperance, and judgment to come, [until finally] Felix trembled, and answered, Go thy way for this time; when I have a convenient season, I will call for thee –Acts 24:25. Then towards the end of Paul’s oration …Festus said with a loud voice, Paul, thou art beside thyself; much learning doth make thee mad –Acts 26:24.

Festus was not speaking of scientific knowledge, but of the fact that Paul was well-studied. Worse yet, Paul was making the governor uncomfortable with his sinful life and his reasoning made clear that the only solution for both Festus and Agrippa was to follow the Scriptures of the Hebrews.

Paul was well educated. He made clear in his letters and sermons, quoting not only from the Jewish Bible, but also from a variety of Greek and Cretan philosophers and poets.

In more modern times, it seems as though science is not a friend to faith. Many scientists claim that the idea of an intelligent designer of the Universe is ludicrous. Further, many of them would say that those who believe such things are the next thing to savages.

It certainly turns many Christians away from science entirely. They do not see something so antagonistic to the fundamental Christian faith as being useful.

I can understand this point of view, but I think that we should not give up learning simply because some of those who claim to be so knowledgeable are, in actuality, quite foolish.

Creation

When I think about the subject of science, I often begin with the subject of creation. This is the beginning of everything and is the first place where “science” and the Bible first come into conflict.

Science is simply unable to accept that there could have been a Creator God who set in motion everything that we see.

There are many books delving into the subject of intelligent design and seeing God’s fingerprints throughout creation. It takes a lot more faith to believe that the universe happened by chance, than to believe in a Creator.

The Bible makes it clear that God was not only present at the time of Creation, but it was also He who began it (John 1:1-3). Paul says For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse –Romans 1:20.

People should be able to discern that there is a Creator God involved in our world and the universe from the time of Creation. They should be able to understand a few other things about Him as well. Perhaps most important for our discussion here, we can tell by looking at creation that God is an orderly God and that He created the world to function with a specific structure and laws that govern it.

This is one of the big differences between the Creation account found in Genesis and the myths of creation found in other cultures of the time. The Bible makes it clear that God intentionally created the world, that He did so in an orderly fashion, and that He made certain that every part of it meshed with all the other parts. There is no magic or mystical thinking in the Genesis account.

The Laws of the Universe Still Stand

There are many people who believe that they can alter the way that the universe functions, that they can behave in immoral ways and not suffer the rewards of sin, and that they can do foolish things and not suffer the consequences of their behavior.

The Prophet Jeremiah tells us that there are laws which are in place that will not cease to function. Thus saith the LORD, which giveth the sun for a light by day, and the ordinances of the moon and of the stars for a light by night, which divideth the sea when the waves thereof roar; The LORD of hosts is his name: If those ordinances depart from before me, saith the LORD, then the seed of Israel also shall cease from being a nation before me for ever –Jeremiah 31:35-36.

There is a whole set of laws that governs the way that the earth rotates on its axis and orbits the sun. Everything from the speed of light to the way that gravity pulls things towards large bodies of mass was instituted at the time of Creation—…all things continue as they were from the beginning of the creation –2 Peter 3:4.

Since those laws continue and do not fluctuate, we are able to understand them—at least in part. This is what science is—the study of the natural world that we see and an attempt to comprehend the ways in which it works. God created our world in such a way that if you do an experiment the same way every time, you will get the same results every time.

Science Will Never Understand Everything

The Prophet Isaiah says, For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways, saith the LORD. For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts –Isaiah 55:8-9.

Even the smartest quantum physicists will admit that they don’t understand everything. In fact, the number of questions that they have is greater than the whole storehouse of knowledge that has been accumulated.

Most of us will have far less understanding of the universe than that. We won’t understand all the details of how the atom functions. We won’t be able to do the calculus necessary to put a satellite into orbit. That’s all right. The important thing is that we learn what we can in order to understand what an amazing and orderly God we serve.

Presuppositions are a Problem

The biggest problem that we see in science is not the science itself, rather it is the biases of the people performing the science. The fool hath said in his heart, There is no God… –Psalm 14:1. By this definition, many scientists are fools.

I don’t say this lightly. Atheists observe the universe and since they believe that there cannot be a God, they must then explain how it exists without the presence of an actual Creator. This is the heart of foolishness.

When they come to gaps in their knowledge, they are silent and yet the Christian can explain them in a few simple words. As I said before, when we look at the complexity of the universe, from the tiniest things to the largest galaxies, we can see the hands of God at work.

When I consider thy heavens, the work of thy fingers, the moon and the stars, which thou hast ordained; What is man, that thou art mindful of him? and the son of man, that thou visitest him? –Psalm 8:3-4. When we think about the world around us, when we read what scientists write, it is crucial that we come to it with a knowledge that God is behind all of this. For in him we live, and move, and have our being… – Acts 17:28, and nothing that science can discern will change that.

Science should be like a detective, uncovering God’s fingerprints on the universe, not someone bound and determined to discredit His very real presence.

Many Scientists Believe in God

Looking into the past, many scientists were men who believed in the God of the Bible. Isaac Newton, Francis Bacon, Nicholas Copernicus and many others believed in the Bible and were forthright in their expression of this faith to others.

In more modern days, there are many men and women of science who believe in the God of the Bible. Just because one is working in science doesn’t mean that they are unable to have a life of faith.

Many people have co-opted scientific discoveries to push messages that are against Christian belief and teaching.

We need to remember that when there is a set of facts, there are usually different explanations that can account for their presence. Creation and evolution examine the same facts of nature, yet from a different perspective or bias, thus they end up with vastly different conclusions. Perhaps it is a little like a Sherlock Holmes story, where Dr. Watson routinely takes the facts and gives an inaccurate explanation of them, while the detective takes the same information and gives the right explanation.

Science and Medicine

It is not against Scripture to research how things work in our universe, as long as we do so within a Biblical framework and understanding that there is a Creator God who is ordering it all.

Modern medicine is an application of many various fields, including anatomy, microanatomy, genetics, and biochemistry. The point, in this case, is to observe the human body the best that we can and then to fix the things that go wrong with it. Doctors can be scientists, but most of them are simply applying knowledge which has been passed down to them through their training.

Observation is where things start. Let’s consider diabetes as an example. Aretaeus of Cappadocia in the second century AD was the first person to give a complete description of diabetes and actually gave the disease the name diabetes. The problem was that while he was able to diagnose people with this illness, he had no treatment to help his patients. Observation had only taken him so far.

Over time, other work was done that demonstrated that the problem was an issue in the pancreas and that something was specifically wrong with the islet cells. Even into the early 1900s, there was no cure for Diabetes Mellitus and the only solution that doctors had to offer was an extremely low glycemic diet with severe calorie limits—attempting to keep patients at 500 or 600 calories a day. As can be imagined, this wasn’t an ideal treatment.

It wasn’t until the 1920s that a couple of researchers in Canada discovered a way to extract insulin from dogs and administered it to a 14-year-old who was dying of diabetes. The extract saved his life and began a new era for people with diabetes.

This is the way that things work. We begin by observing a disease and various medications that seem to be effective for it, then over time and through meticulous testing we can assess what treatments are most effective for that illness.

Studies in which half of the participants with a disease are given a medication or treatment and half are given a placebo (a pill without medical efficacy) are still the most effective way of telling whether something really works.

Why Treatments Need to be Studied

There is a real tendency to believe that the things that you have been taught are effective. We know that George Washington died of pneumonia. His doctors probably damaged his chances of recovery by bleeding him four times for a total of close to 40 percent of his blood volume. They probably would have bled him a fifth time, but he wasn’t thought to be strong enough to survive the procedure.

Doctors bled patients because they believed that there were toxic build ups in the blood stream that had to be let out. Most of the people who died after bloodletting would probably have died anyway, but bleeding people who are really sick certainly doesn’t help them recover.

Maybe the doctors simply wanted to be doing something. Patients expected bloodletting and so they met those expectations, even though it harmed the patients.

Experience is what lets you make the same mistakes with a lot more confidence.

What Makes a Good Study

Good studies—have plenty of patients in them, have a control group (that either receives an inactive pill called a placebo, or the current best treatment for that disease), and have the test group getting the new treatment. It is also important for the control group and the test group to be matched as closely as possible. Finally, the size of the groups in the study is vital to the conclusions of the study. If there are only ten or twenty patients in the study, it is not a large enough group to really sort out if something works or doesn’t.

For many diseases there is something called a placebo effect. This placebo effect is when people get better from an illness even though they are not receiving something that should be effective at treating the malady. Interestingly, in studies, many people get side effects from the inert pills. If 20 percent of the people getting the placebo get better and 45 percent of the people getting the treatment get better, that would indicate that the treatment is effective. If the difference is minimal—say 20 percent of the placebo group and 23 percent of the treatment group improve—then the treatment isn’t effective.

Problems

The biggest problem with many treatments is that they simply aren’t studied. Vitamin supplements and herbal compounds may work, but many of them have never actually been studied in a trial comparing them with a control group. Most of the information is anecdotal. The fact that someone’s grandmother or uncle benefited from something is possibly an indication that it is effective, but it doesn’t tell us how effective this treatment is or what dosage level is ideal.

Another issue is when studies simply don’t have enough participants to really give accurate information. Many studies only include ten or twenty patients. That is simply not enough to identify how well a treatment works or what side effects can be expected. For a drug to be approved by the FDA, it will typically have been studied on between 1,000 to 3,000 patients with the disease.

A final issue with studies is when they show that a medication is effective, but the effect isn’t clinically significant. As an example, a new injectable medication for dementia (aducanumab) was recently approved by the FDA. It is very expensive, and the benefit seemed to be small. Patients who were on it got an average of 1.5 more test questions right on an 85-question mental status questionnaire after 18 months compared to the control group.

One can rightly question if the benefits shown by this medication are worth the 50,000 dollar-per-year cost. More than that, how much of a meaningful improvement in someone’s everyday activities would come from using such a medicine? It seems unlikely that it would make very much of a difference.

It is unfortunate, but drug companies will always try to make it seem like their medicine is the best, even if the studies do not show significant benefit over existing, cheaper options.

Conclusion

Christians are faced with a world which does not love them or their beliefs. Many would try to use science as a way to bludgeon them into giving up their faith. I hope that does not lead us to give up on the scientific method or to give up attempting to understand the laws behind the universe that God created.

The scientific method is valid, even if many of the people who use it are atheists or agnostics. If a treatment works, it should be observable, testable, and repeatable.

Even as we approach it, we have a basic understanding of the universe that atheists don’t have. Knowing that there is a Creator God who loves us makes a major difference as we interpret the results of all the different observations that are being made in the fields of medicine and other places.

Those who do not know God are bound to be ever learning, and never able to come to the knowledge of the truth –2 Timothy 3:7. On the other hand, if we begin with a Biblical understanding, we can use science as a tool to help us to understand the creation that He has placed around us.
