El Espíritu del Señor está sobre mí, por cuanto me ungió para predicar el evangelio a los pobres; me ha enviado a sanar a los quebrantados de corazón, a pregonar libertad a los cautivos, y vista a los ciegos, a poner en libertad a los quebrantados, a predicar el año agradable del Señor –Lucas 4:18-19.

Jesús estaba en su ciudad natal, Nazaret. Era el día de reposo, y se puso de pie para leer las Escrituras como lo había hecho antes. Ese sábado leyó Isaías 61. Cuando terminó dijo: …Hoy se ha cumplido esta Escritura en vuestros oídos –Lucas 4:21.

Esto marcó el comienzo del ministerio terrenal de Jesús. En este primer sermón describió la naturaleza de su ministerio. Fíjese en las numerosas referencias en este pasaje a la sanidad: sanar a los quebrantados de corazón, pregonar libertad a los cautivos, dar vista a los ciegos y libertad a los quebrantados. Jesús vino a proveer un remedio para nuestra quebrantura. Vino a reparar el daño que el pecado ha introducido en la humanidad.

En este artículo examinaremos la posibilidad de sanidad que se encuentra en Jesús. La sanidad es un proceso que requiere restauración interna con remediación externa. La sanidad física comienza a nivel celular y restaura la función física. La sanidad espiritual comienza en el corazón y nos restaura a la plenitud de la vida. Jesús dijo: …He venido para que tengan vida, y para que la tengan en abundancia –Juan 10:10.

Mientras Jesús caminaba por los polvorientos caminos de Judea, se encontró con muchos que necesitaban sanidad física. Fue su capacidad para sanar lo que atrajo a muchos a buscarle y seguirle. Muchos trajeron a sus amigos y familiares para que fueran sanados por Él. En todos nosotros hay un deseo de sanidad e integridad. En el huerto del Edén, la humanidad fue creada para estar íntegra. Cuando no estamos íntegros, buscamos todo remedio posible. Así, multitudes se congregaban alrededor de Jesús con la esperanza de ser sanadas.

Un día, mientras Jesús viajaba por Jericó, un ciego llamado Bartimeo oyó que Él se acercaba. La esperanza brotó en su pecho. Comenzó a clamar a Jesús: «Jesús, hijo de David, ten misericordia de mí». Intentaron callarlo, pero él gritó más fuerte: «Jesús, hijo de David, ten misericordia de mí».

Se echó su manto a un lado y, a tientas, se precipitó a la calle. Jesús le dijo: «¿Qué quieres que te haga?» Él respondió: «Señor, que reciba mi vista». La respuesta de Jesús a esa fe simple fue: «Vete; tu fe te ha sanado». Inmediatamente recibió la vista y siguió a Jesús. Este es solo un ejemplo del ministerio de sanidad de Jesús. Los ejemplos son muchos. Sanó leprosos. Sanó paralíticos. Sanó a hombres y mujeres de espíritus inmundos.

¿Sigue sanando Jesús en nuestros días? Me gustaría responder a esa pregunta compartiendo mi propio camino de sanidad. Soy consciente de que no todos son sanados. Incluso en los días de Jesús, no todos fueron sanados. Pero quiero compartir mi experiencia de sanidad para demostrar la interconexión entre lo físico y lo espiritual.

Me diagnosticaron cáncer en mayo de 2020. Oír a un médico decir: «Tienes millones de células cancerosas en tu cuerpo», me confrontó con mi mortalidad como nunca antes. Oh, sabía que algún día moriría, pero eso siempre había estado muy lejos en el futuro. Ahora tenía que enfrentar el hecho de que había una enfermedad creciendo dentro de mí con el potencial de destruir mi cuerpo.

¿Está alguno enfermo entre vosotros? Llame a los ancianos de la iglesia, y oren por él, ungiéndole con aceite en el nombre del Señor; Y la oración de fe salvará al enfermo, y el Señor le levantará; y si hubiere cometido pecados, le serán perdonados. Confesaos vuestros pecados unos a otros, y orad unos por otros, para que seáis sanados. La oración ferviente del justo puede mucho –Santiago 5:14-16.

Siempre he sido un firme defensor de la unción con aceite. Tal como se nos enseña en el libro de Santiago, llamé a los ancianos de la iglesia y les pedí que me ungieran con aceite. En la enseñanza bíblica sobre la sanidad de Dios mediante la unción con aceite hay una serie de cosas que se esperan de quienes buscan la sanidad. Está: llamar a los ancianos de la iglesia, la oración de fe, orar unos por otros, confesarse los pecados unos a otros, la oración ferviente del justo… y la lista continúa. Por tanto, una de las necesidades para buscar sanidad mediante la unción con aceite es la limpieza del corazón de cualquier pecado conocido y no confesado. Así que examiné mi corazón y lo limpié de todo aquello que pudiera estorbar la sanidad de mi cuerpo por parte de Dios.

Note la estrecha correlación en este pasaje entre lo físico y lo espiritual. Encontré en mi camino de sanidad que lo uno afecta a lo otro. La sanidad física comienza con la sanidad espiritual. Unas gotas de aceite no tienen beneficio terapéutico por sí mismas. Esta unción con aceite es primariamente un ejercicio espiritual. Si practicamos esta ordenanza como la ofrece Santiago, limpiamos nuestro corazón interiormente y luego le pedimos a Dios la sanidad física.

Este fue mi primer paso hacia la sanidad, pero quedaba un largo camino por delante. Consultamos con varios médicos y, finalmente, escogimos un protocolo de tratamiento que incluyó radioterapia y terapia hormonal. Este tratamiento me debilitó físicamente y me hizo sentir mi humanidad. Me hizo depender más de Dios y de los demás y menos confiar en mis propias fuerzas. Vivir con debilidad me llevó a sacar fuerzas de mi Padre Celestial, que es la fuente de fortaleza. Dependí en gran medida del aliento y apoyo que me brindaron mi esposa y mi familia.

Hay lecciones que solo pueden aprenderse mediante la debilidad humana. Fue por esta razón que a Pablo se le dio una espina en la carne. Él buscó al Señor tres veces para ser sanado. La respuesta de Dios fue siempre la misma: «Mi gracia te basta, porque mi poder se perfecciona en la debilidad». Puedo dar testimonio de que eso es cierto.

Tuve múltiples tratamientos de radiación en enero de 2021. Había programado una serie de reuniones para el mes de febrero pensando que mis tratamientos habrían terminado y volvería a la normalidad. Lo que no había previsto fue el efecto retardado de la radiación. Pasé los tratamientos sin mayor problema, pero en febrero experimenté muchos problemas digestivos y mucha debilidad física.

Se esperaba que predicara una serie de cuatro sermones en cuatro noches consecutivas. Oramos y, aunque no podía pasar el día sin dormir siestas, Dios me proveyó de fuerza sobrenatural para esos mensajes nocturnos. Alabo a Dios porque su poder se perfeccionó en mi debilidad.

Mis médicos han aplicado su saber. Estoy agradecido por la atención médica profesional que recibí. He hecho lo que pude con hierbas y suplementos y Dios ha sido misericordioso. Mis últimos análisis de sangre resultaron «indetectables». ¡Sea alabado Dios!

Comparto mi experiencia para mostrar la correlación entre lo físico y lo espiritual. La enfermedad física, en mi experiencia, tuvo un efecto santificador sobre mi espíritu y la renovación espiritual condicionó a mi cuerpo para la sanidad. Siempre estaré agradecido por la atención profesional de mis médicos, pero incluso ellos reconocen los límites de su profesión. En mi última visita con mi oncólogo médico, me dijo: «Ahora vamos a confiar en el Señor». ¡Gracias a Dios por médicos que temen a Dios!

Hay varios ejemplos en las Escrituras que demuestran esta correlación entre la sanidad física y la espiritual. En Marcos 2, cuando bajan al paralítico por el techo a la presencia de Jesús, Él le dice al paralítico: «Tus pecados te son perdonados». Luego le dijo: «Levántate y anda». Cuando los fariseos lo cuestionaron por perdonar pecados, Él les dijo: «¿Qué es más fácil decir levántate y anda o tus pecados te son perdonados?», demostrando que tenía poder para hacer ambas cosas. Si creemos que Jesús tiene poder para perdonar nuestros pecados, ¿no creemos también que tiene poder para sanar nuestros cuerpos? ¡Yo sí!

En Juan 5, Jesús sanó a un hombre que yacía junto a la piscina de Betesda. Tenía esa dolencia por treinta y ocho años. Jesús pasó por allí y lo sanó. Más tarde, cuando lo encontró en el templo, le dijo: «Mira, has sido sanado; no peques más, para que no te venga algo peor». Nótese la correlación entre lo físico y lo espiritual.

La dolencia física tiene un enorme potencial para abrir nuestro corazón a realidades espirituales si se lo permitimos. El salmista dijo: Antes que fuese yo humillado, andaba descarriado; mas ahora guardo tu palabra –Salmo 119:67. Jesús dijo: El Espíritu del Señor está sobre mí, por cuanto me ungió para predicar el evangelio a los pobres; me ha enviado a sanar a los quebrantados de corazón, a pregonar libertad a los cautivos, y vista a los ciegos, a poner en libertad a los quebrantados, a predicar el año agradable del Señor –Lucas 4:18-19.

Mire de nuevo nuestro texto probatorio para este artículo y observe que Jesús ofrece más que sanidad física. Promete sanar a los quebrantados de corazón, dar libertad a los cautivos y poner en libertad a los que están heridos. Estas promesas son de sanidad emocional: sanidad para las heridas que recibimos como resultado de vivir en un mundo quebrado y maldecido por el pecado.

Estoy seguro de que hay muchas personas leyendo este artículo que han experimentado traumas de los que yo no sé nada. Pero quiero asegurarles que pueden ser sanados. ¿Lo creen? ¿Creen que el dolor puede desaparecer? ¿Creen que pueden ser librados del miedo, la ansiedad, la ira y la amargura?

Hemos tratado la correlación entre la sanidad espiritual y la física. También existe una correlación entre la sanidad espiritual y la emocional. Si tienes el corazón quebrantado, Jesús quiere sanar tu corazón. Si eres un cautivo—si estás atado a un pasado o a una adicción que te impide la libertad—Jesús te libertará. Si has sido herido, Jesús te sanará.

Mi esposa y yo estamos consternados por la gran cantidad de personas en nuestras iglesias anabautistas que recurren a fármacos psiquiátricos (medicación para la mente) y a la consejería secular buscando soluciones para los trastornos emocionales. La Biblia aborda la mayoría de los trastornos emocionales:

Miedo

  • No hay temor en el amor; mas el perfecto amor echa fuera el temor –1 Juan 4:18.
  • En el día que temo, yo en ti confío –Salmo 56:3.
  • «No temas» se encuentra 63 veces en la Biblia

Ansiedad

  • No os afanéis por nada; antes bien, en todo, mediante oración y súplica con acción de gracias, sean dadas a conocer vuestras peticiones delante de Dios –Filipenses 4:6.

Ira

  • Quítense de vosotros toda amargura, enojo, ira, gritería y maledicencia, y toda malicia –Efesios 4:31.

Esto es solo una muestra de los trastornos emocionales que encontramos en la vida, y soy consciente de que detrás de estas emociones suele haber traumas profundos. Tu trauma no es una sorpresa para Jesús. Él quizá no haya experimentado exactamente lo que tú viviste, pero ha descendido al fondo de tu dolor y ha salido victorioso.

Porque no tenemos un sumo sacerdote que no pueda compadecerse de nuestras debilidades, sino uno que fue tentado en todo según nuestra semejanza, pero sin pecado. Acerquémonos, pues, confiadamente al trono de la gracia, para alcanzar misericordia y hallar gracia para el oportuno socorro –Hebreos 4:15-16.

El evangelio provee un remedio holístico al problema del pecado del hombre. Nuestra herencia anabautista ha enfatizado el hecho de que la fe en Jesús afecta todas las áreas de nuestra vida. Esta fe nos motiva a seguir a Jesús de maneras muy prácticas en nuestra vida diaria. Esto resulta en una vida de radical inconformidad con el mundo que nos rodea.

Este discipulado radical también debería afectar nuestras respuestas emocionales ante personas y circunstancias difíciles. ¿O nos hemos vuelto tan emocionalmente frágiles que si la vida no nos da exactamente lo que queremos se altera nuestro equilibrio emocional? O quizás el evangelio que predicamos se ha convertido en una letanía de palabras que apaciguan la mente pero no afectan el alma.

Temamos, pues, no sea que habiendo promesa de entrar en su reposo, alguno de vosotros parezca quedarse corto. Porque a nosotros también se nos ha anunciado el evangelio; pero la palabra anunciada no les aprovechó a los que la escucharon, por no estar mezclada con fe en los que la oyeron –Hebreos 4:1-2. ¿Es nuestra fe en Dios tan débil (recuerde que en los relatos bíblicos de sanidad, fue su fe la que posibilitó la sanidad) que tenemos más fe en la medicación o en un consejero secular certificado que en Dios y su Palabra?

Esta es una serie de discipulado. Ven conmigo al monte donde Jesús está enseñando. Sí, hay una gran multitud, pero sígueme de cerca, intentaremos acercarnos lo bastante para oír. Oigo su voz—él está hablando de “la sal de la tierra” y “la luz del mundo”. Aquí hay un espacio vacío—apenas lugar para dos. Sentémonos en la hierba y escuchemos:

«Habéis oído que fue dicho: Ojo por ojo, y diente por diente. Pero yo os digo: No resistáis al mal; antes, a cualquiera que te abofetee en la mejilla derecha, vuélvele también la otra.

Y al que quiera ponerte a pleito y quitarte la ropa, déjale también tu capa; y a cualquiera que te obligue a llevar una milla, ve con él dos. Da a todo el que te pida, y no rehúses al que quiera pedir prestado de ti.

Habéis oído que fue dicho: Amarás a tu prójimo, y odiarás a tu enemigo. Pero yo os digo: Amad a vuestros enemigos, bendecid a los que os maldicen, haced bien a los que os aborrecen, y orad por los que os ultrajan y os persiguen; para que seáis hijos de vuestro Padre que está en los cielos; porque él hace salir su sol sobre malos y buenos, y llueve sobre justos e injustos».

Estas son enseñanzas radicales. Radicales en cuanto que son tan opuestas a nuestras inclinaciones naturales, y sin embargo, este es el camino de la paz. La mayoría de nuestras emociones negativas como la ira, el miedo y la ansiedad pueden ser remediadas aplicando estas enseñanzas de Jesús a nuestras situaciones. Esto puede sonar demasiado simplista, pero esa es la naturaleza del evangelio y millones de personas han encontrado vida y libertad por medio de la fe en Cristo.

Bendice, alma mía, al SEÑOR, y bendiga todo mi ser su santo nombre. Bendice, alma mía, al SEÑOR, y no olvides ninguno de sus beneficios: El que perdona todas tus iniquidades; el que sana todas tus dolencias; El que rescata del hoyo tu vida; el que te corona de favores y misericordias; El que sacia de bien tu boca, de modo que te rejuvenezcas como el águila –Salmo 103:1-5.

Greetings of brotherly love to one and all. The year 2022 is almost gone. A lot has happened. Another year of devastating storms, floods, fires, earthquakes, wars, and rumors of wars. America has gone through another season of political elections, causing the conservatives and liberals to become even more polarized into opposing parties.

Recently, I have been reflecting on the current status of life as a committed Bible-believing Christian in our world today. Sure, there are certain places in our world where Christians live in constant threat of imprisonment or death simply because they are trying to live according to God’s Word. However, the world, seems to be moving towards an increasingly negative perspective of God’s people. In an increasingly developing trend, there is a surprising rise of hostility towards the committed believer.

What is happening? I have had numerous conversations with various believers from around the country who seem to have a growing alarm about the current victorious march of evil over good, of liberal agendas over a conservative lifestyle, and the list goes on. Current skyrocketing inflation, the potential of unprecedented heating costs for many, the rumors of rising interest rates, and the ongoing shortage of goods all tend to cause a person to be jolted out of a sense of normality.

For us as Christians, let us always keep our focus fixed on the God of heaven. This is the God that Paul declared on Mars Hill—God that made the world and all things therein, seeing that he is Lord of heaven and earth, dwelleth not in temples made with hands; Neither is worshipped with men’s hands, as though he needed any thing, seeing he giveth to all life, and breath, and all things; –Acts 17:24-25.

Let’s stop focusing on the fact that evil seems to be prevailing and increasing around us and then concluding that somehow Satan has the upper hand right now. Rather, let us be reminded about what God’s Word says. But evil men and seducers shall wax worse and worse, deceiving, and being deceived. But continue thou in the things which thou hast learned and hast been assured of, knowing of whom thou hast learned them; And that from a child thou hast known the holy scriptures, which are able to make thee wise unto salvation through faith which is in Christ Jesus. All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness: That the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works –2 Timothy 3:13-17.

Let us keep our eyes fixed on Jesus …the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God –Hebrews 12:2. Instead of believing Satan’s lie that he is somehow winning the battle for Truth right now, let’s remember that the Bible reveals that Satan can do nothing without God allowing him a temporary free rein. It seemed to those looking on that Satan had the complete upper hand when Jesus was crucified and buried. Surprise, surprise! Satan had unwittingly allowed God to use him to accomplish everything that had been prophesied throughout the Scriptures. It is the same today… God will again allow Satan whatever free rein is necessary to bring to fulfillment all that the Bible has foretold will come to pass regarding the end of time.

In this issue of the magazine, we have once more endeavored to bring you information in the articles that is both helpful and relevant to our time in history. Brother Leonard Martin, a bishop in one of our churches has shared an exhortation on spiritual gifts in the church with a number of clear, practical observations for us today. The article that we have chosen to share from “Bible Helps” in this issue is one of the best discourses on the subject of “faith and works” that I have ever read. The writer even delves, with biblical simplicity and clarity, into the controversial subjects of divine election and predestination. Finally, we have The Foolishness of Preaching an evaluation regarding the basis of churches using “the altar call”—is it founded in the Scriptures and the history of the church or is it a method that the church has borrowed from the world in more recent years?!

All of this is sure to stir thoughts and discussion—which is our goal with these types of articles. Please feel free to respond via email or regular mail with your thoughts of caution or encouragement. This is helpful for us and our writers. When you write, we also ask that you mention yes or no if we can use your questions or comments in our magazine. We have had various requests to establish a section in our magazine dedicated to hearing from our readers.

One final thought… over the years our readers have, at times, shared with us ways that they think we could improve our magazine for the good of all who read it and to present a more clear gospel message. We welcome this to continue.

May God richly bless each of you,

Curvin L. Wenger

Hilsener i broderlig kjærlighet til hver og en. Året 2022 er nesten over. Det har skjedd mye. Nok et år med ødeleggende stormer, flom, branner, jordskjelv, kriger og rykter om krig. Amerika har gått gjennom enda en valgperiode som har ført til at konservative og liberale har blitt enda mer polariserte og står som motstående partier.

Nylig har jeg reflektert over hvordan det er å leve som en forpliktet bibeltroende kristen i vår verden i dag. Visst finnes det steder i verden der kristne lever under konstant trussel om fengsling eller død bare fordi de forsøker å leve etter Guds Ord. Likevel synes verden å gå mot et stadig mer negativt syn på Guds folk. I en stadig utviklende trend ser vi en overraskende økning i fiendtlighet mot den forpliktede troende.

Hva skjer? Jeg har hatt en rekke samtaler med ulike troende rundt om i landet som synes å være stadig mer bekymret over den nåværende seiersmarsjen til det onde over det gode, av liberale agendaer over en konservativ livsstil, og listen fortsetter. Den nåværende kraftige inflasjonen, muligheten for uvanlig høye oppvarmingskostnader for mange, ryktene om stigende renter og den vedvarende mangelen på varer har en tendens til å ryste en ut av følelsen av normalitet.

For oss som kristne, la oss alltid holde vårt fokus festet på himmelens Gud. Dette er den Gud som Paulus forkynte på Mars' ås —Gud som skapte verden og alt som er i den, og som, siden han er Herre over himmel og jord, ikke bor i tempeler laget med hender; heller ikke blir han betjent av menneskehender, som om han trengte noe, siden han gir alle liv og pust og alle ting; –Apostlenes gjerninger 17:24-25.

La oss slutte å fokusere på at det onde ser ut til å råde og øke rundt oss, og så konkludere med at Satan på en eller annen måte har overtaket nå. La oss heller bli minnet om hva Guds Ord sier. Men onde mennesker og bedrageriske skal forverres mer og mer, bedragende og bedraget. Men hold fast ved det du har lært og blitt overbevist om, du vet hvem du har lært det av; og fra barndommen har du kjennskap til de hellige skrifter, som kan gjøre deg vis til frelse ved troen som er i Kristus Jesus. All skrift er innåndt av Gud og nyttig til lærdom, til overbevisning, til retting, til undervisning i rettferdighet, for at Guds menneske må være fullkommen, udrustet til all god gjerning –2 Timoteus 3:13-17.

La oss holde våre øyne festet på Jesus …vår tros opphavsmann og fullender; han som for den glede som lå foran ham utholdt korset, og foraktet skammen, og sitter ved Guds trones høyre hånd –Hebreerne 12:2. I stedet for å tro på Satans løgn om at han på en eller annen måte vinner kampen om sannheten nå, la oss huske at Bibelen viser at Satan ingenting kan gjøre uten at Gud tillater ham en midlertidig fri tøyling. For dem som så på, så det ut som om Satan hadde full kontroll da Jesus ble korsfestet og begravet. Overraskelse, overraskelse! Satan hadde uvitende latt Gud bruke ham til å fullføre alt som var profetert gjennom Skriftene. Det er det samme i dag… Gud vil igjen tillate Satan den frihet som er nødvendig for å bringe til oppfyllelse alt det Bibelen har forutsagt om tidens ende.

I dette nummeret av magasinet har vi nok en gang forsøkt å gi dere artikler som både er nyttige og relevante for vår tid i historien. Bror Leonard Martin, en biskop i en av våre kirker, har delt en formaning om åndelige gaver i kirken med en rekke klare, praktiske observasjoner for oss i dag. Artikkelen vi har valgt å dele fra «Bible Helps» i dette nummeret er en av de beste avhandlinger om emnet «tro og gjerninger» jeg noen gang har lest. Forfatteren går til og med, med bibelsk enkelhet og klarhet, inn på de kontroversielle temaene guddommelig utvelgelse og predestinasjon. Til slutt har vi «Forkynnelsens dårskap» — en vurdering av grunnlaget for kirker som bruker «alterkallet» — er det forankret i Skriftene og kirkens historie eller er det en metode kirken har lånt fra verden i nyere tid?!

Alt dette vil sikkert vekke tanker og diskusjon — noe som er vårt mål med denne typen artikler. Vennligst føl deg fri til å svare på e-post eller vanlig post med dine tanker av advarsel eller oppmuntring. Dette er nyttig for oss og våre forfattere. Når du skriver, ber vi også at du oppgir ja eller nei på om vi kan bruke dine spørsmål eller kommentarer i vårt magasin. Vi har fått forskjellige forespørsler om å opprette en seksjon i magasinet viet til å høre fra våre lesere.

En siste tanke… gjennom årene har våre lesere av og til delt med oss måter de mener vi kan forbedre magasinet til beste for alle som leser det og for å presentere et klarere evangeliebudskap. Vi ønsker at dette skal fortsette.

Må Gud rikelig velsigne hver og en av dere,

Curvin L. Wenger

Lunchtime was over and it was that delightful hour of the day when mom said it was time for a break. Since Ellie was ten, she wasn’t required to take a daily nap anymore, so she set about trying to decide just how she would spend this free time. She loved being outdoors, so the sunny skies and fresh air of this particularly lovely summer day fairly pulled her outside.

“I know!” she thought to herself. “This would be a perfect time to try some whittling with that knife Paul gave me.”

She had spent a week with her aunt and uncle who lived several counties over from hers and while there, her cousin Paul had given her a knife that he had made. It had a short, round handle and he had inserted a small piece of steel into one end. He then honed the blade to a nice sharp edge. He could carve the funniest little faces on small blocks of wood and Ellie was always eager to see what he would create next. She tried to copy him, but it didn’t seem as if she would be turning out anything very exciting any time soon. Still, it was fun to try, so she got the knife from her drawer in her bedroom and headed outside.

The large maple tree in front of their old stone farmhouse beckoned to her. Its low hanging branches seemed like the perfect place to perch and try out that knife again. Ellie selected a few large twigs and then hoisted herself up into the cool shade of the tree. Once situated, she began cutting and picking away at her pieces of wood. She still couldn’t make eyes and a nose appear, but she had fun carving notches and shaving off small pieces of bark. It was a relaxing thing with which to be occupied while enjoying the quietness of the afternoon. She was so glad this tree was in their yard, and she was so glad that Paul had given her that whittling knife.

After a time, the branch Ellie was sitting on began to feel rough and hard, and the twigs she was whittling had nearly disappeared. “I should go see what the boys are doing,” she thought. She shifted to the lowest branch and sat poised, ready to jump down like she always did to get out of the tree.

She paused, looking at the knife in her hand. “Never jump down from anywhere while holding a knife in your hand!” her mother’s voice rang in her memory. “It is a very dangerous thing to do. You could get cut very badly.” Ellie sat thinking about that for a little.

“Yes, I know that’s probably true,” she told herself. “But I think if I am very careful, I could jump down and it will be fine,” she reasoned.

She firmly grasped the knife in her right hand, then quickly jumped the distance to the ground. Just as she landed, her ankle turned and gave way under her. She fell awkwardly onto her left leg. And, oh no! That little knife had plunged into her left wrist as she was trying to keep her balance. She quickly pulled it out and watched, with her heart beating rapidly, as the blood welled up, dark and warm. It was a small cut, only about one quarter of an inch long, but it had gone in rather deeply.

What should she do now? Yes, there was no doubt about it, her mom had been right after all! In her heart, she knew the right thing to do would be to go directly to her mother and tell her what she had done. But she felt guilty and ashamed. She had known better than to jump down with that knife, yet she had gone ahead and done it anyway. Guiltily, she quickly pressed her thumb on top of the wound and slipped into the house. The bleeding soon stopped, and after finding a little bandage and placing it on her cut, she quietly put her knife away and found a book to read. She never told her mom what she had done until many years later when she was a grown woman.

Today, as she looks at that scar, which is still visible from 40 years ago, she wonders why God had protected her. She had been a foolish little girl to not go immediately to her mother and confess what she had done. She could have gotten a severe infection from getting cut with a dirty, slightly rusty knife. Even though she acted foolishly, she is grateful that God protected her, but she still wishes she had confessed her disobedience to her mother.

It is never wise to hide anything from your parents. They need to know those wrong things you do, no matter how embarrassed or ashamed you might feel. Parents need to know all the things that happen to their children It is God’s design for fathers and mothers to be there for their children, to help you when you get hurt, and to guide and teach you as you learn how to be good, obedient children. God’s way is always the best.

দুপুরের খাবার শেষ হয়ে গেছে এবং মা যখন বললেন বিরতির সময়, তখন সেই দিনটার সেই মধুর সময়টা এসে গেছে। এলি এখন দশ বছর বয়েসি, তাই প্রতিদিন এখন আর নিদ্রা নেওয়ার নিয়ম নেই—অর্থাৎ সে সিদ্ধান্ত নেওয়ার চেষ্টা করল কীভাবে এই খালি সময়টা কাটাবে। বাইরে থাকতে সে খুব পছন্দ করত, তাই এই বিশেষ সুন্দর গ্রীষ্মের日の উজ্জ্বল আকাশ আর সতেজ বাতাসই যেন তাকে বাইরে টেনে নিয়ে গেল।

“আমি জানি!” সে নিজের মনের মধ্যে ভাবল। “পল আমাকে যে ছুরিটা দিয়েছিল, সেটা নিয়ে খোদাই করার চেষ্টা করার জন্য এটা একদম উপযুক্ত সময়।”

সে তার আন্টি-চাচার সঙ্গে এক সপ্তাহ কাটিয়েছিল, যারা তার থেকে কয়েকটি কাউন্টি দূরে থাকতেন, এবং সেখানে তার কজ পল তাকে একটি ছুরি দিয়েছিল যা সে নিজে বানিয়েছিল। এর হ্যান্ডলটা ছোট আর গোলাকৃতি ছিল ও এক প্রান্তে সে স্টিলের একটি ছোট টুকরা ঢুকিয়ে দিয়েছিল। তারপর সে ব্লেডটাকে সুন্দর করে ধারালো করে নিয়েছিল। সে ছোট ছোট কাঠের খণ্ডে সবচেয়ে মজার মুখগুলো খোদাই করতে পারত এবং এলি সবসময় আগ্রহভরে দেখত সে পরেরবার কী বানাবে। সে কপি করার চেষ্টা করত, কিন্তু তেমন কিছু উত্তেজনাপূর্ণ বানাতে পারত না। তবুও চেষ্টা করা মজার ছিল, তাই সে তার শোবার ঘরের আলমারির ড্রয়ার থেকে ছুরিটা বের করে বাইরে গেল।

তাদের পুরনো পাথরের ফার্মহাউসের সামনে দাঁড়ানো বড় ম্যাপল গাছটি তাকে আকর্ষিত করল। এর নীচে ঝুলে থাকা শাখাগুলো যেন সেই নিদিফলক জায়গা যেখানে বসে আবার ছুরিটা ব্যবহার করা যাবে। এলি কয়েকটি বড় কুঁড়ি বেছে নিল এবং তারপর নিজেকে গাছের ঠাণ্ডা ছায়ায় উঁচু শাখায় তুলল। ঠিক করে বসে সে তার কাঠের টুকরোগুলো কেটে এবং ক্ষুদ্র ছাল-খসান ছেঁটে শুরু করল। সে এখনও চোখ আর নাক বানাতে পারছিল না, কিন্তু নটচ কাটা এবং খাস্কি ছেঁড়ে ফেলা মজাদার ছিল। বিকেলের নীরবতা উপভোগ করতে করতে এটা একটি আরামদায়ক কাজ ছিল। সে এই গাছটি তাদের বাগানে আছে বলে খুব খুশি ছিল, আর পল যে ছুরিটি দিয়েছিল তাতেও সে খুব খুশি ছিল।

কিছুক্ষণ পর, এলি যে শাখায় বসে ছিল তা কটু ও শক্ত হয়ে উঠতে লাগল, এবং সে যেসব কুঁড়ি খোদাই করছিল তা প্রায় শেষ হয়ে এসেছিল। “আমি কি দেখতে যাই ছেলেরা কী করছে,” সে ভাবল। সে নিচু শাখায় সরে গেল এবং লাফ দিয়ে নিচে নামার জন্য প্রস্তুত হয়ে বসল, যেমনটা সে সব সময় করত গাছ থেকে নামার সময়।

সে থামল, হাতে থাকা ছুরিটা দেখে। “হতে পারে, যেকোনো জায়গা থেকে ছুরি হাতে নিয়ে লাফ না দেওয়াই ভালো!”–মায়ের কণ্ঠস্বরটা তার স্মৃতিতে বাজল। “এটা খুবই বিপজ্জনক কাজ। তুমি খুব বাজে করে কাটা পড়তে পারো।” এলি একটু সময় ধরে সে বিষয়টা নিয়ে ভাবল।

“হ্যাঁ, আমি জানি এটা হয়তো সত্যি,” সে নিজের সঙ্গে বলল। “কিন্তু আমি ভেবে দেখছি, যদি আমি খুব সাবধানে করি, তাহলে লাফ দিলেও ঠিক থাকবে,” সে যুক্তি দিল।

সে দৃঢ়ভাবে ডান হাতে ছুরিটা ধরল, তারপর দ্রুত মাটির দিকে লাফ দিল। ঠিক যেমনটা সে ল্যান্ড করল, তার গোড়ালি মোচড় খেল এবং সরে গেল। সে বাঁ পায়ে অদ্ভুতভাবে পড়ে গেল। আর, ওহ না! ভারসাম্য বজায় রাখার চেষ্টা করার সময় সেই ছোট ছুরিটা তার বাঁ কবজিতে ঢুকে গেল। সে দ্রুত তা টেনে বের করল এবং হৃদয় দ্রুত ধক্‌ধক্‌ করে উঠতে থাকল, যখন রক্ত গাঢ় ও উষ্ণ হয়ে ওপর উঠল। এটা ছিল ছোট এক কাটা, মাত্র প্রায় এক চতুর্থাংশ ইঞ্চি লম্বা, কিন্তু তা যথেষ্ট গভীরে ঢুকেছিল।

এখন কী করা উচিত? হ্যাঁ, এতে কোনো সন্দেহ নেই, মা শেষ পর্যন্ত ঠিক বলেছিলেন! তার হৃদয়ে সঠিক কাজটি হল সরাসরি তার মায়ের কাছে গিয়ে সে যা করেছে তা স্বীকার করা। কিন্তু সে লজ্জা ও অপরাধবোধে ভুগছে। সে জানত ছুরি হাতে লাফ দেয়া ঠিক নয়, তবু সে সেটা করে বসেছিল। দোষবোধে, সে দ্রুত তার থাম্ব (আঙুলের তালু) দিয়ে কাটা জায়গার ওপর চাপ দিল এবং ঘরে ঢুকল। রক্ত দ্রুত থেমে গেল, এবং একটু ব্যান্ডেজ খুঁজে পেয়ে কাটা জায়গায় লাগিয়ে সে চুপচাপ ছুরিটা সরিয়ে রেখে একটি বই পড়তে বসল। সে অনেক বছর পরে যখন বড় মহিলা হয়, তখনই সে তার মাকে এই ঘটনার কথা বলেছিল।

আজ, যখন সে সেই দাগটা দেখে—যা 40 বছর আগের হলেও এখনও দৃশ্যমান—তবে সে বিস্মিত হয় কেন ঈশ্বর তাকে রক্ষা করেছিলেন। সে তৎকালীন কালে সরাসরি তার মায়ের কাছে গিয়ে নিজের ভুল স্বীকার না করার জন্য নিজেকে একজন অল্পবুদ্ধি ছোট মেয়েসহ মনে করে। সে একটি ময়লা, সামান্য জং ধরে থাকা ছুরিতে কাটা পড়ে মারাত্মক সংক্রমণ পেতে পারত। যাইহোক, সে ভুল করেছিল, তবু কৃতজ্ঞ যে ঈশ্বর তাকে রক্ষা করেছিলেন, কিন্তু এখনও সে কামনা করে যে সে তার অবাধ্য আচরণটা মাকে স্বীকার করত।

আপনার পিতামাতা থেকে কিছু লুকানো কখনোই বুদ্ধিমানের কাজ নয়। তারা জানতে চাইবে আপনি যে ভুল কাজগুলো করেছেন, তা যতই লজ্জাজনক বা অপমানজনক মনে হোক। অভিভাবকদের তাদের সন্তানদের সব ঘটনা জানতে হবে। ঈশ্বরের পরিকল্পনা হচ্ছে পিতা-মাতা সন্তানদের পাশে থাকার জন্য—যখন আপনারা আঘাত পান তখন আপনাদের সাহায্য করা, এবং যখন আপনি ভালো, আজ্ঞাকর সন্তান হওয়ার পথে শিখছেন তখন আপনাদের গাইড ও শেখানো। ঈশ্বরের পথ সবসময় শ্রেষ্ঠ।

Greetings of brotherly love to one and all. The year 2022 is almost gone. A lot has happened. Another year of devastating storms, floods, fires, earthquakes, wars, and rumors of wars. America has gone through another season of political elections, causing the conservatives and liberals to become even more polarized into opposing parties.

Recently, I have been reflecting on the current status of life as a committed Bible-believing Christian in our world today. Sure, there are certain places in our world where Christians live in constant threat of imprisonment or death simply because they are trying to live according to God’s Word. However, the world, seems to be moving towards an increasingly negative perspective of God’s people. In an increasingly developing trend, there is a surprising rise of hostility towards the committed believer.

What is happening? I have had numerous conversations with various believers from around the country who seem to have a growing alarm about the current victorious march of evil over good, of liberal agendas over a conservative lifestyle, and the list goes on. Current skyrocketing inflation, the potential of unprecedented heating costs for many, the rumors of rising interest rates, and the ongoing shortage of goods all tend to cause a person to be jolted out of a sense of normality.

For us as Christians, let us always keep our focus fixed on the God of heaven. This is the God that Paul declared on Mars Hill—God that made the world and all things therein, seeing that he is Lord of heaven and earth, dwelleth not in temples made with hands; Neither is worshipped with men’s hands, as though he needed any thing, seeing he giveth to all life, and breath, and all things; –Acts 17:24-25.

Let’s stop focusing on the fact that evil seems to be prevailing and increasing around us and then concluding that somehow Satan has the upper hand right now. Rather, let us be reminded about what God’s Word says. But evil men and seducers shall wax worse and worse, deceiving, and being deceived. But continue thou in the things which thou hast learned and hast been assured of, knowing of whom thou hast learned them; And that from a child thou hast known the holy scriptures, which are able to make thee wise unto salvation through faith which is in Christ Jesus. All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness: That the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works –2 Timothy 3:13-17.

Let us keep our eyes fixed on Jesus …the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God –Hebrews 12:2. Instead of believing Satan’s lie that he is somehow winning the battle for Truth right now, let’s remember that the Bible reveals that Satan can do nothing without God allowing him a temporary free rein. It seemed to those looking on that Satan had the complete upper hand when Jesus was crucified and buried. Surprise, surprise! Satan had unwittingly allowed God to use him to accomplish everything that had been prophesied throughout the Scriptures. It is the same today… God will again allow Satan whatever free rein is necessary to bring to fulfillment all that the Bible has foretold will come to pass regarding the end of time.

In this issue of the magazine, we have once more endeavored to bring you information in the articles that is both helpful and relevant to our time in history. Brother Leonard Martin, a bishop in one of our churches has shared an exhortation on spiritual gifts in the church with a number of clear, practical observations for us today. The article that we have chosen to share from “Bible Helps” in this issue is one of the best discourses on the subject of “faith and works” that I have ever read. The writer even delves, with biblical simplicity and clarity, into the controversial subjects of divine election and predestination. Finally, we have The Foolishness of Preaching an evaluation regarding the basis of churches using “the altar call”—is it founded in the Scriptures and the history of the church or is it a method that the church has borrowed from the world in more recent years?!

All of this is sure to stir thoughts and discussion—which is our goal with these types of articles. Please feel free to respond via email or regular mail with your thoughts of caution or encouragement. This is helpful for us and our writers. When you write, we also ask that you mention yes or no if we can use your questions or comments in our magazine. We have had various requests to establish a section in our magazine dedicated to hearing from our readers.

One final thought… over the years our readers have, at times, shared with us ways that they think we could improve our magazine for the good of all who read it and to present a more clear gospel message. We welcome this to continue.

May God richly bless each of you,

Curvin L. Wenger

Приветствия братской любви всем и каждому. Год 2022 почти ушёл. Многое произошло. Ещё один год разрушительных бурь, наводнений, пожаров, землетрясений, войн и слухов о войнах. Америка прошла через очередной сезон политических выборов, что ещё больше раскололо консерваторов и либералов на противоположные партии.

В последнее время я размышлял о нынешнем положении жизни как преданных Библии христиан в нашем мире сегодня. Конечно, есть места в мире, где христиане живут под постоянной угрозой тюрьмы или смерти просто за то, что пытаются жить в соответствии со Словом Божьим. Однако мир, по-видимому, всё больше склоняется к негативному восприятию Божьего народа. Наметилась тревожная тенденция роста враждебности к преданному верующему.

Что происходит? У меня было множество разговоров с разными верующими из разных частей страны, у которых, кажется, растёт обеспокоенность по поводу нынешнего победоносного марширования зла над добром, либеральных программ над консервативным образом жизни, и список можно продолжать. Текущая стремительно растущая инфляция, возможные беспрецедентно высокие счета за отопление для многих, слухи о повышении процентных ставок и постоянная нехватка товаров всё это склонно выбить человека из ощущения нормальности.

Для нас, как для христиан, давайте всегда держать наш взор устремлённым на Бога небесного. Это тот Бог, о котором Павел провозгласил на Марсовом холме—God that made the world and all things therein, seeing that he is Lord of heaven and earth, dwelleth not in temples made with hands; Neither is worshipped with men’s hands, as though he needed any thing, seeing he giveth to all life, and breath, and all things; –Acts 17:24-25.

Перестанем сосредотачиваться на том, что зло, кажется, преобладает и усиливается вокруг нас, и делать вывод, будто сатана сейчас имеет преимущество. Вместо этого давайте вспомним, что говорит Божье Слово. But evil men and seducers shall wax worse and worse, deceiving, and being deceived. But continue thou in the things which thou hast learned and hast been assured of, knowing of whom thou hast learned them; And that from a child thou hast known the holy scriptures, which are able to make thee wise unto salvation through faith which is in Christ Jesus. All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness: That the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works –2 Timothy 3:13-17.

Держим же очи свои на Иисусе …the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God –Hebrews 12:2. Вместо того чтобы верить лжи сатаны о том, что он якобы выигрывает битву за Истину сейчас, вспомним, что Библия показывает: сатана ничего не может сделать без того, чтобы Бог не дозволил ему временную свободу действий. Казалось тем, кто наблюдал, что сатана имел полное преимущество, когда Иисус был распят и похоронен. Сюрприз, сюрприз! Сатана невольно позволил Богу использовать себя для осуществления всего, что было предсказано в Писаниях. То же и сегодня… Бог вновь позволит сатане ту свободу, которая необходима, чтобы привести в исполнение всё, о чём Библия предрекла, что случится в последние времена.

В этом выпуске журнала мы снова старались предложить вам статьи, которые полезны и актуальны для нашего времени в истории. Брат Леонард Мартин, епископ в одной из наших церквей, поделился наставлением о духовных дарах в церкви с рядом ясных практических наблюдений для нас сегодня. Статья, которую мы выбрали для пересказа из «Bible Helps» в этом выпуске, — одна из лучших дискуссий по теме «вера и дела», что мне когда-либо приходилось читать. Автор даже затрагивает, с библейской простотой и ясностью, спорные темы божественной избранности и предопределения. Наконец, у нас есть The Foolishness of Preaching an evaluation regarding the basis of churches using “the altar call”—is it founded in the Scriptures and the history of the church or is it a method that the church has borrowed from the world in more recent years?!

Всё это, без сомнения, вызовет мысли и обсуждения — что и есть наша цель с такими статьями. Пожалуйста, не стесняйтесь отвечать по электронной почте или обычной почтой с вашими предостережениями или ободрениями. Это полезно для нас и наших авторов. Когда вы пишете, мы также просим указать «да» или «нет», можем ли мы использовать ваши вопросы или комментарии в нашем журнале. У нас были разные просьбы учредить в журнале раздел, посвящённый откликам читателей.

Ещё одна последняя мысль… на протяжении многих лет наши читатели иногда делились с нами идеями о том, как, по их мнению, мы могли бы улучшить наш журнал ради пользы всех читателей и для более ясного провозглашения Евангелия. Мы приветствуем продолжение этих предложений.

Пусть Бог щедро благословит каждого из вас,

Curvin L. Wenger

I grew up in the same church setting in which my parents were born and raised. However, by the time I was 10, my parents began to be concerned with the direction the young folks were going and wanted something different for their children. So, my parents got in touch with a church from another state, which helped them make connections with a small church that was located close to where we lived.

I was more of a quiet, strong-willed child and was quickly turning into a rebellious teenager. My parents did all they knew to do with me at the time. One of which was making the move to this new church since it had more of a godly youth environment. I had a hard time with this change. At our old church, I had friends that were on the same page as me and supported me in my rebellious ways, but at the new church I was more of the “bad guy” and didn’t fit in with the other young people.

Over the course of time that church dissolved, and my parents decided to move to another state, closer to a more stable church. So it was, that, when I was 14, we spent our first night in a different state, in a different house, on a different road, and with different neighbors. We went shopping in a different town and went to a different church, with people that I barely knew. I didn’t like change. I found it challenging to meet new people and make new friends. I struggled majorly with all these changes, so, I never bothered trying to plug in and be an active part in our new life. Instead, I slowly built walls around my life and heart, all the while growing colder and more rebellious.

As I grew older and harder, my parents tried to work with me, but I would have nothing to do with it. I eventually got a job and was introduced to country music and other worldly things. Since I enjoy work, I poured myself into it and worked long hours. That way I wouldn’t need to be around the family or church people, and I wouldn’t need to go to church activities. Thus, I became more removed and isolated from those around me.

The church people didn’t know how to relate to me; most of them just left me to myself. Deep down I was desperately longing for love and acceptance from my family and church. This caused me to spiral downward. I continued to stuff my feelings and build a wall around myself, all the while hardening my heart further. As time went on, I withdrew more and more from my family and the church. I felt more and more like a social misfit that no one knew what to do with. I decided I was going to run away and live my own life.

Somehow my parents got wind of this idea and tried to do all that they knew to do to help me, but I resented it. Looking back, I know without a doubt that they were doing it out of love and care, but there was a great lack in our relationship. Thus, I continued to grow harder and colder.

The summer I was 17, a visiting minister (‘Mike’) and his family came to our church for meetings. I knew them from years before and somehow through our interaction during the meetings my heart started to soften and open. I’m not quite sure why, but for some reason, I decided that I wanted to go spend the winter with them. So, my parents got in contact with them, and it was decided that I could stay with them for a few months.

My plan was to spend a few months away from everything and then I would return home when I was almost 18. Once I was 18, I was planning to leave home and do my own thing. I was certain no one could stop me because I would be of legal age. However, God obviously had different plans...

Somehow ‘Mike’ convinced me to go to along to a week of meetings in another state. While we were there, I don’t remember that the conviction was any stronger than any other time. However, one evening after the service he asked me if I wanted to become a Christian and have my sins forgiven. I don’t remember what I told him, but we talked for a while. He took me through the Bible, helping me to see what God says about it all; then we prayed. When we got up from praying, I can’t say that something major happened, but it was definitely the night that I found salvation! That night, something changed in my heart. I knew that I now wanted to do things God’s way. I knew that my end goal in life was to run the race well and to finish victoriously. That is what has helped me through the years.

On July 31, 2011, I was baptized upon the confession of my faith. The next number of years were definitely not easy. I would even say that at times it seemed to have been harder than in the years before my conversion. Out of respect to others, I don’t feel I can share everything that has happened over the years, but I will try to share several main points. You can imagine that with the walls I had built around myself and the comfort I had found in this, that the years following my conversion were full of ups and downs as I tried to relearn how to relate to other believers and to people in general.

Even though I had reached out to God for forgiveness of my sins and had committed my life to following Him, I had many old habits of relating to others in wrong ways that still needed to be sanctified. Things at home continued to improve but there was still room for progress, which added to the stress. As the years went by, my stress level continued to rise. I didn’t know what to do with it, so I resorted to taking high doses of NoDoz® with an energy drink before I went to bed, trying to get my nerves to relax enough so I could sleep (don’t try this at home, it is dangerous). The next day I would get up and face it all again. One year for most of the year I struggled with thoughts of not wanting to continue on with life. During this time, I had a very close friend who gave me much encouragement. I believe that the regular contact I had with this close friend, the prayers of others, and God’s faithfulness all working together kept me from doing something that I would have later regretted.

I had another close friend who had also gone through a lot but seemed to be finding God’s answers to life’s struggles. We would go out for supper, spending time together talking about life’s struggles. I remember times that I would leave his car and tears would be streaming down his face because he wasn’t sure if I was going to make it. Then he went to the mission field for two years to teach English.

I’m not sure what all was going on in his life but one day we got word that he was missing. Eventually we heard from him; he was okay and was living back in the states again. My heart was torn… One of the few friends that I had, had now turned his back on what he had once believed and on that which he had once tried to convince me of. Yet here I was, still struggling… Why not just give up fighting…? Why not just go live the easy life…? As time went on, I continued to long for love and acceptance. At times the struggle, the aching, and the longing seemed almost unbearable. But I knew deep down that giving up was not what I wanted. It would not get the end result that I wanted. Once more through the encouragement and regular contact with my close friend, the prayers of others, and God’s faithfulness, I continued to press on.

Another young man started taking an interest in my life and we eventually became close friends. He and his wife were a great encouragement to me. Then due to some disagreements with the church, they became dissatisfied and left the church. They threw aside a lot of what they had once stood for. So here I was once again with a close friend that had turned his back on what he had once stood for. What’s the use? Why does life need to be so hard? Maybe I should also give up… But I didn’t want to totally throw God out. Maybe I could find a church that was less strict. Once again, I came to my senses and realized that’s not really what I wanted. That direction wouldn’t take me where I wanted to go. So once more through the encouragement and regular contact with my close friend, the prayers of others, and God’s faithfulness, I continued to press on. At the time it was tough, but looking back, I see I have learned a lot by all I have gone through.

In the fall of 2015, I went to Washington state due to a work opportunity. At the time I went, there were things going on at my home church that I was struggling with. Because of all the stress that I was facing, I was feeling quite discouraged about Church life, Christianity, and life in general. I wasn’t wanting to throw my Christianity away, but I was wondering, “Is this really what it’s all about?” “Why can’t people just get along?” Is this really what God had in mind for His people? If we are “little Christs” like we claim to be, shouldn’t we be able to get along? Shouldn’t we be the ones that are joyful and full of life?

I went to Washington with these kinds of thoughts on my mind. While there, I attended a church that was both Biblical and spiritually minded. It’s hard to explain all that went on in my mind, heart, and life during those six months. But I left there and went back home with a renewed strength and vision.

We should be the light of the world! We should have something to offer others! We should be able to get along with one another! Yes, we do go through hard times individually and collectively as a church, but if we fight the good fight of faith, if we finish our course, if we keep the faith, there is laid up for each of us a crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, shall give me at that day: and not to me only but unto all them also that love his appearing. I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith: Henceforth there is laid up for me a crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, shall give me at that day: and not to me only, but unto all them also that love his appearing –2 Timothy 4:7-8.

* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

June 15, 2018, at 4:40 pm. the scream of the emergency services’ pager split the peaceful afternoon as it crackled to life. “One-car rollover on ‘Gingko Avenue’, possible entrapment,” was the repeated dispatch. As we walked onto the scene, there sat a young girl who appeared to be in her mid-twenties and was visibly banged up. With blood and tears streaming down her face, she repeated these phrases, “I don’t want to die… I’m not ready to die… I may never see my baby again.” As seconds turned to minutes, the paramedics tried to calm her anxious nerves. We searched the mangled car and surrounding area for the supposed missing baby. All the while she sat there with lines of worry and fear. She had tears and blood streaming down her face, as she repeated, “I may never see my baby again… I don’t want to die… I’m not ready to die.”

As first responders, all we found was a car seat that wasn’t fastened in, with no evidence of a baby anywhere. As the ambulance crew strapped her to the stretcher and loaded her in the ambulance, she was still repeating, “Where’s my baby…? I’m not ready to die… I don’t want to die… I may never see my baby again.”

As I left the scene that evening, with that image and those phrases running through my mind, I was struck with two sober thoughts. If that was me, miraculously surviving an accident and sitting there beside my vehicle, barely coherent, with blood streaming down my face, what would I be saying? What would the paramedics and rescue team remember me by? Would I be ready to die? Would I be clear before God?

* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

As Christians, when is the last time we helped someone prepare their soul for death? As believers who have been redeemed from the misery and chaos of a life of sin (see 1 Corinthians 6:9-11), we should …be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh [us] you a reason of the hope that is in [us] you with meekness and fear: –1 Peter 3:15.

In the fall of 2018, God opened the door for me to move to a church in a different state where I have found stability. It was here that God brought a godly young lady into my life, and we were married on November 30, 2019. Being married and having brothers who surrounded me with discipleship, compassion, and prayerful support helped me to grow in the Lord in many ways.

Being here has awakened within me a renewed vision to be the light of the world. Today, I am thankful that God did not let me go. As I kept fighting the spiritual fight, God kept giving me the strength and wisdom to do the next right thing. With each victory, my strength has grown stronger. Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you… –James 4:8. I thank God for giving me victory and for helping me find my ultimate source of love, security, and purpose—my Lord and Saviour, Jesus Christ.

Ich bin in demselben Gemeindeumfeld aufgewachsen, in dem auch meine Eltern geboren und aufgewachsen sind. Als ich jedoch zehn war, begannen meine Eltern, sich Sorgen über die Richtung zu machen, in die die jungen Leute gingen, und sie wollten etwas anderes für ihre Kinder. Also nahmen meine Eltern Kontakt zu einer Kirche in einem anderen Bundesstaat auf, die ihnen half, Verbindungen zu einer kleinen Gemeinde herzustellen, die in der Nähe unseres Wohnorts lag.

Ich war eher ein ruhiges, willensstarkes Kind und verwandelte mich schnell in einen rebellischen Teenager. Meine Eltern taten alles, was sie damals wussten, um mir zu helfen. Unter anderem zogen sie in diese neue Gemeinde, da es dort eine gottesfürchtigere Jugendumgebung gab. Mir fiel diese Veränderung schwer. In unserer alten Kirche hatte ich Freunde, die auf derselben Seite wie ich standen und mich in meinem rebellischen Verhalten unterstützten, aber in der neuen Gemeinde war ich mehr der „Bösewicht“ und passte nicht zu den anderen jungen Leuten.

Mit der Zeit löste sich diese Kirche auf, und meine Eltern beschlossen, in einen anderen Bundesstaat zu ziehen, näher an eine stabilere Gemeinde. So kam es, dass wir, als ich 14 war, unsere erste Nacht in einem anderen Bundesstaat, in einem anderen Haus, in einer anderen Straße und mit anderen Nachbarn verbrachten. Wir gingen einkaufen in einer anderen Stadt und gingen in eine andere Kirche, zu Leuten, die ich kaum kannte. Ich mochte Veränderungen nicht. Es fiel mir schwer, neue Leute kennenzulernen und neue Freunde zu finden. Ich kämpfte sehr mit all diesen Veränderungen, daher bemühte ich mich nie, mich einzubringen und ein aktiver Teil unseres neuen Lebens zu werden. Stattdessen baute ich langsam Mauern um mein Leben und mein Herz, während ich immer kälter und rebellischer wurde.

Als ich älter und härter wurde, versuchten meine Eltern, mit mir zu arbeiten, aber ich wollte nichts damit zu tun haben. Schließlich bekam ich einen Job und wurde mit Country-Musik und anderen weltlichen Dingen bekannt gemacht. Da mir Arbeit Freude machte, stürzte ich mich hinein und arbeitete lange Stunden. So musste ich nicht in der Nähe der Familie oder der Gemeindeglieder sein, und ich musste nicht an Gemeindeaktivitäten teilnehmen. Dadurch entfernte und isolierte ich mich immer mehr von den Menschen um mich herum.

Die Leute aus der Gemeinde wussten nicht, wie sie mit mir umgehen sollten; die meisten ließen mich einfach für sich sein. Tief in mir sehnte ich mich verzweifelt nach Liebe und Anerkennung von meiner Familie und der Gemeinde. Das ließ mich abwärtsspiralen. Ich unterdrückte weiterhin meine Gefühle und errichtete eine Mauer um mich, wobei ich mein Herz immer mehr verhärtete. Mit der Zeit zog ich mich immer mehr von meiner Familie und der Gemeinde zurück. Ich fühlte mich zunehmend wie ein sozialer Außenseiter, mit dem niemand wusste, was er tun sollte. Ich beschloss, wegzulaufen und mein eigenes Leben zu führen.

Irgendwie bekamen meine Eltern Wind von dieser Idee und versuchten alles, was sie wussten, um mir zu helfen, aber ich war nachtragend. Rückblickend weiß ich ohne Zweifel, dass sie es aus Liebe und Fürsorge taten, aber in unserer Beziehung gab es große Mängel. So wurde ich weiterhin härter und kälter.

Im Sommer, als ich 17 war, kam ein gastierender Prediger („Mike“) mit seiner Familie zu Versammlungen in unsere Kirche. Ich kannte sie von Jahren zuvor, und irgendwie begann sich mein Herz durch unsere Begegnungen während der Versammlungen zu erweichen und zu öffnen. Ich weiß nicht genau warum, aber aus irgendeinem Grund entschied ich, dass ich den Winter bei ihnen verbringen wollte. Also nahmen meine Eltern Kontakt mit ihnen auf, und es wurde beschlossen, dass ich ein paar Monate bei ihnen bleiben könnte.

Mein Plan war, ein paar Monate weg von allem zu verbringen und dann nach Hause zurückzukehren, wenn ich fast 18 war. Sobald ich 18 war, hatte ich vor, das Zuhause zu verlassen und mein eigenes Ding zu machen. Ich war sicher, dass mich niemand aufhalten könnte, weil ich dann volljährig wäre. Aber Gott hatte offenbar andere Pläne...

Irgendwie überzeugte mich „Mike“, mit ihm zu einer Woche von Versammlungen in einen anderen Bundesstaat mitzufahren. Während wir dort waren, kann ich mich nicht erinnern, dass die Überführung stärker war als sonst. Jedoch fragte er mich eines Abends nach dem Gottesdienst, ob ich Christ werden und meine Sünden vergeben haben wolle. Ich erinnere mich nicht, was ich ihm geantwortet habe, aber wir redeten eine Weile. Er führte mich durch die Bibel und half mir zu sehen, was Gott darüber sagt; dann beteten wir. Als wir vom Gebet aufstanden, kann ich nicht sagen, dass etwas Großes geschah, aber es war definitiv die Nacht, in der ich das Heil fand! In jener Nacht veränderte sich etwas in meinem Herzen. Ich wusste, dass ich nun tun wollte, was Gott gefällt. Ich wusste, dass mein letztes Ziel im Leben war, das Rennen gut zu laufen und siegreich zu enden. Das hat mir im Laufe der Jahre geholfen.

Am 31. Juli 2011 wurde ich auf das Bekenntnis meines Glaubens getauft. Die folgenden Jahre waren definitiv nicht einfach. Ich würde sogar sagen, dass es manchmal härter erschien als in den Jahren vor meiner Bekehrung. Aus Rücksicht auf andere kann ich nicht alles teilen, was im Laufe der Jahre geschehen ist, aber ich werde versuchen, mehrere Hauptpunkte zu nennen. Man kann sich vorstellen, dass mit den Mauern, die ich um mich gebaut hatte, und dem Trost, den ich darin gefunden hatte, die Jahre nach meiner Bekehrung voller Höhen und Tiefen waren, während ich versuchte, neu zu lernen, wie man sich zu anderen Gläubigen und im Allgemeinen zu Menschen verhält.

Obwohl ich Gott um Vergebung meiner Sünden gebeten und mein Leben ihm anvertraut hatte, gab es viele alte Gewohnheiten im Umgang mit anderen, die noch geheiligt werden mussten. Die Dinge zu Hause verbesserten sich weiterhin, doch es gab noch Raum für Fortschritt, was den Stress erhöhte. Im Laufe der Jahre stieg mein Stresslevel weiter an. Ich wusste nicht, was ich damit tun sollte, also griff ich dazu, hohe Dosen NoDoz® mit einem Energydrink zu nehmen, bevor ich ins Bett ging, um meine Nerven so weit zu beruhigen, dass ich schlafen konnte (probier das nicht zu Hause, es ist gefährlich). Am nächsten Tag stand ich wieder auf und stellte mich allem erneut. Ein Jahr lang kämpfte ich den Großteil des Jahres mit Gedanken, das Leben nicht weiterführen zu wollen. In dieser Zeit hatte ich einen sehr engen Freund, der mir viel Ermutigung gab. Ich glaube, dass der regelmäßige Kontakt mit diesem engen Freund, die Gebete anderer und Gottes Treue zusammenwirkend mich davon abhielten, etwas zu tun, das ich später bereut hätte.

Ein anderer enger Freund, der auch viel durchgemacht hatte, schien Gottes Antworten auf die Lebenskämpfe zu finden. Wir gingen oft zum Abendessen aus und verbrachten Zeit miteinander, um über die Kämpfe des Lebens zu sprechen. Ich erinnere mich an Zeiten, in denen ich sein Auto verließ und Tränen über sein Gesicht liefen, weil er nicht sicher war, ob ich es schaffen würde. Dann ging er für zwei Jahre ins Missionsfeld, um Englisch zu unterrichten.

Ich weiß nicht genau, was in seinem Leben vor sich ging, aber eines Tages erhielten wir die Nachricht, dass er vermisst wurde. Schließlich hörten wir von ihm; er war in Ordnung und lebte wieder in den Staaten. Mein Herz war zerrissen... Einer der wenigen Freunde, die ich hatte, hatte jetzt dem, woran er einst glaubte, und dem, wovon er einst versuchte, mich zu überzeugen, den Rücken gekehrt. Und doch kämpfte ich noch... Warum nicht einfach aufhören zu kämpfen...? Warum nicht einfach das leichte Leben führen...? Mit der Zeit sehnte ich mich weiterhin nach Liebe und Anerkennung. Manchmal schienen der Kampf, das Sehnen und die Sehnsucht fast unerträglich. Aber tief in mir wusste ich, dass Aufgeben nicht das war, was ich wollte. Es würde nicht das gewünschte Endergebnis bringen. Noch einmal, durch die Ermutigung und den regelmäßigen Kontakt mit meinem engen Freund, die Gebete anderer und Gottes Treue, setzte ich meinen Weg fort.

Ein anderer junger Mann zeigte Interesse an meinem Leben, und wir wurden schließlich enge Freunde. Er und seine Frau waren eine große Ermutigung für mich. Dann aber, aufgrund einiger Meinungsverschiedenheiten mit der Gemeinde, wurden sie unzufrieden und verließen die Kirche. Sie warfen viel von dem weg, wofür sie einst gestanden hatten. Da stand ich also wieder da mit einem engen Freund, der dem, wofür er einst stand, den Rücken gekehrt hatte. Wozu das Ganze? Warum muss das Leben so schwer sein? Vielleicht sollte auch ich aufgeben... Aber ich wollte Gott nicht völlig ausschließen. Vielleicht könnte ich eine Gemeinde finden, die weniger strikt ist. Wieder besann ich mich und erkannte, dass das nicht wirklich das war, was ich wollte. Diese Richtung würde mich nicht dorthin führen, wohin ich gehen wollte. So setzte ich nochmals durch die Ermutigung und den regelmäßigen Kontakt mit meinem engen Freund, die Gebete anderer und Gottes Treue meinen Weg fort. Damals war es schwer, aber rückblickend sehe ich, dass ich durch alles, was ich durchgemacht habe, viel gelernt habe.

Im Herbst 2015 ging ich aus beruflichen Gründen nach Washington State. Zu der Zeit, als ich dorthin ging, gab es Dinge in meiner Heimatgemeinde, mit denen ich kämpfte. Wegen all des Stresses, dem ich ausgesetzt war, fühlte ich mich ziemlich entmutigt gegenüber dem Gemeindeleben, dem Christentum und dem Leben allgemein. Ich wollte meine Christlichkeit nicht wegwerfen, aber ich fragte mich: „Ist das wirklich alles?“ „Warum können die Menschen nicht einfach miteinander auskommen?“ Ist das wirklich das, was Gott für sein Volk vorgesehen hat? Wenn wir „kleine Christe“ sind, wie wir behaupten, sollten wir dann nicht miteinander auskommen? Sollten wir nicht diejenigen sein, die freudig und lebensfroh sind?

Mit solchen Gedanken im Kopf ging ich nach Washington. Dort besuchte ich eine Gemeinde, die sowohl biblisch als auch geistlich gesinnt war. Es ist schwer zu erklären, was in diesen sechs Monaten in meinem Geist, meinem Herzen und meinem Leben vorging. Aber ich verließ den Ort und kehrte mit erneuerter Kraft und Vision nach Hause zurück.

Wir sollten das Licht der Welt sein! Wir sollten anderen etwas zu bieten haben! Wir sollten miteinander auskommen können! Ja, wir haben individuell und kollektiv als Gemeinde schwere Zeiten, aber wenn wir den guten Kampf des Glaubens kämpfen, wenn wir unser Rennen beenden, wenn wir den Glauben bewahren, wartet für jeden von uns eine Krone der Gerechtigkeit, die der Herr, der gerechte Richter, an jenem Tag geben wird: und nicht nur mir, sondern auch allen, die seine Erscheinung lieben. Ich habe den guten Kampf gekämpft, ich habe den Lauf vollendet, ich habe den Glauben bewahrt: künftig ist mir aufbewahrt die Krone der Gerechtigkeit, welche mir der Herr, der gerechte Richter, an jenem Tage geben wird; und nicht mir nur, sondern auch allen, die seine Erscheinung lieben –2 Timotheus 4:7-8.

* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

15. Juni 2018, 16:40 Uhr. Der Schrei des Pagers der Rettungsdienste zerriss den friedlichen Nachmittag, als er zum Leben erwachte. „Ein-Pkw-Überschlag in der ‚Gingko Avenue‘, mögliche Einklemmung“, lautete die wiederholte Meldung. Als wir an die Unfallstelle gingen, saß dort ein junges Mädchen, das etwa Mitte zwanzig zu sein schien und sichtbar zugerichtet war. Mit Blut und Tränen, die ihr über das Gesicht liefen, wiederholte sie diese Sätze: „Ich will nicht sterben… Ich bin nicht bereit zu sterben… Ich werde mein Baby vielleicht nie wiedersehen.“ Als Sekunden zu Minuten wurden, versuchten die Sanitäter, ihre ängstlichen Nerven zu beruhigen. Wir durchsuchten das verformte Auto und das Umfeld nach dem angeblich vermissten Baby. Die ganze Zeit saß sie da mit Linien von Sorge und Angst. Sie hatte Tränen und Blut im Gesicht und wiederholte: „Ich werde mein Baby vielleicht nie wiedersehen… Ich will nicht sterben… Ich bin nicht bereit zu sterben.“

Als Ersthelfer fanden wir nur einen Kindersitz, der nicht befestigt war, ohne irgendwelche Hinweise auf ein Baby. Als die Besatzung des Krankenwagens sie auf die Trage schnallte und in den Krankenwagen verlud, wiederholte sie immer noch: „Wo ist mein Baby…? Ich bin nicht bereit zu sterben… Ich will nicht sterben… Ich werde mein Baby vielleicht nie wiedersehen.“

Als ich an diesem Abend die Unfallstelle verließ, mit diesem Bild und diesen Sätzen in meinem Kopf, wurde ich von zwei ernsten Gedanken getroffen. Wenn ich es wäre, die auf wundersame Weise einen Unfall überlebt und neben meinem Fahrzeug gesessen hätte, kaum bei Bewusstsein, mit Blut im Gesicht, was würde ich sagen? Woran würden sich die Sanitäter und das Rettungsteam an mich erinnern? Wäre ich bereit zu sterben? Wäre ich vor Gott klar?

* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

Als Christen: Wann haben wir zuletzt jemandem geholfen, seine Seele auf den Tod vorzubereiten? Als Gläubige, die aus dem Elend und Chaos eines Lebens in Sünde erlöst wurden (siehe 1 Korinther 6:9-11), sollten wir …immer bereit sein, jedermann Rede und Antwort zu stehen über die Hoffnung, die in uns ist, mit Sanftmut und Furcht: –1. Petrus 3:15.

Im Herbst 2018 öffnete Gott mir die Tür, in eine Gemeinde in einem anderen Bundesstaat zu ziehen, in der ich Stabilität gefunden habe. Hier brachte Gott eine gottesfürchtige junge Frau in mein Leben, und wir heirateten am 30. November 2019. Verheiratet zu sein und Brüder zu haben, die mich durch Jüngerschaft, Mitgefühl und gebetsvolle Unterstützung umgaben, half mir, in vielerlei Hinsicht im Herrn zu wachsen.

Hier zu sein hat in mir eine erneuerte Vision geweckt, das Licht der Welt zu sein. Heute bin ich dankbar, dass Gott mich nicht losgelassen hat. Während ich weiterhin den geistlichen Kampf kämpfte, gab Gott mir beständig die Kraft und Weisheit, das nächste richtige zu tun. Mit jedem Sieg wuchs meine Kraft stärker. Nähert euch Gott, so wird er sich euch nähern… –Jakobus 4:8. Ich danke Gott, dass er mir Sieg geschenkt und mir geholfen hat, meine endgültige Quelle von Liebe, Sicherheit und Sinn zu finden—meinen Herrn und Retter, Jesus Christus.

Greetings of brotherly love to one and all. The year 2022 is almost gone. A lot has happened. Another year of devastating storms, floods, fires, earthquakes, wars, and rumors of wars. America has gone through another season of political elections, causing the conservatives and liberals to become even more polarized into opposing parties.

Recently, I have been reflecting on the current status of life as a committed Bible-believing Christian in our world today. Sure, there are certain places in our world where Christians live in constant threat of imprisonment or death simply because they are trying to live according to God’s Word. However, the world, seems to be moving towards an increasingly negative perspective of God’s people. In an increasingly developing trend, there is a surprising rise of hostility towards the committed believer.

What is happening? I have had numerous conversations with various believers from around the country who seem to have a growing alarm about the current victorious march of evil over good, of liberal agendas over a conservative lifestyle, and the list goes on. Current skyrocketing inflation, the potential of unprecedented heating costs for many, the rumors of rising interest rates, and the ongoing shortage of goods all tend to cause a person to be jolted out of a sense of normality.

For us as Christians, let us always keep our focus fixed on the God of heaven. This is the God that Paul declared on Mars Hill—God that made the world and all things therein, seeing that he is Lord of heaven and earth, dwelleth not in temples made with hands; Neither is worshipped with men’s hands, as though he needed any thing, seeing he giveth to all life, and breath, and all things; –Acts 17:24-25.

Let’s stop focusing on the fact that evil seems to be prevailing and increasing around us and then concluding that somehow Satan has the upper hand right now. Rather, let us be reminded about what God’s Word says. But evil men and seducers shall wax worse and worse, deceiving, and being deceived. But continue thou in the things which thou hast learned and hast been assured of, knowing of whom thou hast learned them; And that from a child thou hast known the holy scriptures, which are able to make thee wise unto salvation through faith which is in Christ Jesus. All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness: That the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works –2 Timothy 3:13-17.

Let us keep our eyes fixed on Jesus …the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God –Hebrews 12:2. Instead of believing Satan’s lie that he is somehow winning the battle for Truth right now, let’s remember that the Bible reveals that Satan can do nothing without God allowing him a temporary free rein. It seemed to those looking on that Satan had the complete upper hand when Jesus was crucified and buried. Surprise, surprise! Satan had unwittingly allowed God to use him to accomplish everything that had been prophesied throughout the Scriptures. It is the same today… God will again allow Satan whatever free rein is necessary to bring to fulfillment all that the Bible has foretold will come to pass regarding the end of time.

In this issue of the magazine, we have once more endeavored to bring you information in the articles that is both helpful and relevant to our time in history. Brother Leonard Martin, a bishop in one of our churches has shared an exhortation on spiritual gifts in the church with a number of clear, practical observations for us today. The article that we have chosen to share from “Bible Helps” in this issue is one of the best discourses on the subject of “faith and works” that I have ever read. The writer even delves, with biblical simplicity and clarity, into the controversial subjects of divine election and predestination. Finally, we have The Foolishness of Preaching an evaluation regarding the basis of churches using “the altar call”—is it founded in the Scriptures and the history of the church or is it a method that the church has borrowed from the world in more recent years?!

All of this is sure to stir thoughts and discussion—which is our goal with these types of articles. Please feel free to respond via email or regular mail with your thoughts of caution or encouragement. This is helpful for us and our writers. When you write, we also ask that you mention yes or no if we can use your questions or comments in our magazine. We have had various requests to establish a section in our magazine dedicated to hearing from our readers.

One final thought… over the years our readers have, at times, shared with us ways that they think we could improve our magazine for the good of all who read it and to present a more clear gospel message. We welcome this to continue.

May God richly bless each of you,

Curvin L. Wenger

형제적 사랑의 문안 인사를 드립니다. 2022년이 거의 저물어 가고 있습니다. 많은 일들이 일어났습니다. 또 한 해 동안 파괴적인 폭풍, 홍수, 화재, 지진, 전쟁과 전쟁의 소문들이 이어졌습니다. 미국은 정치 선거의 계절을 또 한 번 겪으면서 보수와 진보가 서로 더욱 분열되어 반대 진영으로 나뉘게 되었습니다.

최근에 저는 오늘날 우리 세계에서 성경을 믿는 헌신된 그리스도인으로 살아가는 현재의 상태에 대해 반성해 왔습니다. 물론 세상에는 하나님의 말씀에 따라 살려고 한다는 이유만으로 끊임없이 투옥이나 죽음의 위협을 받으며 사는 곳들이 분명히 있습니다. 그럼에도 불구하고 세상은 점점 더 하나님의 백성에 대해 부정적인 관점을 취하는 쪽으로 나아가는 것처럼 보입니다. 점점 발전하는 추세 속에서 헌신된 신자들에 대한 적대감이 놀랍도록 증가하고 있습니다.

무슨 일이 일어나고 있는 걸까요? 저는 전국 각지의 여러 신자들과 수많은 대화를 나누어 왔는데, 그들 대부분은 선이 악에 의해, 보수적 생활 방식이 자유주의적 의제에 의해 승리를 빼앗기고 있는 현재의 상황에 대해 점점 더 큰 경고를 느끼고 있는 것 같습니다. 현재 치솟는 인플레이션, 많은 사람들에게 닥칠 수 있는 전례 없는 난방비, 금리 상승 소문, 지속되는 물자 부족 등은 모두 사람들로 하여금 정상감각에서 벗어나게 만드는 경향이 있습니다.

우리 그리스도인으로서는 항상 우리의 시선을 하늘의 하나님께 고정시켜야 합니다. 이것이 사도 바울이 마스 힐(Mars Hill)에서 선포한 하나님입니다—세상과 그 가운데 있는 만물을 지으신 하나님을 보고 또 그가 하늘과 땅의 주이심으로 손으로 지은 전당에 거하지 아니하시며 사람의 손으로 섬김을 받지도 아니하시나니 곧 그가 모든 사람에게 생명과 호흡과 만물을 주시나니 –사도행전 17:24-25.

악이 우리 주변에서 우세해지고 증가하는 것에 주목한 다음에 어쩐지 지금 사탄이 우위를 점하고 있다고 결론짓는 것을 멈춥시다. 대신에 하나님의 말씀이 무엇이라고 하는지 상기합시다. 사람들이 악하고 속이는 자들은 더욱 악하여져서 속이고 또 미혹을 받게 되리니 너는 배운 바와 확신한 바를 계속 지키라 누구에게서 배웠는지 알고 어린 적부터 성경을 알았으니 이로 말미암아 그리스도 예수 안에 있는 믿음으로 말미암아 구원에 이르는 지혜가 있느니라. 모든 성경은 하나님의 감동으로 된 것으로 교훈과 책망과 바르게 함과 의 훈련에 유익하니 이는 하나님의 사람이 온전하게 되어 모든 선한 일을 행할 능력으로 온전히 갖추게 하려 함이라 –디모데후서 3:13-17.

우리의 눈을 예수께 고정합시다…믿음의 주요 또 온전케 하시는 이인 예수를 바라보자 저가 보심으로 인하여 고난을 참아 십자가를 지고 치욕을 경히 여기시고 하나님 보좌 우편에 앉으셨느니라 –히브리서 12:2. 지금 사탄이 어느 정도 진리의 싸움에서 이기고 있다는 사탄의 거짓을 믿기보다는, 성경이 사탄이 하나님의 허락 없이 아무것도 할 수 없음을 계시하고 있음을 기억합시다. 예수께서 십자가에 못 박혀 장사되셨을 때 보는 이들에게는 사탄이 완전히 우위를 점한 것처럼 보였습니다. 그러나 놀랍게도 사탄은 자신도 모르게 성경 곳곳에 예언된 모든 것을 성취하시기 위해 하나님이 사용하신 도구가 되었습니다. 오늘도 마찬가지입니다… 하나님은 성경이 말하는 종말에 관하여 이루어질 모든 일이 성취되도록 필요에 따라 사탄에게 일시적인 자유를 허락하실 것입니다.

이번 호에서는 역사적 시점에서 유익하고 적절한 정보를 제공하려는 노력으로 여러 글을 담았습니다. 우리 교회 중 한 곳의 감독인 레너드 마틴 형제가 교회 안의 영적 은사들에 관해 오늘날 우리에게 유용한 명확하고 실용적인 관찰들을 담은 권면을 나누었습니다. 이번 호에 실은 "Bible Helps"에서 가져온 글은 제가 읽어본 것 중 ‘믿음과 행위’라는 주제에 대한 가장 훌륭한 설교 중 하나입니다. 글쓴이는 심지어 신학적으로 논란이 되는 택하심과 예정의 문제들까지 성경적 단순성과 명료성으로 파고듭니다. 마지막으로 우리는 ‘전도에서의 어리석음’이라는 글을 실었는데, 교회들이 사용하는 "제단 호소(altar call)"의 근거—그것이 성경과 교회의 역사에 기초한 것인지 아니면 근래 교회가 세상으로부터 차용한 방법인지—에 관해 평가하고 있습니다!

이 모든 글들은 생각과 논의를 불러일으킬 것이고—그것이 바로 이러한 유형의 글들을 싣는 우리의 목표입니다. 주저하지 마시고 이메일이나 일반 우편으로 경고의 말씀이나 격려의 생각들을 보내 주십시오. 이는 저희와 저희 필자들에게 도움이 됩니다. 편지를 쓰실 때에는 저희가 귀하의 질문이나 의견을 잡지에 사용할 수 있는지 여부를 반드시 언급해 주시기 바랍니다. 독자들의 의견을 듣기 위한 섹션을 잡지에 개설해 달라는 여러 요청을 받아 왔습니다.

마지막 한 가지… 수년 동안 독자들은 때때로 잡지를 더 많은 사람들에게 유익하게 하고 보다 분명한 복음 메시지를 전하기 위해 우리가 개선할 수 있는 방법들을 공유해 왔습니다. 저희는 이러한 의견들이 계속되기를 환영합니다.

하나님께서 여러분 각 사람을 풍성히 축복하시기를 기도합니다.

Curvin L. Wenger
