The year was around 60 AD. The Apostle Paul had been apprehended and almost killed in the Temple at Jerusalem by a mob of angry Jews.

A few days later, he had been whisked off to the Roman Procurator Felix because of danger from a group of Jewish plotters. Felix had heard his case and though there was no evidence to convict Paul, Felix had kept him in prison for the next two years until the new Procurator, Festus, took his place.

King Herod Agrippa II came to visit Festus and the two of them listened to Paul speak. During the hearing Paul …reasoned of righteousness, temperance, and judgment to come, [until finally] Felix trembled, and answered, Go thy way for this time; when I have a convenient season, I will call for thee –Acts 24:25. Then towards the end of Paul’s oration …Festus said with a loud voice, Paul, thou art beside thyself; much learning doth make thee mad –Acts 26:24.

Festus was not speaking of scientific knowledge, but of the fact that Paul was well-studied. Worse yet, Paul was making the governor uncomfortable with his sinful life and his reasoning made clear that the only solution for both Festus and Agrippa was to follow the Scriptures of the Hebrews.

Paul was well educated. He made clear in his letters and sermons, quoting not only from the Jewish Bible, but also from a variety of Greek and Cretan philosophers and poets.

In more modern times, it seems as though science is not a friend to faith. Many scientists claim that the idea of an intelligent designer of the Universe is ludicrous. Further, many of them would say that those who believe such things are the next thing to savages.

It certainly turns many Christians away from science entirely. They do not see something so antagonistic to the fundamental Christian faith as being useful.

I can understand this point of view, but I think that we should not give up learning simply because some of those who claim to be so knowledgeable are, in actuality, quite foolish.

Creation

When I think about the subject of science, I often begin with the subject of creation. This is the beginning of everything and is the first place where “science” and the Bible first come into conflict.

Science is simply unable to accept that there could have been a Creator God who set in motion everything that we see.

There are many books delving into the subject of intelligent design and seeing God’s fingerprints throughout creation. It takes a lot more faith to believe that the universe happened by chance, than to believe in a Creator.

The Bible makes it clear that God was not only present at the time of Creation, but it was also He who began it (John 1:1-3). Paul says For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse –Romans 1:20.

People should be able to discern that there is a Creator God involved in our world and the universe from the time of Creation. They should be able to understand a few other things about Him as well. Perhaps most important for our discussion here, we can tell by looking at creation that God is an orderly God and that He created the world to function with a specific structure and laws that govern it.

This is one of the big differences between the Creation account found in Genesis and the myths of creation found in other cultures of the time. The Bible makes it clear that God intentionally created the world, that He did so in an orderly fashion, and that He made certain that every part of it meshed with all the other parts. There is no magic or mystical thinking in the Genesis account.

The Laws of the Universe Still Stand

There are many people who believe that they can alter the way that the universe functions, that they can behave in immoral ways and not suffer the rewards of sin, and that they can do foolish things and not suffer the consequences of their behavior.

The Prophet Jeremiah tells us that there are laws which are in place that will not cease to function. Thus saith the LORD, which giveth the sun for a light by day, and the ordinances of the moon and of the stars for a light by night, which divideth the sea when the waves thereof roar; The LORD of hosts is his name: If those ordinances depart from before me, saith the LORD, then the seed of Israel also shall cease from being a nation before me for ever –Jeremiah 31:35-36.

There is a whole set of laws that governs the way that the earth rotates on its axis and orbits the sun. Everything from the speed of light to the way that gravity pulls things towards large bodies of mass was instituted at the time of Creation—…all things continue as they were from the beginning of the creation –2 Peter 3:4.

Since those laws continue and do not fluctuate, we are able to understand them—at least in part. This is what science is—the study of the natural world that we see and an attempt to comprehend the ways in which it works. God created our world in such a way that if you do an experiment the same way every time, you will get the same results every time.

Science Will Never Understand Everything

The Prophet Isaiah says, For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways, saith the LORD. For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts –Isaiah 55:8-9.

Even the smartest quantum physicists will admit that they don’t understand everything. In fact, the number of questions that they have is greater than the whole storehouse of knowledge that has been accumulated.

Most of us will have far less understanding of the universe than that. We won’t understand all the details of how the atom functions. We won’t be able to do the calculus necessary to put a satellite into orbit. That’s all right. The important thing is that we learn what we can in order to understand what an amazing and orderly God we serve.

Presuppositions are a Problem

The biggest problem that we see in science is not the science itself, rather it is the biases of the people performing the science. The fool hath said in his heart, There is no God… –Psalm 14:1. By this definition, many scientists are fools.

I don’t say this lightly. Atheists observe the universe and since they believe that there cannot be a God, they must then explain how it exists without the presence of an actual Creator. This is the heart of foolishness.

When they come to gaps in their knowledge, they are silent and yet the Christian can explain them in a few simple words. As I said before, when we look at the complexity of the universe, from the tiniest things to the largest galaxies, we can see the hands of God at work.

When I consider thy heavens, the work of thy fingers, the moon and the stars, which thou hast ordained; What is man, that thou art mindful of him? and the son of man, that thou visitest him? –Psalm 8:3-4. When we think about the world around us, when we read what scientists write, it is crucial that we come to it with a knowledge that God is behind all of this. For in him we live, and move, and have our being… – Acts 17:28, and nothing that science can discern will change that.

Science should be like a detective, uncovering God’s fingerprints on the universe, not someone bound and determined to discredit His very real presence.

Many Scientists Believe in God

Looking into the past, many scientists were men who believed in the God of the Bible. Isaac Newton, Francis Bacon, Nicholas Copernicus and many others believed in the Bible and were forthright in their expression of this faith to others.

In more modern days, there are many men and women of science who believe in the God of the Bible. Just because one is working in science doesn’t mean that they are unable to have a life of faith.

Many people have co-opted scientific discoveries to push messages that are against Christian belief and teaching.

We need to remember that when there is a set of facts, there are usually different explanations that can account for their presence. Creation and evolution examine the same facts of nature, yet from a different perspective or bias, thus they end up with vastly different conclusions. Perhaps it is a little like a Sherlock Holmes story, where Dr. Watson routinely takes the facts and gives an inaccurate explanation of them, while the detective takes the same information and gives the right explanation.

Science and Medicine

It is not against Scripture to research how things work in our universe, as long as we do so within a Biblical framework and understanding that there is a Creator God who is ordering it all.

Modern medicine is an application of many various fields, including anatomy, microanatomy, genetics, and biochemistry. The point, in this case, is to observe the human body the best that we can and then to fix the things that go wrong with it. Doctors can be scientists, but most of them are simply applying knowledge which has been passed down to them through their training.

Observation is where things start. Let’s consider diabetes as an example. Aretaeus of Cappadocia in the second century AD was the first person to give a complete description of diabetes and actually gave the disease the name diabetes. The problem was that while he was able to diagnose people with this illness, he had no treatment to help his patients. Observation had only taken him so far.

Over time, other work was done that demonstrated that the problem was an issue in the pancreas and that something was specifically wrong with the islet cells. Even into the early 1900s, there was no cure for Diabetes Mellitus and the only solution that doctors had to offer was an extremely low glycemic diet with severe calorie limits—attempting to keep patients at 500 or 600 calories a day. As can be imagined, this wasn’t an ideal treatment.

It wasn’t until the 1920s that a couple of researchers in Canada discovered a way to extract insulin from dogs and administered it to a 14-year-old who was dying of diabetes. The extract saved his life and began a new era for people with diabetes.

This is the way that things work. We begin by observing a disease and various medications that seem to be effective for it, then over time and through meticulous testing we can assess what treatments are most effective for that illness.

Studies in which half of the participants with a disease are given a medication or treatment and half are given a placebo (a pill without medical efficacy) are still the most effective way of telling whether something really works.

Why Treatments Need to be Studied

There is a real tendency to believe that the things that you have been taught are effective. We know that George Washington died of pneumonia. His doctors probably damaged his chances of recovery by bleeding him four times for a total of close to 40 percent of his blood volume. They probably would have bled him a fifth time, but he wasn’t thought to be strong enough to survive the procedure.

Doctors bled patients because they believed that there were toxic build ups in the blood stream that had to be let out. Most of the people who died after bloodletting would probably have died anyway, but bleeding people who are really sick certainly doesn’t help them recover.

Maybe the doctors simply wanted to be doing something. Patients expected bloodletting and so they met those expectations, even though it harmed the patients.

Experience is what lets you make the same mistakes with a lot more confidence.

What Makes a Good Study

Good studies—have plenty of patients in them, have a control group (that either receives an inactive pill called a placebo, or the current best treatment for that disease), and have the test group getting the new treatment. It is also important for the control group and the test group to be matched as closely as possible. Finally, the size of the groups in the study is vital to the conclusions of the study. If there are only ten or twenty patients in the study, it is not a large enough group to really sort out if something works or doesn’t.

For many diseases there is something called a placebo effect. This placebo effect is when people get better from an illness even though they are not receiving something that should be effective at treating the malady. Interestingly, in studies, many people get side effects from the inert pills. If 20 percent of the people getting the placebo get better and 45 percent of the people getting the treatment get better, that would indicate that the treatment is effective. If the difference is minimal—say 20 percent of the placebo group and 23 percent of the treatment group improve—then the treatment isn’t effective.

Problems

The biggest problem with many treatments is that they simply aren’t studied. Vitamin supplements and herbal compounds may work, but many of them have never actually been studied in a trial comparing them with a control group. Most of the information is anecdotal. The fact that someone’s grandmother or uncle benefited from something is possibly an indication that it is effective, but it doesn’t tell us how effective this treatment is or what dosage level is ideal.

Another issue is when studies simply don’t have enough participants to really give accurate information. Many studies only include ten or twenty patients. That is simply not enough to identify how well a treatment works or what side effects can be expected. For a drug to be approved by the FDA, it will typically have been studied on between 1,000 to 3,000 patients with the disease.

A final issue with studies is when they show that a medication is effective, but the effect isn’t clinically significant. As an example, a new injectable medication for dementia (aducanumab) was recently approved by the FDA. It is very expensive, and the benefit seemed to be small. Patients who were on it got an average of 1.5 more test questions right on an 85-question mental status questionnaire after 18 months compared to the control group.

One can rightly question if the benefits shown by this medication are worth the 50,000 dollar-per-year cost. More than that, how much of a meaningful improvement in someone’s everyday activities would come from using such a medicine? It seems unlikely that it would make very much of a difference.

It is unfortunate, but drug companies will always try to make it seem like their medicine is the best, even if the studies do not show significant benefit over existing, cheaper options.

Conclusion

Christians are faced with a world which does not love them or their beliefs. Many would try to use science as a way to bludgeon them into giving up their faith. I hope that does not lead us to give up on the scientific method or to give up attempting to understand the laws behind the universe that God created.

The scientific method is valid, even if many of the people who use it are atheists or agnostics. If a treatment works, it should be observable, testable, and repeatable.

Even as we approach it, we have a basic understanding of the universe that atheists don’t have. Knowing that there is a Creator God who loves us makes a major difference as we interpret the results of all the different observations that are being made in the fields of medicine and other places.

Those who do not know God are bound to be ever learning, and never able to come to the knowledge of the truth –2 Timothy 3:7. On the other hand, if we begin with a Biblical understanding, we can use science as a tool to help us to understand the creation that He has placed around us.

Het jaar was ongeveer 60 na Christus. De apostel Paulus was gearresteerd en bijna gedood in de tempel in Jeruzalem door een menigte boze Joden.

Enkele dagen later was hij vanwege gevaar van een groep Joodse samenzweerders aan de Romeinse procurator Felix overgedragen. Felix had zijn zaak gehoord en hoewel er geen bewijs was om Paulus te veroordelen, hield Felix hem de volgende twee jaar gevangen totdat de nieuwe procurator, Festus, zijn plaats innam.

Koning Herodes Agrippa II kwam op bezoek bij Festus en beiden luisterden naar Paulus spreken. Tijdens de hoorzitting …redeneerde hij over rechtvaardigheid, zelfbeheersing en het komende oordeel, [totdat eindelijk] Felix beefde en antwoordde: Ga nu heen; wanneer ik een geschikt ogenblik heb, zal ik u roepen – Handelingen 24:25. Tegen het einde van Paulus’ rede …zei Festus met luide stem: Paulus, gij zijt buiten uzelf; veel geleerdheid maakt u krankzinnig – Handelingen 26:24.

Festus sprak niet over wetenschappelijke kennis, maar over het feit dat Paulus goed geleerd was. Het ergste was dat Paulus de gouverneur ongemakkelijk maakte met zijn zondige leven en zijn redenering maakte duidelijk dat de enige oplossing voor zowel Festus als Agrippa was de Schriften van de Hebreeën te volgen.

Paulus was goed opgeleid. Hij maakte in zijn brieven en predicaties duidelijk dat hij niet alleen uit de Joodse Bijbel citeerde, maar ook uit verschillende Griekse en Kretenzische filosofen en dichters.

In meer moderne tijden lijkt het alsof de wetenschap geen vriend van het geloof is. Veel wetenschappers beweren dat het idee van een intelligente ontwerper van het universum belachelijk is. Bovendien zouden velen zeggen dat degenen die zulke dingen geloven, haast niet anders dan wilden zijn.

Het verjaagt zeker veel christenen helemaal van de wetenschap. Zij zien iets dat zo antagonistisch is ten opzichte van het fundamentele christelijke geloof niet als nuttig.

Ik kan dit standpunt begrijpen, maar ik denk dat we het leren niet moeten opgeven alleen omdat sommigen die beweren zo deskundig te zijn, in werkelijkheid nogal dwaas zijn.

Schepping

Als ik aan het onderwerp wetenschap denk, begin ik vaak bij het onderwerp schepping. Dit is het begin van alles en is de eerste plaats waar "wetenschap" en de Bijbel in conflict komen.

De wetenschap kan zich eenvoudigweg niet voorstellen dat er een Scheppende God zou kunnen zijn die in beweging zette wat wij zien.

Er zijn veel boeken die ingaan op intelligent ontwerp en op het zien van Gods vingerafdrukken door de schepping heen. Het vergt veel meer geloof te geloven dat het universum per toeval is ontstaan dan om in een Schepper te geloven.

De Bijbel maakt duidelijk dat God niet alleen aanwezig was bij de schepping, maar dat Hij die ook begon (Johannes 1:1-3). Paulus zegt: Want de onzienlijke dingen van Hem, namelijk Zijn eeuwige kracht en Godheid, worden sinds de schepping van de wereld door de dingen die gemaakt zijn, gezien en verstaan, zodat zij geen verontschuldiging hebben – Romeinen 1:20.

Mensen zouden moeten kunnen onderscheiden dat er een Scheppende God betrokken is bij onze wereld en het heelal vanaf de schepping. Ze zouden ook een paar andere dingen over Hem moeten kunnen begrijpen. Misschien het belangrijkste voor onze bespreking hier is dat we door naar de schepping te kijken kunnen zeggen dat God een ordelijke God is en dat Hij de wereld heeft geschapen om te functioneren met een specifieke structuur en wetten die haar beheersen.

Dit is een van de grote verschillen tussen het scheppingsverslag in Genesis en de scheppingsmythen uit andere culturen van die tijd. De Bijbel maakt duidelijk dat God opzettelijk de wereld schiep, dat Hij dat op ordelijke wijze deed, en dat Hij ervoor zorgde dat elk onderdeel op elkaar aansloot. Er is geen magie of mystiek denken in het Genesisverslag.

De wetten van het heelal blijven gelden

Er zijn veel mensen die geloven dat zij de manier waarop het heelal functioneert kunnen veranderen, dat zij immoreel kunnen leven zonder de gevolgen van zonde te ondervinden, en dat zij dwaze dingen kunnen doen zonder de consequenties van hun gedrag te lijden.

De profeet Jeremia vertelt ons dat er wetten zijn die ingesteld zijn en die niet zullen ophouden te functioneren. Zo zegt de HEER, die de zon geeft als licht overdag en de verordeningen van de maan en de sterren als licht 's nachts, die de zee deelt als haar golven bruisen; De HEER der heerscharen is Zijn naam: Indien die verordeningen van voor Mij weggaan, zegt de HEER, dan zal ook het zaad Israëls ophouden voor Mij een volk te zijn, voor eeuwig – Jeremia 31:35-36.

Er is een heel stel wetten dat regelt hoe de aarde om haar as draait en de zon omcirkelt. Alles, van de snelheid van het licht tot de manier waarop zwaartekracht dingen naar grote massa's toe trekt, werd ingesteld bij de schepping—…al deze dingen blijven zo voortgaan sinds het begin der schepping – 2 Petrus 3:4.

Aangezien die wetten blijven bestaan en niet fluctueren, kunnen wij ze begrijpen—althans gedeeltelijk. Dat is wat wetenschap is—de studie van de natuurlijke wereld die wij zien en een poging te begrijpen hoe zij werkt. God heeft onze wereld zodanig geschapen dat als je een experiment elke keer op dezelfde manier uitvoert, je elke keer dezelfde resultaten zult krijgen.

De wetenschap zal nooit alles begrijpen

De profeet Jesaja zegt: Want Mijn gedachten zijn niet uw gedachten, en uw wegen zijn niet Mijn wegen, spreekt de HEER. Want gelijk de hemelen hoger zijn dan de aarde, alzo zijn Mijn wegen hoger dan uw wegen, en Mijn gedachten dan uw gedachten – Jesaja 55:8-9.

Zelfs de slimste quantumfysici zullen toegeven dat ze niet alles begrijpen. In feite is het aantal vragen dat zij hebben groter dan de totale voorraad kennis die is vergaard.

De meesten van ons zullen veel minder begrip van het heelal hebben dan dat. We zullen niet alle details van hoe het atoom functioneert begrijpen. We zullen niet in staat zijn het nodige rekenwerk te doen om een satelliet in een baan te brengen. Dat is prima. Het belangrijkste is dat we leren wat we kunnen om te begrijpen wat voor een verbazingwekkende en ordelijke God wij dienen.

Presupposities zijn een probleem

Het grootste probleem dat we in de wetenschap zien is niet de wetenschap zelf, maar de vooroordelen van de mensen die de wetenschap bedrijven. De dwaas heeft gezegd in zijn hart: Er is geen God… – Psalm 14:1. Volgens deze definitie zijn veel wetenschappers dwazen.

Ik zeg dit niet lichtvaardig. Atheïsten observeren het heelal en omdat zij geloven dat er geen God kan zijn, moeten zij dan verklaren hoe het bestaat zonder de aanwezigheid van een werkelijke Schepper. Dit is de kern van dwaasheid.

Wanneer zij op hiaten in hun kennis stuiten, zwijgen zij, terwijl de christen ze met een paar eenvoudige woorden kan verklaren. Zoals ik eerder zei, wanneer we kijken naar de complexiteit van het universum, van de kleinste dingen tot de grootste melkwegstelsels, kunnen we de handen van God aan het werk zien.

Als ik Uw hemelen overzie, het werk van Uw vingers, de maan en de sterren die Gij bereid hebt; wat is de mens, dat Gij aan hem denkt? en het mensenkind, dat Gij naar hem omziet? – Psalm 8:3-4. Wanneer we nadenken over de wereld om ons heen, wanneer we lezen wat wetenschappers schrijven, is het cruciaal dat we dit benaderen met de kennis dat God achter dit alles staat. Want in Hem leven wij, bewegen wij ons en zijn wij – Handelingen 17:28, en niets wat de wetenschap kan waarnemen zal dat veranderen.

Wetenschap zou als een detective moeten zijn, die Gods vingerafdrukken in het heelal onthult, niet iemand die vastbesloten is Zijn zeer reële aanwezigheid in diskrediet te brengen.

Veel wetenschappers geloven in God

Kijkend in het verleden waren veel wetenschappers mannen die geloofden in de God van de Bijbel. Isaac Newton, Francis Bacon, Nicolaas Copernicus en velen anderen geloofden in de Bijbel en spraken openlijk over dit geloof naar anderen toe.

In modernere tijden zijn er veel mannen en vrouwen in de wetenschap die geloven in de God van de Bijbel. Alleen omdat iemand in de wetenschap werkt, betekent dat niet dat diegene geen leven van geloof kan hebben.

Velen hebben wetenschappelijke ontdekkingen toegeëigend om boodschappen te promoten die tegen het christelijk geloof en onderwijs ingaan.

We moeten onthouden dat wanneer er een reeks feiten is, er meestal verschillende verklaringen zijn die hun aanwezigheid kunnen verklaren. Schepping en evolutie onderzoeken dezelfde feiten van de natuur, maar vanaf een ander perspectief of vooroordeel, en komen daardoor tot zeer verschillende conclusies. Misschien is het een beetje zoals een Sherlock Holmes-verhaal, waarin dokter Watson routinematig de feiten neemt en een onnauwkeurige verklaring geeft, terwijl de detective dezelfde informatie neemt en de juiste verklaring geeft.

Wetenschap en geneeskunde

Het is niet tegen de Schrift om te onderzoeken hoe dingen werken in ons heelal, zolang we dat doen binnen een Bijbels kader en met het begrip dat er een Scheppende God is die alles ordent.

Moderne geneeskunde is een toepassing van vele verschillende vakgebieden, waaronder anatomie, microanatomie, genetica en biochemie. Het doel is in dit geval het menselijk lichaam zo goed mogelijk te observeren en vervolgens de dingen die fout gaan te herstellen. Artsen kunnen wetenschappers zijn, maar de meesten passen eenvoudigweg kennis toe die hun via hun opleiding is doorgegeven.

Observatie is waar het begint. Laten we diabetes als voorbeeld nemen. Aretaeus van Cappadocië in de tweede eeuw na Christus was de eerste die een volledige beschrijving van diabetes gaf en gaf daadwerkelijk de ziekte de naam diabetes. Het probleem was dat hoewel hij mensen met deze ziekte kon diagnosticeren, hij geen behandeling had om zijn patiënten te helpen. Observatie had hem slechts zo ver gebracht.

In de loop van de tijd werd verder werk verricht dat aantoonde dat het probleem in de alvleesklier lag en dat er iets specifiek mis was met de eilandjes van Langerhans. Zelfs in het begin van de 1900s was er geen geneesmiddel voor Diabetes Mellitus en de enige oplossing die artsen konden bieden was een extreem laag-glycemisch dieet met strikte caloriebeperkingen—probeerden patiënten op 500 of 600 calorieën per dag te houden. Zoals te verwachten was dit geen ideale behandeling.

Het was pas in de jaren 1920 dat een paar onderzoekers in Canada een manier ontdekten om insuline uit honden te extraheren en het toe te dienen aan een 14-jarige die stierf aan diabetes. Het extract redde zijn leven en begon een nieuw tijdperk voor mensen met diabetes.

Zo werken de dingen. We beginnen met het observeren van een ziekte en verschillende medicijnen die er effectief voor lijken te zijn, en in de loop van de tijd en door zorgvuldig testen kunnen wij beoordelen welke behandelingen het meest effectief zijn voor die aandoening.

Studies waarin de helft van de deelnemers met een ziekte een medicijn of behandeling krijgt en de andere helft een placebo (een pil zonder medische werkzaamheid) blijven de meest effectieve manier om te bepalen of iets echt werkt.

Waarom behandelingen bestudeerd moeten worden

Er is een echte neiging om te geloven dat de dingen die men geleerd heeft effectief zijn. We weten dat George Washington stierf aan longontsteking. Zijn dokters hebben waarschijnlijk zijn kansen op herstel geschaad door hem vier keer te laten aftappen, in totaal bijna 40 procent van zijn bloedvolume. Ze zouden hem waarschijnlijk een vijfde keer hebben laten aftappen, maar men dacht niet dat hij sterk genoeg was om de ingreep te overleven.

Artsen lieten patiënten bloedden omdat ze geloofden dat er toxische ophopingen in de bloedbaan waren die eruit moesten. De meeste mensen die na het bloed laten daten stierven zouden waarschijnlijk toch gestorven zijn, maar bloed laten bij mensen die erg ziek zijn helpt zeker niet bij hun herstel.

Misschien wilden de artsen gewoon iets doen. Patiënten verwachtten bloedonttrekking en dus voldeden zij aan die verwachtingen, hoewel het de patiënten schaadde.

Ervaring is wat je dezelfde fouten met veel meer vertrouwen laat maken.

Wat een goede studie maakt

Goede studies hebben veel patiënten, een controlegroep (die óf een inactieve pil krijgt, een placebo, óf de huidige beste behandeling voor die ziekte), en een testgroep die de nieuwe behandeling krijgt. Het is ook belangrijk dat de controlegroep en de testgroep zo nauw mogelijk op elkaar worden afgestemd. Ten slotte is de omvang van de groepen in de studie van cruciaal belang voor de conclusies. Als er slechts tien of twintig patiënten in de studie zijn, is dat niet groot genoeg om echt uit te zoeken of iets werkt of niet.

Voor veel aandoeningen is er iets dat het placebogeffect wordt genoemd. Dit placebogeffect treedt op wanneer mensen van een ziekte beter worden hoewel zij niets krijgen dat effectief zou moeten zijn voor de aandoening. Interessant genoeg krijgen veel mensen in studies bijwerkingen van de niet-werkzame pillen. Als 20 procent van de mensen die de placebo krijgen beter worden en 45 procent van de mensen die de behandeling krijgen beter worden, zou dat aangeven dat de behandeling effectief is. Als het verschil minimaal is—zeg 20 procent van de placebogroep en 23 procent van de behandelingsgroep verbetert—dan is de behandeling niet effectief.

Problemen

Het grootste probleem met veel behandelingen is dat ze simpelweg niet worden bestudeerd. Vitaminesupplementen en kruidenmengsels kunnen werken, maar vele daarvan zijn nooit daadwerkelijk in een proef vergeleken met een controlegroep bestudeerd. De meeste informatie is anekdotisch. Het feit dat iemands grootmoeder of oom baat had bij iets is mogelijk een aanwijzing dat het effectief is, maar het vertelt ons niet hoe effectief die behandeling is of wat de ideale dosering is.

Een ander probleem is wanneer studies simpelweg niet genoeg deelnemers hebben om echt nauwkeurige informatie te geven. Veel studies nemen slechts tien of twintig patiënten op. Dat is gewoon niet genoeg om te identificeren hoe goed een behandeling werkt of welke bijwerkingen te verwachten zijn. Om een geneesmiddel door de FDA te laten goedkeuren, wordt het doorgaans bestudeerd bij tussen de 1.000 en 3.000 patiënten met de ziekte.

Een laatste probleem met studies is wanneer zij aantonen dat een medicijn effectief is, maar het effect niet klinisch significant is. Als voorbeeld werd onlangs een nieuw injecteerbaar medicijn voor dementie (aducanumab) goedgekeurd door de FDA. Het is zeer duur, en het voordeel leek klein. Patiënten die het kregen beantwoordden gemiddeld 1,5 vraag meer correct op een mentale statusvragenlijst van 85 vragen na 18 maanden vergeleken met de controlegroep.

Men kan terecht betwijfelen of de getoonde voordelen van dit medicijn de kosten van 50.000 dollar per jaar waard zijn. Meer nog, hoeveel betekenisvolle verbetering in iemands dagelijkse activiteiten zou het gebruik van zo'n medicijn opleveren? Het lijkt onwaarschijnlijk dat het veel verschil zou maken.

Het is jammer, maar farmaceutische bedrijven zullen altijd proberen hun medicijn als het beste te laten lijken, zelfs als de studies geen significante meerwaarde tonen ten opzichte van bestaande, goedkopere opties.

Conclusie

Christenen staan tegenover een wereld die hen of hun geloof niet liefheeft. Velen zouden proberen de wetenschap te gebruiken om hen te dwingen hun geloof op te geven. Ik hoop dat dit er niet toe leidt dat wij de wetenschappelijke methode opgeven of het proberen te begrijpen van de wetten achter het universum dat God heeft geschapen.

De wetenschappelijke methode is geldig, zelfs als velen die haar gebruiken atheïsten of agnostici zijn. Als een behandeling werkt, moet zij observeerbaar, toetsbaar en herhaalbaar zijn.

Zelfs wanneer wij haar benaderen, hebben wij een basisbegrip van het heelal dat atheïsten niet hebben. Te weten dat er een Scheppende God is die ons liefheeft maakt een groot verschil bij het interpreteren van de resultaten van alle verschillende waarnemingen die worden gedaan op het gebied van geneeskunde en andere vakgebieden.

Degenen die God niet kennen zijn geneigd altijd lerend te zijn en nooit tot de kennis der waarheid te komen – 2 Timoteüs 3:7. Aan de andere kant, als wij beginnen met een Bijbels begrip, kunnen wij wetenschap gebruiken als een hulpmiddel om de schepping die Hij rondom ons geplaatst heeft te begrijpen.

Greetings of brotherly love to one and all. The year 2022 is almost gone. A lot has happened. Another year of devastating storms, floods, fires, earthquakes, wars, and rumors of wars. America has gone through another season of political elections, causing the conservatives and liberals to become even more polarized into opposing parties.

Recently, I have been reflecting on the current status of life as a committed Bible-believing Christian in our world today. Sure, there are certain places in our world where Christians live in constant threat of imprisonment or death simply because they are trying to live according to God’s Word. However, the world, seems to be moving towards an increasingly negative perspective of God’s people. In an increasingly developing trend, there is a surprising rise of hostility towards the committed believer.

What is happening? I have had numerous conversations with various believers from around the country who seem to have a growing alarm about the current victorious march of evil over good, of liberal agendas over a conservative lifestyle, and the list goes on. Current skyrocketing inflation, the potential of unprecedented heating costs for many, the rumors of rising interest rates, and the ongoing shortage of goods all tend to cause a person to be jolted out of a sense of normality.

For us as Christians, let us always keep our focus fixed on the God of heaven. This is the God that Paul declared on Mars Hill—God that made the world and all things therein, seeing that he is Lord of heaven and earth, dwelleth not in temples made with hands; Neither is worshipped with men’s hands, as though he needed any thing, seeing he giveth to all life, and breath, and all things; –Acts 17:24-25.

Let’s stop focusing on the fact that evil seems to be prevailing and increasing around us and then concluding that somehow Satan has the upper hand right now. Rather, let us be reminded about what God’s Word says. But evil men and seducers shall wax worse and worse, deceiving, and being deceived. But continue thou in the things which thou hast learned and hast been assured of, knowing of whom thou hast learned them; And that from a child thou hast known the holy scriptures, which are able to make thee wise unto salvation through faith which is in Christ Jesus. All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness: That the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works –2 Timothy 3:13-17.

Let us keep our eyes fixed on Jesus …the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God –Hebrews 12:2. Instead of believing Satan’s lie that he is somehow winning the battle for Truth right now, let’s remember that the Bible reveals that Satan can do nothing without God allowing him a temporary free rein. It seemed to those looking on that Satan had the complete upper hand when Jesus was crucified and buried. Surprise, surprise! Satan had unwittingly allowed God to use him to accomplish everything that had been prophesied throughout the Scriptures. It is the same today… God will again allow Satan whatever free rein is necessary to bring to fulfillment all that the Bible has foretold will come to pass regarding the end of time.

In this issue of the magazine, we have once more endeavored to bring you information in the articles that is both helpful and relevant to our time in history. Brother Leonard Martin, a bishop in one of our churches has shared an exhortation on spiritual gifts in the church with a number of clear, practical observations for us today. The article that we have chosen to share from “Bible Helps” in this issue is one of the best discourses on the subject of “faith and works” that I have ever read. The writer even delves, with biblical simplicity and clarity, into the controversial subjects of divine election and predestination. Finally, we have The Foolishness of Preaching an evaluation regarding the basis of churches using “the altar call”—is it founded in the Scriptures and the history of the church or is it a method that the church has borrowed from the world in more recent years?!

All of this is sure to stir thoughts and discussion—which is our goal with these types of articles. Please feel free to respond via email or regular mail with your thoughts of caution or encouragement. This is helpful for us and our writers. When you write, we also ask that you mention yes or no if we can use your questions or comments in our magazine. We have had various requests to establish a section in our magazine dedicated to hearing from our readers.

One final thought… over the years our readers have, at times, shared with us ways that they think we could improve our magazine for the good of all who read it and to present a more clear gospel message. We welcome this to continue.

May God richly bless each of you,

Curvin L. Wenger

भाईचारे के प्रेम की शुभकामनाएँ आप सभी को। वर्ष 2022 लगभग समाप्त हो रहा है। बहुत कुछ हुआ है। विनाशकारी तूफान, बाढ़, आग, भूकंप, युद्ध और युद्ध की अफ़वाहों का एक और वर्ष। अमेरिका ने राजनीतिक चुनावों का एक और दौर देखा, जिससे रुढ़िवादी और उदारवादी और भी अधिक ध्रुवीकृत होकर विरोधी दलों में बँट गए।

हाल ही में, मैं आज की दुनिया में एक प्रतिबद्ध बाइबिल-विश्वास रखने वाले ईसाई के रूप में जीवन की वर्तमान स्थिति पर विचार कर रहा था। निश्चित रूप से, हमारी दुनिया के कुछ स्थान ऐसे हैं जहाँ ईसाइयों को केवल इसलिए निरंतर कारावास या मृत्यु के खतरे में रहना पड़ता है क्योंकि वे ईश्वर के वचन के अनुसार जीने का प्रयास कर रहे हैं। फिर भी, ऐसा लगता है कि दुनिया ईश्वर के लोगों के प्रति एक बढ़ती नकारात्मक दृष्टि की ओर बढ़ रही है। एक विकसित होते हुए रुझान में, प्रतिबद्ध श्रद्धालु के प्रति शत्रुता में आश्चर्यजनक वृद्धि देखी जा रही है।

क्या हो रहा है? मैंने देश भर के विभिन्न विश्वासियों से कई बातचीत की हैं जो ऐसा प्रतीत होता है कि वे बुराई के अच्छाई पर वर्तमान विजयपूर्ण मार्च, रुढ़िवादी जीवनशैली पर उदार एजेंडों की बढ़त, और इसी तरह की बातों के बारे में बढ़ती चिंता व्यक्त करते हैं। वर्तमान आसमान छूती महंगाई, कई लोगों के लिए अभूतपूर्व हीटिंग लागत की संभावनाएँ, बढ़ती ब्याज दरों की अफ़वाहें, और सामानों की जारी कमी — ये सभी किसी व्यक्ति को स्वाभाविक स्थिति से झटके में बाहर कर देती हैं।

हम ईसाइयों के रूप में हमेशा अपना ध्यान स्वर्ग के परमेश्वर पर बनाए रखें। यह वही परमेश्वर है जिसे पौलुस ने मार्स हिल पर घोषित किया—यह परमेश्वर जिसने संसार और उसमें सब वस्तुओं को बनाया; क्योंकि वही स्वर्ग और पृथ्वी का प्रभु है; वह मनुष्यों द्वारा बने मन्दिरों में न रहता; न ही मनुष्यों के हाथों से पूजा किया जाता है, मानो उसे किन्हीं चीजों की आवश्यकता हो; क्योंकि वह ही सबको जीवन और श्वास और सब वस्तुएँ देता है। – प्रेरितों के काम 17:24-25।

आइए हम इस तथ्य पर ध्यान केंद्रित करना बंद करें कि बुराई हमारे चारों ओर बढ़ती और हावी होती दिखती है और फिर यह निष्कर्ष निकाल लें कि किसी तरह शैतान के पास अभी बढ़त है। बल्कि, आइए हम परमेश्वर के वचन को याद रखें। पर बुरे मनुष्य और लोलुप और अधिक-बढ़ते होंगे, भ्रामक और भ्रामित होते रहेंगे। पर तू उन बातों में ठहर, जिनको तूने सीखा है और जिनमें तू आश्वस्त हुआ है, और जान ले कि तूने किससे सीखा है; और बालक अवस्था से ही तू पवित्र शास्त्रों को जानता आया है, जो विश्वास में जो मसीह यीशु में है उससे तुझे उद्धार के लिये बुद्धिमान कर सकती हैं। समस्त शास्त्र परमेश्वर की प्रेरणा से दी गई है, और नीति के लिये, प्रेरणा के लिये, सुधार के लिये, धर्म में परिपाठ्य शिक्षा के लिये लाभकारी है; ताकि परमेश्वर का मनुष्य सम्पूर्ण रूप से सिद्ध हो, सब अच्छे कार्यों के लिये कारगर ढंग से सुसज्जित हो। – 2 तिमोथियुस 3:13-17।

आइए हम अपनी आँखें यीशु पर टिकाएँ —जो हमारे विश्वास के आरम्भकर्ता और पूर्णकर्त्ता हैं; जिन्होंने अपने सामने रखी हुई हुई आनन्द के लिये क्रूस को सहन किया, उस अपमान को तिरस्कृत करके, और परमेश्वर के सिंहासन के दाएँ बैठे हैं। – इब्रानियों 12:2। शैतान के उस झूठ पर विश्वास करने के बजाय कि वह किसी तरह आकर सत्य के लिये अभी जंग जीत रहा है, याद रखें कि बाइबिल बताती है कि शैतान कुछ भी नहीं कर सकता जब तक परमेश्वर उसे अस्थायी स्वतंत्रता देने की अनुमति न दे। जब यीशु को क्रूस पर चढ़ाया गया और दफन किया गया तब देखने वालों को ऐसा लगा कि शैतान का पूरा वर्चस्व था। आश्चर्य, आश्चर्य! शैतान ने अनजाने में परमेश्वर को उन्हीं सब बातों की पूर्ति के लिये उपयोग करने की अनुमति दे दी जो शास्त्रों में भविष्यवाणी की गई थीं। आज भी यही है… परमेश्वर फिर शैतान को वह स्वतंत्रता देगा जितनी आवश्यक होगी ताकि वे सब बातें जो बाइबिल ने अंतिम समय के विषय में कहा हैं, पूर्ण हो सकें।

इस अंक में, हमने फिर से कोशिश की है कि आपको ऐसे लेखों में जानकारी प्रस्तुत करें जो हमारे इतिहास के समय के लिये सहायक और प्रासंगिक दोनों हों। हमारे चर्चों में से एक के बिशप ब्रदर लियोनार्ड मार्टिन ने चर्च में आध्यात्मिक दानों पर एक उपदेश साझा किया है जिसमें हमारे लिये आज कई स्पष्ट, व्यावहारिक टिप्पणियाँ हैं। इस अंक में हमने “बाइबिल हेल्प्स” से जो लेख चुना है वह “विश्वास और कर्म” के विषय पर मैंने अब तक पढ़ी सबसे अच्छी व्याख्याओं में से एक है। लेखक ने दिव्य चुनाव और पूर्वनिर्धारण के विवादास्पद विषयों में भी बाइबिल की सरलता और स्पष्टता के साथ गोता लगाया है। अंत में, हमारे पास है "The Foolishness of Preaching"—एक मूल्यांकन कि चर्चों द्वारा "ऑल्टर कॉल" के प्रयोग की आधारशिला क्या है—क्या यह शास्त्रों और चर्च के इतिहास में आधारित है या क्या यह अधिक हाल के वर्षों में चर्च द्वारा दुनिया से उधार ली गई एक विधि है?!

इन सब से निश्चित ही विचार और चर्चा उठेंगी—यही हमारे इन प्रकार के लेखों का उद्देश्य है। कृपया ईमेल या सामान्य पत्र के माध्यम से अपने सावधानी या उत्साह के विचार साझा करने के लिये स्वतंत्र महसूस करें। यह हमारे तथा हमारे लेखकों के लिये सहायक है। जब आप लिखें, तो हम यह भी अनुरोध करते हैं कि आप उल्लेख करें कि क्या हम आपके प्रश्नों या टिप्पणियों का उपयोग अपनी पत्रिका में कर सकते हैं या नहीं। हमारे पास पाठकों से सुनने के लिये पत्रिका में एक अनुभाग स्थापित करने के विभिन्न अनुरोध आए हैं।

एक अंतिम विचार… वर्षों के दौरान हमारे पाठकों ने कभी-कभी हमसे ऐसे तरीके साझा किए हैं जिनसे उन्हें लगता है कि हम अपनी पत्रिका को सभी पाठकों के हित के लिये और भी बेहतर बना सकते हैं और एक अधिक स्पष्ट सुसमाचार संदेश प्रस्तुत कर सकते हैं। हम इसके जारी रहने का स्वागत करते हैं।

परमेश्वर आपमें से प्रत्येक को समृद्धि से आशीर्वाद दे,

Curvin L. Wenger

This hymn is generally thought to be one of the most loved hymns written during the latter part of the 19th century. The writing of this thoughtful and beautifully constructed text is even more amazing when we consider that its author was one who was almost completely blind and who describes the writing of this hymn as the “fruit of much mental suffering,” and “the quickest bit of work I ever did in my life.”

Born in Glasgow, Scotland, March 27, 1842, George Matheson had only partial vision as a boy, and, after entering Glasgow University, his eyesight continued to fail rapidly. Except for “moments of shadowy eyesight”, he was totally blind by the age of 18. This affliction of blindness seemed to be a tragedy since he was an eager and avid scholar, yet it caused him to trust in the Lord, and it strengthened his walk with God.

He entered the university at the early age of 15 and graduated with high honors in 1861 at the age of 19. He was a brilliant scholar, even spending four more years after graduation in more theological studies, all the while remaining single. After his graduation he became entirely dependent on others, relying much upon his two sisters, who were so dedicated that they learned Latin, Greek, and Hebrew since they thought it might aid him in his theological studies. One of them continued to be his faithful co-worker and helper throughout his life, assisting in his calling of being a pastor and other ministerial duties.

After completing his theological course, he became assistant pastor to the renowned Dr. Macduff, in whose church of thousands of members he had been brought up. Soon, however, he was chosen minister of the Church of Scotland in the seaport summer resort of Innellan. Here he stayed for eighteen years. Many families came to spend the summer there chiefly to be inspired by his preaching ministry.

Whenever he preached, the open Bible was before him as he stood in the pulpit, and to the congregation, he seemed to be reading from it. During the messages, his eyes looked straight at the congregation, and many went away with no clue that they just listened to a blind preacher. It was during this time that he made a practice of memorizing his sermons, as well as the passages of Scripture he used in his messages. His memory was so sharp that if someone read one of his prepared sermons to him twice, or whatever else he wanted to memorize, he could from then on repeat it perfectly. One Sunday, however, after doing this for 12 years, when in the middle of a powerful sermon his memory completely collapsed, and the topic on which he was preaching vanished from his mind. He sat down and commenced to request a psalm to be sung, and, after the song, with perfect calmness told the audience what had happened. With this done, he stood to his feet, gave out a new text, and preached an impromptu sermon of great power. After that experience George wrote little of his sermons, and finally prepared only an outline from which to preach.

Dr. Matheson’s final pastorate was taken up in 1886 at the age of 44 where he became pastor of the large St. Bernard’s Parish Church in Edinburgh, where his eloquent preaching consistently attracted large throngs of people to the services. Here he remained for 13 years, his church growing from 1,494 members to 1,703 in the first 5 years. He continued faithfully preaching the gospel and became well known as one of Scotland’s outstanding preachers and pastors and was greatly esteemed in Edinburgh where he resided.

Many speculations have been made regarding the cause of the mental distress which prompted the author to write this text. A very popular account, although never verified, is that this text was a result of the severe trial Matheson faced after his soon-to-be bride left him just before their marriage when she learned of his impending total blindness. Although this story cannot be documented, there are many significant hints in this hymn reflecting a saddened heart, such as the “flickering torch” and the “borrowed ray” in the second verse, the tracing of the “rainbow through the rain” in the third stanza, as well as the “cross” in the last verse.

Fortunately, Dr. Matheson did relate an account of his writing of this hymn:

“My hymn was composed in the manse of Innellan on the evening of June 6, 1882. I was at that time alone. It was the day of my sister’s wedding, and the rest of the family were staying overnight in Glasgow. Something happened to me, which was known only to myself, and which caused me the most severe mental suffering. The hymn was the fruit of that suffering and was the quickest bit of work I ever did in my life. A genuine inspiration, I had the impression rather of having it dictated to me by some inward voice than of working it out myself. I am quite sure that the whole work was completed in five minutes and equally sure it never received at my hands any retouching or correction. I have no natural gift of rhythm. All the other verses I have ever written are manufactured articles; this came like a dayspring from on high. I have never been able to gain once more the same fervor in verse.”

The hymn first appeared in the Church of Scotland monthly magazine, Life and Work, in January 1883. The tune was composed one year later by a prominent Scotch organist of his day, Albert L. Peace, who was asked to write a tune especially for Matheson’s text.

Peace’s own account of the writing of this fine tune is as follows, “After reading it over carefully, I wrote the music straight off, and may say that the ink of the first note was hardly dry when I had finished the tune.” The origin or the tune name, St. Margaret, is unknown except that it is a name much revered in Scotland, and certainly because of the beloved Queen Margaret of Scotland.

The later years of Matheson’s life from the age of 57 to his death at age 64 were spent in writing some of the finest devotional writings in the English tongue, including Moments on the Mount, Voice of the Spirit, and Rests by the River. Although this is his only hymn found in most hymnals, he did write a few other fine hymns, including “Make Me A Captive Lord”, and “Then I Shall Be Free.”

The four key words of “O Love, That Wilt Not Let Me Go” are: love, light, joy, and cross. These words have been described as the complete satisfaction for any believer whose life is totally surrendered to the will of God. It could take the rest of one’s life to completely discover the personal significance of these four expressions.

Composer       -Albert L. Peace, 1844 – 1912

Denna hymn anses allmänt vara en av de mest älskade hymnerna som skrevs under senare delen av 19th seklet. Att den eftertänksamma och vackert uppbyggda texten är författad av någon som nästan helt var blind och som beskriver tillkomsten av hymnen som "frukten av stor mental ångest" och "det snabbaste arbete jag någonsin gjort i mitt liv" är ännu mer anmärkningsvärt.

George Matheson föddes i Glasgow, Skottland, den 27 mars 1842. Som pojke hade han endast partiell syn, och efter att ha börjat vid Glasgow University försämrades hans syn snabbt. Bortsett från "stunder av skuggig syn" var han helt blind vid 18 års ålder. Denna blindhet tycktes vara en tragedi eftersom han var en ivrig och flitig student, men den fick honom att sätta sin tillit till Herren och stärkte hans vandring med Gud.

Han började vid universitetet vid tidig ålder, 15 år, och tog examen med höga utmärkelser 1861 vid 19 års ålder. Han var en briljant lärd och tillbringade ytterligare fyra år efter examen med teologiska studier, samtidigt som han förblev ogift. Efter examen blev han helt beroende av andra och förlitade sig mycket på sina två systrar, som var så hängivna att de lärde sig latin, grekiska och hebreiska eftersom de trodde att det kunde hjälpa honom i hans teologiska studier. En av dem fortsatte att vara hans trogna medarbetare och hjälp genom hela hans liv och bistod i hans kallelse som pastor och i andra tjänster.

Efter att ha avslutat sina teologistudier blev han assistentpastor åt den berömde Dr. Macduff, i den kyrka med tusentals medlemmar där han hade vuxit upp. Snart valdes han dock till minister i Church of Scotland i badorten Innellan. Där stannade han i arton år. Många familjer kom dit för att tillbringa sommaren, i första hand för att inspireras av hans predikoverksamhet.

När han predikade låg den öppna Bibeln framför honom när han stod i predikstolen, och för församlingen tycktes han läsa ur den. Under budskapen såg hans ögon rakt mot församlingen, och många lämnade utan en aning om att de just hade lyssnat till en blind predikant. Det var under denna tid han skaffade sig vanan att memorera sina predikningar liksom de skriftställen han använde. Hans minne var så skarpt att om någon läste en av hans färdigskrivna predikningar för honom två gånger, eller vad det nu var han ville memorera, kunde han därifrån upprepa den perfekt. En söndag, dock, efter att ha gjort detta i 12 år, kollapsade hans minne fullständigt mitt i en kraftfull predikan och ämnet han predikade om försvann ur hans sinne. Han satte sig ner och bad om att en psalm skulle sjungas, och efter sången berättade han med fullständig lugn vad som hade hänt. Därefter reste han sig, gav ut en ny text och predikade en improviserad predikan med stor kraft. Efter den erfarenheten skrev George lite av sina predikningar och förberedde slutligen endast en disposition att predika efter.

Dr. Mathesons sista pastorat började 1886 vid 44 års ålder då han blev pastor i den stora St. Bernard’s Parish Church i Edinburgh, där hans vältaliga predikningar konsekvent drog stora folkskaror till gudstjänsterna. Här stannade han i 13 år; hans kyrka växte från 1 494 medlemmar till 1 703 under de första fem åren. Han fortsatte troget att predika evangeliet och blev känd som en av Skottlands framstående predikanter och pastorer och var högt aktad i Edinburgh där han bodde.

Många spekulationer har framförts angående orsaken till den mentala prövning som föranledde författaren att skriva denna text. En mycket populär berättelse, även om den aldrig verifierats, är att texten var ett resultat av den svåra prövning Matheson mötte efter att hans blivande brud lämnade honom strax före deras äktenskap när hon fick kännedom om hans förestående totala blindhet. Även om denna berättelse inte kan dokumenteras finns det många betydelsefulla antydningar i hymnen som speglar ett sorgset hjärta, såsom den "fladdrande facklan" och den "lånade strålen" i andra versen, uppritandet av "regnbågen genom regnet" i tredje strofen, liksom "korset" i sista versen.

Lyckligtvis beskrev Dr. Matheson själv hur han skrev denna hymn:

"Min hymn komponerades i prästgården i Innellan på kvällen den 6 juni 1882. Jag var då ensam. Det var min systers bröllopsdag och resten av familjen stannade över natten i Glasgow. Något hände mig, vilket endast var känt för mig själv, och vilket orsakade mig den svåraste mentala lidanden. Hymnen var frukten av det lidandet och var det snabbaste arbete jag någonsin gjort i mitt liv. En genuin inspiration, jag hade intrycket snarare av att den diktades åt mig av någon inre röst än att jag arbetade fram den själv. Jag är helt säker på att hela verket färdigställdes på fem minuter och lika säker på att det aldrig mottog någon omarbetning eller korrigering av mig. Jag har ingen naturlig gåva för rytm. Alla andra verser jag någonsin skrivit är tillverkade artiklar; denna kom som en daggry från höjden. Jag har aldrig kunnat återfå samma glöd i vers."

Hymnen publicerades första gången i Church of Scotland:s månadstidning Life and Work i januari 1883. Melodin komponerades ett år senare av en framstående skotsk organist i hans tid, Albert L. Peace, som blev ombedd att skriva en melodi särskilt för Mathesons text.

Peaces egen redogörelse för tillkomsten av denna fina melodi lyder: "Efter att noggrant ha läst igenom den skrev jag musiken direkt, och man kan säga att bläcket på den första noten knappt hade torkat när jag hade färdigställt melodin." Ursprunget till melodinamnet, St. Margaret, är okänt förutom att det är ett namn som är högt vördat i Skottland, och säkert på grund av den älskade drottning Margaret av Skottland.

De senare åren av Mathesons liv, från 57 års ålder till hans död vid 64, tillbringades med att skriva några av de finaste fromma skrifterna på engelska, inklusive Stunder på berget (Moments on the Mount), Andens röst (Voice of the Spirit) och Vila vid floden (Rests by the River). Även om detta är hans enda hymn som återfinns i de flesta psalmböcker, skrev han några andra fina hymner, inklusive "Make Me A Captive Lord" och "Then I Shall Be Free."

Huvudorden i "O Love, That Wilt Not Let Me Go" är: kärlek, ljus, glädje och kors. Dessa ord har beskrivits som den fullständiga tillfredsställelsen för varje troende vars liv är helt överlämnat åt Guds vilja. Det kan ta resten av ens liv att helt upptäcka den personliga betydelsen av dessa fyra uttryck.

101 Hymn Stories

Composer       -Albert L. Peace, 1844 – 1912

Jehoshaphat was in trouble. He had just heard the news that a great multitude was coming to fight against him. At that moment he did what all of us naturally do when a multitude of problems come against us. He was afraid. How well I know the feeling of fear, the dread that grips my heart at times. Sometimes it’s the big things, like being misunderstood and misused, or the fear and pain of sickness, or the death of a loved one. Sometimes it’s small things, like loneliness on a Sunday afternoon. This is not comfortable, God, and I’m afraid.

Jehoshaphat laid his fear aside, set himself to seek the Lord, and proclaimed a fast throughout all the land of Judah – verse 3. Even in this seemingly impossible situation of having thousands of men on their way to destroy him and his people, he fell before the Lord and acknowledged His perfect, omnipotent rule. And [he] said, O LORD God of our fathers, art not thou God in heaven? and rulest not thou over all the kingdoms of the heathen? and in thine hand is there not power and might, so that none is able to withstand thee? –verse 6.

The choice is mine. I wrestle with my own fearful thoughts, turning them over and over in my mind as if hoping to change the situation with my messy and fearful concoctions. Clinging to my fear gives me a feeling of being in control. But it is killing me from the inside out, even without the dreaded “what ifs” becoming reality. Finally, I let go and fall exhausted at my Lord’s feet, and my heart echoes the words of Jehoshaphat, the king of Judah.

In humble entreaty, Jehoshaphat acknowledges their weakness and need for God’s power. O our God, wilt thou not judge them? for we have no might against this great company that cometh against us; neither know we what to do: but our eyes are upon thee. –verse 12.

Yes, God, I am nothing in the grand scheme of things. I have no power, not even to be the fruitful worker in Your kingdom that I always dreamed of being. I can’t fight this battle.

Jehoshaphat realized that he alone, as one man, had no strength. He called all the people of Judah together, And all Judah stood before the LORD, with their little ones, their wives, and their children –verse 13. They knew the strength in unity. As they stood before the Lord, waiting for Him to speak, the Spirit of the Lord came down and God gave them the words of help and hope that they were desperate for.

…Be not afraid nor dismayed by reason of this great multitude; for the battle is not yours, but God’s –verse 15. Often I try to fight my battles inside of myself rather than making myself vulnerable to others. But, as soon as I invite others into my life and into my battles, I find the strength of God through His people. When we are confused and disillusioned, we need the people of God. When we all pray together, we will get an answer to our prayer for direction.

Jehoshaphat heard the next directive from God. Tomorrow go ye down against them … Ye shall not need to fight in this battle: set yourselves, stand ye still, and see the salvation of the LORD … fear not, nor be dismayed; to morrow go out against them: for the LORD will be with you –verses 16-17. These words comfort my heart. Often the easiest thing to do is try to fix things, to quickly come up with a remedy of some sort to get myself out of this dilemma, to try to convince myself that everything will be okay. But God tells my heart to sit still without fear and let Him do the fighting. This takes more spiritual muscle than all the action, all the doing, and all the worrying; plus, it accomplishes a lot more.

And Jehoshaphat bowed his head with his face to the ground: and all Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem fell before the LORD, worshipping the LORD –verse 18. If I obey and trust instead of worry and sit still instead of jumping into the middle of things, then I will see God do miracles. No, not always in changing my circumstances or removing all the hard things, but He does a miracle in my own soul which changes my focus and attitude. And that causes me to worship because it’s a miracle which only the all-mighty, all-powerful God can do.

Do you think any of them slept that night? They knew a fearsome army was on its way to destroy them and yet… they had heard God speak. Just perhaps there was a joyful expectation in their hearts and an eager anticipation to see how God was going to win this battle. When I learn to practice trust in the little things and the big things that pile into my life, I will soon learn to have a heart of excited expectation, because I know He is going to do something! He is going to give me a way out. Even if the worst happens, He will show my heart the way of peace and He has promised to be with me through it all. And after all, the ultimate victory is already won, so what do all these infractions really have to do with my peace and joy? Nothing.

Morning dawned; it was the day God had told them to go out against these enemies. They arose with no delay. They all knew obedience was paramount in receiving God’s blessing that day. And as they went out of the city, Jehoshaphat exhorted them. And they rose early in the morning, …and as they went forth, Jehoshaphat stood and said, …Believe in the LORD your God, so shall ye be established; believe his prophets, so shall ye prosper. And… he appointed singers unto the LORD, and that should praise the beauty of holiness, as they went out before the army… – verses 21-20. He appointed singers to sing as they went, proclaiming to everyone and to the opposing army that they were on the Lord’s side.

I would have liked to see that huge army going out of the city, singing. They were facing a daunting task and one that would have made the strongest man tremble, but they were singing. And when they began to sing and to praise, the LORD set… [an ambush] against the children of Ammon, [and] Moab, …which were come against Judah; and they were smitten …every one helped to destroy another –verses 22-23.

The people of Judah went to their watch tower and in amazement saw that their enemies had destroyed each other, and they saw nothing but an army of dead bodies. When a fearsome battle is set in array against me, I can still make the decision to trust and sing. Singing is a deliberate act of worship; it reminds our own souls and the souls of everyone listening that the Lord, He is God. He is the One in complete charge of my circumstances, of my tiny world, and all its problems. Suddenly the enemies are dead. The circumstances may not have changed, but the battle is finished in my soul.

The army of Judah spent the next three days gathering the riches and spoils from the dead bodies of their enemies, collecting so much that they couldn’t carry it all away with them. Astonishing! But that is how it is every time. My spirit benefits from the hard things that I endure successfully. Each victory allows me to collect ‘spoils’ which will profit me for the rest of my life. My heart is full of blessing, of being cared for, and being carried by a Heavenly Father. The “armies of Moab and Ammon” have brought blessing instead of ruin.

They came again to their homes in Jerusalem with singing, and harps, and trumpets, overloaded with all their spoil. The fear of God fell on all the kingdoms of the land when they heard how God had fought this huge battle, then Jehoshaphat’s realm was quiet. Peace reigned.

The peace of knowing that all I really need is God and His working in my life is the ultimate peace. This broken world can bring all manner of pain, sickness, and disappointments, but God brings rest to the heart that was once so full of tumult and fear. There is rest ‘round about’ and all the ‘kingdoms of the land’ will be amazed and curious at the strength that is within us, because it is the strength that no one can match—the strength of our amazing God.

Иосафат оказался в беде. Он только что получил весть о том, что на него идёт большое множество войск, чтобы сразиться с ним. В тот момент он сделал то, что свойственно нам всем, когда на нас обрушивается множество проблем. Он испугался. Как хорошо я знаю это чувство страха, ужас, который порой охватывает моё сердце. Иногда это большие вещи — быть неправильно понятым и использованным, или страх и боль болезни, или смерть любимого человека. Иногда это мелочи, вроде одиночества в воскресный полдень. Это неуютно, Бог, и мне страшно.

Иосафат отложил свой страх, стал искать Господа и провозгласил пост по всей земле Иуды — стих 3. Даже в этой, казалось бы, безнадёжной ситуации, когда тысячи людей шли, чтобы уничтожить его и его народ, он преклонился пред Господом и признал Его совершенное, всемогущее владычество. И сказал: О Господь Бог наших отцов, не Ты ли Бог на небеси? разве Ты не властвуешь над всеми царствами язычников? и разве в руке Твоей нет силы и могущества, так что никто не в состоянии противиться Тебе? — стих 6.

Выбор за мной. Я борюсь со своими собственными пугающими мыслями, верчу их в голове, как будто надеясь изменить ситуацию своими неуклюжими и испуганными выдумками. Привязанность к страху даёт мне ощущение контроля. Но это убивает меня изнутри, даже если пугающие «а что если» не становятся реальностью. Наконец я отпускаю и падаю измождённый у ног моего Господа, и моё сердце откликается словами Иосафата, царя Иуды.

В смиренной просьбе Иосафат признаёт их слабость и необходимость силы Божьей. О Боже наш! не судишь ли Ты их? ибо у нас нет силы против этого великого множества, которое идёт против нас; и не знаем мы, что делать; но взоры наши на Тебе — стих 12.

Да, Бог, я ничто в общей картине. У меня нет силы, даже чтобы быть тем плодоносным тружеником в Твоём царстве, каким я всегда мечтал быть. Я не могу вести эту битву.

Иосафат понял, что он один, как один человек, бессилен. Он созвал всех жителей Иуды, и весь Иуда стал пред Господом, с малолетними своими, женами и детьми — стих 13. Они знали силу единства. Стоя пред Господом, в ожидании Его слова, сошёл Дух Господень, и Бог дал им слова помощи и надежды, в которых они так отчаянно нуждались.

…Не бойтесь и не ужасайтесь ради этого великого множества; ибо не ваша битва, а Божья — стих 15. Часто я пытаюсь вести свои битвы внутри себя, вместо того чтобы открыться другим. Но как только я приглашаю людей в свою жизнь и в свои сражения, я нахожу силу Божью через Его народ. Когда мы сбиты с толку и разочарованы, нам нужны люди Божьи. Когда мы все молимся вместе, мы получаем ответ на нашу молитву о направлении.

Иосафат услышал дальше повеление от Бога. Завтра сойдите против них … вам не нужно будет сражаться в этой битве: приготовьтесь, стойте и увидите спасение Господа … не бойтесь и не ужасайтесь; завтра идите против них, ибо Господь с вами — стихи 16–17. Эти слова утешают моё сердце. Часто проще всего попытаться всё починить, быстро подсобрать какое-то решение, чтобы выбраться из затруднения, убедить себя, что всё будет в порядке. Но Бог говорит моему сердцу спокойно сидеть без страха и позволить Ему вести борьбу. Для этого требуется больше духовной силы, чем для всех действий, всей суеты и всех тревог; при том это приносит гораздо больший результат.

И Иосафат поклонился лицом до земли: и весь Иуда и жители Иерусалима пали пред Господом, и поклонялись Господу — стих 18. Если я повину́сь и доверюсь вместо того, чтобы волноваться, и сижу спокойно вместо того, чтобы врываться в ситуацию, тогда увижу, как Бог творит чудеса. Нет, не всегда менять мои обстоятельства или устранять все трудности, но Он творит чудо в моей душе, что меняет мой фокус и отношение. И это ведёт меня к поклонению, потому что это чудо, которое способен сотворить только всемогущий Бог.

Думаете, кто‑то из них спал той ночью? Они знали, что на них идёт грозная армия, но… они слышали голос Бога. Возможно, в их сердцах поселилось радостное ожидание и нетерпеливое предвкушение увидеть, как Бог одержит победу. Когда я учусь упражняться в доверии к маленьким вещам и большим проблемам, которые наваливаются на мою жизнь, я скоро научаюсь иметь сердце, полное восторженного ожидания, потому что знаю, что Он что‑то совершит! Он даст мне выход. Даже если случится худшее, Он покажет моему сердцу путь мира и обещал быть со мной во всём этом. И в конце концов окончательная победа уже одержана, так что какое же отношение ко моему миру и радости имеют все эти напасти? Никакого.

Наступило утро; это был день, в который Бог сказал им выйти против врагов. Они поднялись без промедления. Все знали, что послушание — первостепенно для получения благословения Божьего в тот день. И выйдя из города, Иосафат ободрял их. «И встал он рано утром, …и когда они выступали, Иосафат стал и сказал: …верьте в Господа Бога вашего, и утвердитесь; верьте пророкам Его, и преуспеете. И… поставил певцов пред Господом, которые восхваляли красоту святости, когда выходили перед войском…" — стихи 21–20. Он назначил певцов, чтобы они шли впереди и пели, провозглашая всем и противостоящей армии, что они на стороне Господа.

Я бы очень хотела увидеть ту огромную армию, выходящую из города, поющую. Им предстояло грозное дело, которое заставило бы дрожать самых сильных людей, но они пели. И когда они начали петь и славить, Господь устроил … [засаду] против сынов Аммоновых и Моавии и против тех, которые пришли на Иуду; и побиты были они … каждый помог уничтожить другого — стихи 22–23.

Жители Иуды поднялись на дозорную башню и в изумлении увидели, что враги истребили друг друга, и никого не было, кроме множества трупов вражеской армии. Когда на меня нависла грозная битва, я всё равно могу принять решение доверять и петь. Пение — это намеренный акт поклонения; оно напоминает моей душе и душам слушающих, что Господь — Он Бог. Он Единственный, кто полностью управляет моими обстоятельствами, моим маленьким миром и всеми его проблемами. Вдруг враги мертвы. Обстоятельства могли и не измениться, но битва завершилась в моей душе.

Армия Иуды провела следующие три дня, собирая добычу и трофеи с тел своих врагов, собирая столько, что не могли всё унести. Поразительно! Но так бывает каждый раз. Мой дух выигрывает от трудностей, которые мне удаётся преодолеть. Каждая победа позволяет мне собрать «трофеи», которые принесут пользу на всю оставшуюся жизнь. Моё сердце полно благословения, заботы и поддержки Небесного Отца. «Армии Моава и Аммона» принесли благословение вместо гибели.

Они возвратились в свой дом в Иерусалиме с песнями, арфами и трубами, перегруженные добычей. Страх перед Богом пал на все царства земли, когда услышали, как Бог сражался в этой великой битве, и царство Иосафата сделалось спокойным. Воссиял мир.

Мир осознания того, что всё, что мне действительно нужно — это Бог и Его действие в моей жизни, — это высший мир. Этот сломленный мир может приносить всевозможную боль, болезни и разочарования, но Бог приносит отдых сердцу, которое было когда‑то полным смятения и страха. Есть отдых «около» меня, и все «царства земли» будут удивлены и заинтересованы той силой, которая в нас, потому что это сила, которой никто не может сравниться — сила нашего удивительного Бога.

Greetings of brotherly love to one and all. The year 2022 is almost gone. A lot has happened. Another year of devastating storms, floods, fires, earthquakes, wars, and rumors of wars. America has gone through another season of political elections, causing the conservatives and liberals to become even more polarized into opposing parties.

Recently, I have been reflecting on the current status of life as a committed Bible-believing Christian in our world today. Sure, there are certain places in our world where Christians live in constant threat of imprisonment or death simply because they are trying to live according to God’s Word. However, the world, seems to be moving towards an increasingly negative perspective of God’s people. In an increasingly developing trend, there is a surprising rise of hostility towards the committed believer.

What is happening? I have had numerous conversations with various believers from around the country who seem to have a growing alarm about the current victorious march of evil over good, of liberal agendas over a conservative lifestyle, and the list goes on. Current skyrocketing inflation, the potential of unprecedented heating costs for many, the rumors of rising interest rates, and the ongoing shortage of goods all tend to cause a person to be jolted out of a sense of normality.

For us as Christians, let us always keep our focus fixed on the God of heaven. This is the God that Paul declared on Mars Hill—God that made the world and all things therein, seeing that he is Lord of heaven and earth, dwelleth not in temples made with hands; Neither is worshipped with men’s hands, as though he needed any thing, seeing he giveth to all life, and breath, and all things; –Acts 17:24-25.

Let’s stop focusing on the fact that evil seems to be prevailing and increasing around us and then concluding that somehow Satan has the upper hand right now. Rather, let us be reminded about what God’s Word says. But evil men and seducers shall wax worse and worse, deceiving, and being deceived. But continue thou in the things which thou hast learned and hast been assured of, knowing of whom thou hast learned them; And that from a child thou hast known the holy scriptures, which are able to make thee wise unto salvation through faith which is in Christ Jesus. All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness: That the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works –2 Timothy 3:13-17.

Let us keep our eyes fixed on Jesus …the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God –Hebrews 12:2. Instead of believing Satan’s lie that he is somehow winning the battle for Truth right now, let’s remember that the Bible reveals that Satan can do nothing without God allowing him a temporary free rein. It seemed to those looking on that Satan had the complete upper hand when Jesus was crucified and buried. Surprise, surprise! Satan had unwittingly allowed God to use him to accomplish everything that had been prophesied throughout the Scriptures. It is the same today… God will again allow Satan whatever free rein is necessary to bring to fulfillment all that the Bible has foretold will come to pass regarding the end of time.

In this issue of the magazine, we have once more endeavored to bring you information in the articles that is both helpful and relevant to our time in history. Brother Leonard Martin, a bishop in one of our churches has shared an exhortation on spiritual gifts in the church with a number of clear, practical observations for us today. The article that we have chosen to share from “Bible Helps” in this issue is one of the best discourses on the subject of “faith and works” that I have ever read. The writer even delves, with biblical simplicity and clarity, into the controversial subjects of divine election and predestination. Finally, we have The Foolishness of Preaching an evaluation regarding the basis of churches using “the altar call”—is it founded in the Scriptures and the history of the church or is it a method that the church has borrowed from the world in more recent years?!

All of this is sure to stir thoughts and discussion—which is our goal with these types of articles. Please feel free to respond via email or regular mail with your thoughts of caution or encouragement. This is helpful for us and our writers. When you write, we also ask that you mention yes or no if we can use your questions or comments in our magazine. We have had various requests to establish a section in our magazine dedicated to hearing from our readers.

One final thought… over the years our readers have, at times, shared with us ways that they think we could improve our magazine for the good of all who read it and to present a more clear gospel message. We welcome this to continue.

May God richly bless each of you,

Curvin L. Wenger

愿弟兄般的爱向众人问安。2022年即将过去。这一年发生了许多事。又是一年毁灭性的风暴、洪水、火灾、地震、战争与战争的传闻。美国又经历了一季政治选举，使保守派和自由派更加两极分化，彼此对立。

最近，我一直在反思，作为当今世界中一名忠于圣经的基督徒，现今的处境如何。当然，在世界的某些地方，基督徒仅仅因为试图按照神的话语生活，就常常面临被囚禁或处死的威胁。然而，世界似乎日益对神的子民抱有负面看法。令人惊讶的是，针对虔诚信徒的敌意正呈增长趋势。

这是怎么回事？我与全国各地的许多信徒进行了大量对话，他们似乎愈发对恶胜过善、自由主义议程胜过保守生活方式等现象感到不安。目前飞涨的通货膨胀、许多人可能面临前所未有的取暖费用、利率上升的传闻以及持续的商品短缺，所有这些都容易把人从常态中震撼出来。

作为基督徒，我们应当时常把目光定睛在天上的神身上。这就是保罗在亚略巴古（马尔斯山）所宣告的那位神——造天地和其中万物的神既是天地的主，便不住人手所造的殿，也不需人手服事，好像缺少什么，乃是自己叫万人生命、气息、万物的——使徒行传 17:24-25。

不要再专注于邪恶似乎在我们周围得势并且日益增长，然后就得出撒但现在占上风的结论。倒不如让我们记住神的话所说的：只是那恶人和迷惑人的必越发恶劣、越发迷惑人，也被人迷惑；你却要持续在所学并确据的事上，知道你是从谁那里学的，并且从小就知道圣经，圣经能使你因信基督耶稣得着救恩的智慧。圣经都是神所默示的，于教导、督责、使人归正、教导人学义都是有益的，叫属神的人得以完全，预备行各样的善事—提摩太后书 3:13-17。

让我们把眼目定在耶稣身上——我们信心的创始成终者；为那摆在前面的喜乐，就轻看羞辱，忍受了十字架，现在坐在　神宝座的右边——希伯来书 12:2。不要相信撒但的谎言，认为他此刻在真理的争战中获胜；当记得圣经显明，若非神允准，撒但不能做什么。看的人好像认为当耶稣被钉十字架并埋葬时，撒但已完全得胜。出人意料的是，撒但无意中被神使用，以成就圣经中所预言的一切。今天也是如此……神仍要允许撒但在必要的范围内有暂时的自由，来成就圣经所预言末世将要发生的一切。

在本期杂志中，我们再次努力在诸篇文章中为你带来既有益又与我们当前时代相关的信息。列昂纳德·马丁弟兄—我们教会中的一位主教—在会中就属灵恩赐分享了一篇劝勉文，其中为我们今日提供了若干清晰且实用的观察。我们在本期选自“圣经助益”（Bible Helps）的一篇文章，是我所读过关于“信与行为”题目中最好的讲论之一。作者甚至以圣经的简单与清晰探讨了有争议的神圣拣选与预定论题目。最后，我们登载了《讲道的愚拙》（The Foolishness of Preaching）对教会使用“呼罪悔改上台祷告”（altar call）基础的评估——这是建立在圣经与教会历史之上，还是近年来教会从世俗借用的方法？

所有这些肯定会激起思想与讨论——这是我们刊登此类文章的目的。欢迎通过电子邮件或平信把你谨慎或鼓励的想法反馈给我们。这对我们和我们的作者都有帮助。当你来信时，我们也请你注明是否允许我们在杂志中使用你的问题或评论。我们曾有多方请求，建议在杂志中设立专栏以听取读者意见。

最后一则想法……多年来我们的读者有时会与我们分享他们认为可为杂志改进的方式，以便对所有读者更有益并更清楚地呈现福音信息。我们欢迎你们继续提出这些意见。

愿　神丰丰富富地赐福给你们每一位，

柯文·L·温格（Curvin L. Wenger）
