Yehoshafati alikuwa katika shida. Alikuwa amepata habari kwamba umati mkubwa ulikuwa unakuja kumwangamiza. Wakati huo alifanya kile tunachokifanya sote kwa kawaida tunapokabiliwa na umati wa matatizo. Alikuwa na hofu. Najua vizuri hisia za hofu, ile taharuki inayoshika moyo wangu kwa nyakati. Wakati mwingine ni mambo makubwa, kama kutokueleweka na kutumika vibaya, au hofu na maumivu ya ugonjwa, au kifo cha mpendwa. Wakati mwingine ni mambo madogo, kama upweke siku ya Jumapili mchana. Hili si jepesi, Mungu, na ninaogopa.

Yehoshafati aliweka hofu yake kando, akajitolea kumtafuta Bwana, na akatangaza sikukuu ya kufunga katika nchi yote ya Yuda – mstari wa 3. Hata katika hali isiyoonekana kuwa na matumaini ya kuwa maelfu ya watu walikuwa njiani kumwangamiza yeye na watu wake, aligonga magoti mbele za Bwana na kukiri utawala Wake kamili, wenye uwezo wote. Na [aka] sema, Ee BWANA Mungu wa baba zetu, huna wewe, si wewe Mungu mbinguni? Je, hunatawala juu ya falme zote za mataifa? Je, si kwa mkono wako kuna nguvu na uwezo, hata mtu hapaswi kukupinga? –mstari wa 6.

Uamuzi ni wangu. Ninapigana na mawazo yangu ya hofu, nikiwazungusha mfululizo akilini mwangu kana kwamba natumaini kubadilisha hali kwa mchanganyiko wangu mchafu wa hofu. Kushikilia hofu kunanipa hisia ya kuwa namdhibiti. Lakini inaniua ndani, hata bila yale “kama” yaukwera kuwa kweli. Hatimaye, ninaachilia na kuanguka nimechoka migongoni mwa Bwana wangu, na moyo wangu unanukuu maneno ya Yehoshafati, mfalme wa Yuda.

Kwa kuomba kwa unyenyekevu, Yehoshafati anakiri udhaifu wao na haja yao ya nguvu za Mungu. Ee Mungu wetu, je, hutaliwa hao? Kwa maana hatuna nguvu dhidi ya umati huu mkubwa unaokuja kwetu; wala hatujui tufanye nini: ila macho yetu yako juu yako. –mstari wa 12.

Ndio, Mungu, mimi sifai katika mpangilio mkubwa wa mambo. Sina nguvu, hata kuwa mfanyakazi mwenye tija katika ufalme Wako kama nilivyokuwa nikitamani kuwa. Siwezi kupigana vita hii.

Yehoshafati alitambua kwamba yeye pekee, kama mtu mmoja, hakuwa na nguvu. Aliwaita watu wote wa Yuda pamoja, Na wote wa Yuda walisimama mbele za BWANA, pamoja na wachanga wao, wake zao, na watoto wao –mstari wa 13. Walijua nguvu iliyokuwa katika umoja. Waliposimama mbele za Bwana, wakimsubiri aongee, Roho wa Bwana alishuka na Mungu akawapa maneno ya msaada na matumaini waliokuwa wakiyataka kwa woga.

...Msihofu wala msipate moyo kwa sababu ya umati huu mkubwa; kwa maana vita si vyenu, bali vya Mungu –mstari wa 15. Mara nyingi ninajaribu kupigania vita zangu ndani ya nafsi yangu badala ya kufanya mwenyewe kuwa mwoga mbele ya wengine. Lakini, mara tu ninapowakaribisha wengine katika maisha yangu na katika vita zangu, napatia nguvu za Mungu kupitia watu Wake. Tunapokuwa wenye mkanganyiko na kukatishwa tamaa, tunahitaji watu wa Mungu. Tunapokuwa tumsali pamoja, tutapokea jibu la sala yetu kuhusu mwanga na mwelekeo.

Yehoshafati alisikia maagizo mengine kutoka kwa Mungu. Kesho mnendeni nao ... Hamta hitaji kupigana katika vita hii: jisahihisheni, simameni mtulivu, mone wokovu wa BWANA ... msihofu wala msipate moyo; kesho nendeni dhidi yao: kwa maana BWANA atakuwa pamoja nanyi –mistari 16-17. Maneno haya yanatuliza moyo wangu. Mara nyingi jambo rahisi zaidi kufanya ni kujaribu kurekebisha mambo, kutafuta tiba ya haraka ya kuondoka katika shida hii, kujiaminisha kwamba kila kitu kitakuwa sawa. Lakini Mungu anasema moyo wangu usimame tulivu bila hofu na Aendelee kupigana. Hii inahitaji misuli ya kiroho zaidi kuliko vitendo vyote, matendo yote, na wasiwasi wote; na zaidi ya hayo, inaleta matokeo mengi zaidi.

Na Yehoshafati alijikubali mguu na uso zake ardhini: na wote wa Yuda na wakaaji wa Yerusalemu waligonga magoti mbele za BWANA, wakimwabudu BWANA –mstari wa 18. Kama nitatii na kuamini badala ya kuwa na wasiwasi na kukaa kimya badala ya kuingia katikati ya mambo, basi nitaona Mungu afanye mafundisho. Hapana, si kila wakati kubadilisha hali zangu au kuondoa mambo magumu yote, lakini Yeye hufanya muujiza katika nafsi yangu ambao hubadilisha mtazamo wangu na mawazo yangu. Na hilo linanifanya nimbuke kwa kuwa ni muujiza ambao ni wa Mungu tu Mwenyezi-mwenye nguvu yote anaweza kufanya.

Je, unaona kama walilala usiku huo? Walijua jeshi la kutisha lilikuwa njiani kuwaharibu na bado... walikuwa wamemsikia Mungu akizungumza. Labda kulikuwa na matumaini yenye furaha mioyoni mwao na hamu ya kuona jinsi Mungu angepata ushindi katika vita hii. Ninapojifunza kutekeleza imani katika mambo madogo na makubwa yanayojikusanya katika maisha yangu, hivi karibuni nitajifunza kuwa na moyo wa matarajio yaliyotiwa shauku, kwa maana najua Atatenda kitu! Atanipeleka njia ya kutoka. Hata ikiwa kibaya zaidi kitatokea, Atataonyesha moyo wangu njia ya amani na ameahidi kuwa pamoja nami kupitia yote hayo. Na kwa kweli, ushindi wa mwisho tayari umeshashinda, kwa hiyo hizo mizozo zote zinahusisha nini na amani na furaha yangu? Hakuna.

Asubuhi ilitokeza; ilikuwa siku ambayo Mungu alikuwa amewaambia waende dhidi ya maadui hawa. Wakasimama bila kuchelewesha. Wote walijua kwamba utiifu ulikuwa muhimu kupata baraka za Mungu siku hiyo. Na walipoondoka mji, Yehoshafati aliwahimiza. Na wakainuka mapema asubuhi, ...na walipoanza kuondoka, Yehoshafati alisimama na kusema, ...Aminini kwa BWANA Mungu wenu, nanyi mtathibika; amini nabii wake, nanyi mtafanikiwa. Na...aliwaita waimbaji kwa BWANA, na wawe wakiwapongeza uzuri wa utakatifu, walipoenda mbele ya jeshi... – mistari 21-20. Aliwaita waimbaji waliokuwa wanaimba wakitoka, wakitangaza kwa kila mtu na kwa jeshi la wapinzani kwamba walikuwa upande wa Bwana.

Nilipenda kuona jeshi hilo kubwa likiishi toka mjini, wakiiimba. Walikuwa wanakabiliana na kazi ya kutisha na ambayo ingewafanya mtu mwenye nguvu aitetemeka, lakini walikuwa wakiimba. Na waliapoanza kuimba na kuabudu, BWANA akafanya ... [kufanyia) mashambulizi dhidi ya wana wa Amini, [na] Moabu, ...walikuja dhidi ya Yuda; na walipigwa ... kila mmoja akasaidia kumwangamiza mwenzake – mistari 22-23.

Watu wa Yuda walikwenda kwenye mnara wa kuangalia na kwa mshangao waliona maadui zao walikuwa wametwikwa wenyewe, na waliona hakuna zaidi ya jeshi la miili wafu. Wakati vita ya kutisha imepangwa dhidi yangu, bado ninaweza kufanya uamuzi wa kuamini na kuimba. Kuimba ni tendo la makusudi la ibada; inakumbusha nafsi zetu na nafsi za watu wote wanaosikiliza kwamba Bwana, Yeye ndiye Mungu. Yeye ndiye Aliye na udhibiti kamili wa hali zangu, dunia yangu ndogo, na matatizo yake yote. Ghafla maadui wanauawa. Hali inaweza kuwa haijabadilika, lakini vita imekamilika katika nafsi yangu.

Jeshi la Yuda lilitumia siku tatu zilizoifuwa kukusanya mali na shinani kutoka kwa miili ya maadui zao waliouawa, wakikusanya kwa wingi kiasi kwamba hawakuweza kubebwa nayo wote. Inashangaza! Lakini kutumia aina hii ni kawaida kila wakati. Roho yangu inafaidi kutokana na mambo magumu niliyoyavumilia kwa mafanikio. Kila ushindi huniruhusu kukusanya ‘shinani’ ambazo zitanifaa maisha yangu yote. Moyo wangu umejaa baraka, ya kutunzwa, na kubebwa na Baba wa Mbinguni. “Majeshi ya Moabu na Amoni” yameleta baraka badala ya uharibifu.

Walikaribishwa nyumbani kwao Yerusalemu wakiwa wakiimba, na vyuma vya mrija, na tarumbeta, wakiwa wamebeba sana shinani zao zote. Hofu ya Mungu ilidondoka juu ya falme zote za nchi waliposikia jinsi Mungu alivyopigana vita hii kubwa, basi ufalme wa Yehoshafati ukawahulusia. Amani ikatawala.

Amani ya kujua kwamba kile pekee ninachohitaji ni Mungu na kazi Yake katika maisha yangu ndiyo amani ya juu kabisa. Dunia hii iliyovunjika inaweza kuleta maumivu, magonjwa, na kukata tamaa, lakini Mungu analeta mapumziko kwa moyo ambao hapo awali ulikuwa umejaa vurugu na hofu. Kuna mapumziko ‘kando yake’ na ‘falme zote za nchi’ zitashangazwa na kutaka kujua nguvu iliyotuwepo ndani, kwa maana ni nguvu ambayo hakuna anayezoshindana nayo—nguvu ya Mungu wetu wa ajabu.

I grew up in the same church setting in which my parents were born and raised. However, by the time I was 10, my parents began to be concerned with the direction the young folks were going and wanted something different for their children. So, my parents got in touch with a church from another state, which helped them make connections with a small church that was located close to where we lived.

I was more of a quiet, strong-willed child and was quickly turning into a rebellious teenager. My parents did all they knew to do with me at the time. One of which was making the move to this new church since it had more of a godly youth environment. I had a hard time with this change. At our old church, I had friends that were on the same page as me and supported me in my rebellious ways, but at the new church I was more of the “bad guy” and didn’t fit in with the other young people.

Over the course of time that church dissolved, and my parents decided to move to another state, closer to a more stable church. So it was, that, when I was 14, we spent our first night in a different state, in a different house, on a different road, and with different neighbors. We went shopping in a different town and went to a different church, with people that I barely knew. I didn’t like change. I found it challenging to meet new people and make new friends. I struggled majorly with all these changes, so, I never bothered trying to plug in and be an active part in our new life. Instead, I slowly built walls around my life and heart, all the while growing colder and more rebellious.

As I grew older and harder, my parents tried to work with me, but I would have nothing to do with it. I eventually got a job and was introduced to country music and other worldly things. Since I enjoy work, I poured myself into it and worked long hours. That way I wouldn’t need to be around the family or church people, and I wouldn’t need to go to church activities. Thus, I became more removed and isolated from those around me.

The church people didn’t know how to relate to me; most of them just left me to myself. Deep down I was desperately longing for love and acceptance from my family and church. This caused me to spiral downward. I continued to stuff my feelings and build a wall around myself, all the while hardening my heart further. As time went on, I withdrew more and more from my family and the church. I felt more and more like a social misfit that no one knew what to do with. I decided I was going to run away and live my own life.

Somehow my parents got wind of this idea and tried to do all that they knew to do to help me, but I resented it. Looking back, I know without a doubt that they were doing it out of love and care, but there was a great lack in our relationship. Thus, I continued to grow harder and colder.

The summer I was 17, a visiting minister (‘Mike’) and his family came to our church for meetings. I knew them from years before and somehow through our interaction during the meetings my heart started to soften and open. I’m not quite sure why, but for some reason, I decided that I wanted to go spend the winter with them. So, my parents got in contact with them, and it was decided that I could stay with them for a few months.

My plan was to spend a few months away from everything and then I would return home when I was almost 18. Once I was 18, I was planning to leave home and do my own thing. I was certain no one could stop me because I would be of legal age. However, God obviously had different plans...

Somehow ‘Mike’ convinced me to go to along to a week of meetings in another state. While we were there, I don’t remember that the conviction was any stronger than any other time. However, one evening after the service he asked me if I wanted to become a Christian and have my sins forgiven. I don’t remember what I told him, but we talked for a while. He took me through the Bible, helping me to see what God says about it all; then we prayed. When we got up from praying, I can’t say that something major happened, but it was definitely the night that I found salvation! That night, something changed in my heart. I knew that I now wanted to do things God’s way. I knew that my end goal in life was to run the race well and to finish victoriously. That is what has helped me through the years.

On July 31, 2011, I was baptized upon the confession of my faith. The next number of years were definitely not easy. I would even say that at times it seemed to have been harder than in the years before my conversion. Out of respect to others, I don’t feel I can share everything that has happened over the years, but I will try to share several main points. You can imagine that with the walls I had built around myself and the comfort I had found in this, that the years following my conversion were full of ups and downs as I tried to relearn how to relate to other believers and to people in general.

Even though I had reached out to God for forgiveness of my sins and had committed my life to following Him, I had many old habits of relating to others in wrong ways that still needed to be sanctified. Things at home continued to improve but there was still room for progress, which added to the stress. As the years went by, my stress level continued to rise. I didn’t know what to do with it, so I resorted to taking high doses of NoDoz® with an energy drink before I went to bed, trying to get my nerves to relax enough so I could sleep (don’t try this at home, it is dangerous). The next day I would get up and face it all again. One year for most of the year I struggled with thoughts of not wanting to continue on with life. During this time, I had a very close friend who gave me much encouragement. I believe that the regular contact I had with this close friend, the prayers of others, and God’s faithfulness all working together kept me from doing something that I would have later regretted.

I had another close friend who had also gone through a lot but seemed to be finding God’s answers to life’s struggles. We would go out for supper, spending time together talking about life’s struggles. I remember times that I would leave his car and tears would be streaming down his face because he wasn’t sure if I was going to make it. Then he went to the mission field for two years to teach English.

I’m not sure what all was going on in his life but one day we got word that he was missing. Eventually we heard from him; he was okay and was living back in the states again. My heart was torn… One of the few friends that I had, had now turned his back on what he had once believed and on that which he had once tried to convince me of. Yet here I was, still struggling… Why not just give up fighting…? Why not just go live the easy life…? As time went on, I continued to long for love and acceptance. At times the struggle, the aching, and the longing seemed almost unbearable. But I knew deep down that giving up was not what I wanted. It would not get the end result that I wanted. Once more through the encouragement and regular contact with my close friend, the prayers of others, and God’s faithfulness, I continued to press on.

Another young man started taking an interest in my life and we eventually became close friends. He and his wife were a great encouragement to me. Then due to some disagreements with the church, they became dissatisfied and left the church. They threw aside a lot of what they had once stood for. So here I was once again with a close friend that had turned his back on what he had once stood for. What’s the use? Why does life need to be so hard? Maybe I should also give up… But I didn’t want to totally throw God out. Maybe I could find a church that was less strict. Once again, I came to my senses and realized that’s not really what I wanted. That direction wouldn’t take me where I wanted to go. So once more through the encouragement and regular contact with my close friend, the prayers of others, and God’s faithfulness, I continued to press on. At the time it was tough, but looking back, I see I have learned a lot by all I have gone through.

In the fall of 2015, I went to Washington state due to a work opportunity. At the time I went, there were things going on at my home church that I was struggling with. Because of all the stress that I was facing, I was feeling quite discouraged about Church life, Christianity, and life in general. I wasn’t wanting to throw my Christianity away, but I was wondering, “Is this really what it’s all about?” “Why can’t people just get along?” Is this really what God had in mind for His people? If we are “little Christs” like we claim to be, shouldn’t we be able to get along? Shouldn’t we be the ones that are joyful and full of life?

I went to Washington with these kinds of thoughts on my mind. While there, I attended a church that was both Biblical and spiritually minded. It’s hard to explain all that went on in my mind, heart, and life during those six months. But I left there and went back home with a renewed strength and vision.

We should be the light of the world! We should have something to offer others! We should be able to get along with one another! Yes, we do go through hard times individually and collectively as a church, but if we fight the good fight of faith, if we finish our course, if we keep the faith, there is laid up for each of us a crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, shall give me at that day: and not to me only but unto all them also that love his appearing. I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith: Henceforth there is laid up for me a crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, shall give me at that day: and not to me only, but unto all them also that love his appearing –2 Timothy 4:7-8.

* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

June 15, 2018, at 4:40 pm. the scream of the emergency services’ pager split the peaceful afternoon as it crackled to life. “One-car rollover on ‘Gingko Avenue’, possible entrapment,” was the repeated dispatch. As we walked onto the scene, there sat a young girl who appeared to be in her mid-twenties and was visibly banged up. With blood and tears streaming down her face, she repeated these phrases, “I don’t want to die… I’m not ready to die… I may never see my baby again.” As seconds turned to minutes, the paramedics tried to calm her anxious nerves. We searched the mangled car and surrounding area for the supposed missing baby. All the while she sat there with lines of worry and fear. She had tears and blood streaming down her face, as she repeated, “I may never see my baby again… I don’t want to die… I’m not ready to die.”

As first responders, all we found was a car seat that wasn’t fastened in, with no evidence of a baby anywhere. As the ambulance crew strapped her to the stretcher and loaded her in the ambulance, she was still repeating, “Where’s my baby…? I’m not ready to die… I don’t want to die… I may never see my baby again.”

As I left the scene that evening, with that image and those phrases running through my mind, I was struck with two sober thoughts. If that was me, miraculously surviving an accident and sitting there beside my vehicle, barely coherent, with blood streaming down my face, what would I be saying? What would the paramedics and rescue team remember me by? Would I be ready to die? Would I be clear before God?

* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

As Christians, when is the last time we helped someone prepare their soul for death? As believers who have been redeemed from the misery and chaos of a life of sin (see 1 Corinthians 6:9-11), we should …be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh [us] you a reason of the hope that is in [us] you with meekness and fear: –1 Peter 3:15.

In the fall of 2018, God opened the door for me to move to a church in a different state where I have found stability. It was here that God brought a godly young lady into my life, and we were married on November 30, 2019. Being married and having brothers who surrounded me with discipleship, compassion, and prayerful support helped me to grow in the Lord in many ways.

Being here has awakened within me a renewed vision to be the light of the world. Today, I am thankful that God did not let me go. As I kept fighting the spiritual fight, God kept giving me the strength and wisdom to do the next right thing. With each victory, my strength has grown stronger. Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you… –James 4:8. I thank God for giving me victory and for helping me find my ultimate source of love, security, and purpose—my Lord and Saviour, Jesus Christ.

Я вырос в той же церковной обстановке, в которой родились и воспитывались мои родители. Однако к тому времени, когда мне исполнилось 10, родители начали беспокоиться о том, куда движется молодёжь, и хотели для своих детей чего‑то иного. Поэтому мои родители связались с церковью из другого штата, которая помогла им установить контакты с небольшой церковью, расположенной недалеко от места, где мы жили.

Я был более тихим, волевым ребёнком и быстро превращался в бунтующего подростка. Родители сделали всё, что знали, чтобы справиться со мной в то время. Одним из таких шагов был переезд в новую церковь, потому что там была более благочестивая молодёжная обстановка. Мне было тяжело с этой переменой. В нашей старой церкви у меня были друзья, которые были на той же волне и поддерживали меня в моих бунтарских наклонностях, но в новой церкви я оказался больше «плохим парнем» и не вписывался среди других молодых людей.

Со временем та церковь распалась, и мои родители решили переехать в другой штат, ближе к более стабильной церкви. Так получилось, что когда мне было 14, мы провели нашу первую ночь в другом штате, в другом доме, на другой улице и с другими соседями. Мы ходили за покупками в другом городе и ходили в другую церковь, с людьми, которых я едва знал. Мне не нравились изменения. Мне было сложно знакомиться с новыми людьми и заводить новых друзей. Я серьёзно боролся со всеми этими переменами, поэтому никогда не пытался включиться и стать активной частью нашей новой жизни. Вместо этого я постепенно выстраивал стены вокруг своей жизни и сердца, всё сильнее остывая и становясь более непокорным.

По мере того как я становился старше и жёстче, родители пытались со мной работать, но я ни в чём не хотел с ними связываться. В конце концов я устроился на работу и познакомился с кантри‑музыкой и другими мирскими вещами. Поскольку мне нравилась работа, я отдался ей целиком и работал долгими часами. Так мне не приходилось находиться рядом с семьёй или церковными людьми, и мне не нужно было посещать церковные мероприятия. В результате я стал более отстранённым и изолированным от окружающих.

Церковные люди не знали, как со мной общаться; большинство просто оставляли меня в покое. В глубине души я отчаянно жаждал любви и принятия со стороны семьи и церкви. Это заставляло меня всё глубже погружаться в ухудшение. Я продолжал зажимать в себе чувства и строить вокруг себя стену, всё сильнее ожесточая сердце. Со временем я всё больше отдалялся от семьи и церкви. Я ощущал себя социальным неудачником, с которым никто не знал, что делать. Я решил, что убегу и буду жить своей собственной жизнью.

Как‑то родители узнали об этой идее и пытались сделать всё, что знали, чтобы мне помочь, но я этому противился. Оглядываясь назад, я без сомнения знаю, что они делали это из любви и заботы, но в наших отношениях всё же была большая пустота. Так я продолжал становиться жёстче и холоднее.

Летом, когда мне было 17, в нашу церковь на собрания приехал проповедник по имени «Майк» вместе со своей семьёй. Я знал их ещё с прежних лет, и в какой‑то момент во время собраний моё сердце стало смягчаться и открываться. Точно не знаю почему, но по какой‑то причине я решил, что хочу провести зиму у них. Мои родители связались с ними, и было решено, что я могу пожить у них несколько месяцев.

Мой план был провести несколько месяцев вдалеке от всего, а затем вернуться домой, когда мне будет почти 18. Когда мне исполнится 18, я собирался уйти из дома и жить по‑своему. Я был уверен, что никто не сможет меня остановить, потому что я стану совершеннолетним. Однако у Бога были иные планы...

Как‑то «Майк» уговорил меня поехать с ними на неделю собраний в другой штат. Когда мы были там, я не помню, чтобы угрызения совести были сильнее, чем в другие времена. Однако однажды вечером после служения он спросил меня, хочу ли я стать христианином и чтобы мои грехи были прощены. Я не помню, что ему ответил, но мы поговорили некоторое время. Он прошёл со мной по Библии, помогая мне увидеть, что Бог говорит обо всём этом; затем мы помолились. Когда мы поднялись после молитвы, я не могу сказать, что произошло что‑то кардинальное, но это была та самая ночь, когда я нашёл спасение! В ту ночь что‑то изменилось в моём сердце. Я понял, что теперь хочу поступать по‑Божьему. Я осознал, что моя конечная цель в жизни — благополучно бежать дистанцию и победоносно финишировать. Это то, что помогало мне все эти годы.

31 июля 2011 года я был крещён по исповеди моей веры. Последующие несколько лет были, без сомнения, нелёгкими. Я бы даже сказал, что порой это казалось труднее, чем годы до моего обращения. Из уважения к другим я не чувствую, что могу рассказать обо всём, что происходило за эти годы, но постараюсь поделиться основными моментами. Можно представить, что с теми стенами, которые я выстроил вокруг себя, и с тем комфортом, который я в этом нашёл, годы после моего обращения были полны взлётов и падений, пока я пытался заново научиться общаться с другими верующими и людьми вообще.

Хотя я и обратился к Богу за прощением грехов и посвятил жизнь следованию за Ним, у меня осталось много давних неправильных привычек общения с людьми, которые ещё требовали освящения. Дела дома продолжали улучшаться, но оставалось место для прогресса, что добавляло стресса. С годами уровень моего стресса продолжал расти. Я не знал, что с этим делать, поэтому прибегал к приёму больших доз NoDoz® с энергетическим напитком перед сном, пытаясь успокоить нервы настолько, чтобы заснуть (не повторяйте этого дома, это опасно). На следующее утро я вставал и снова всё это переживал. В один год большую часть времени я боролся с мыслями о том, что не хочу продолжать жить. В этот период у меня был очень близкий друг, который много меня поощрял. Я верю, что регулярный контакт с этим близким другом, молитвы других и Божья верность вместе удержали меня от того, о чём бы я позже жалел.

У меня был ещё один близкий друг, который тоже прошёл через многое, но, казалось, находил у Бога ответы на жизненные трудности. Мы выходили поужинать, проводили время вместе, разговаривая о жизненных проблемах. Я помню моменты, когда, выходя из его машины, я видел, как по его лицу текли слёзы, потому что он не был уверен, переживу ли я это. Затем он уехал на миссию на два года, чтобы преподавать английский язык.

Я не уверен, что происходило в его жизни, но однажды дошёл слух, что он пропал без вести. В конце концов мы получили от него весть: с ним всё в порядке, и он снова жил в США. Моё сердце было разорвано… Один из немногих друзей, которые у меня были, отвернулся от того, во что он когда‑то верил, и от того, в чём он когда‑то пытался убедить меня. А я всё ещё боролся… Почему бы не сдаться…? Почему бы не жить по‑лёгкому…? Со временем я продолжал жаждать любви и принятия. Иногда борьба, боль и тоска казались почти невыносимыми. Но я глубоко внутри знал, что сдаваться — не то, чего я хочу. Это не принесло бы мне желаемого конечного результата. И снова, благодаря поощрению и регулярному общению с близким другом, молитвам других и Божьей верности, я продолжал идти вперёд.

Другой молодой человек стал проявлять интерес к моей жизни, и в конце концов мы стали близкими друзьями. Он и его жена были для меня большой поддержкой. Затем из‑за разногласий с церковью они испытали недовольство и ушли из церкви. Они отбросили многое из того, за что когда‑то стояли. И вот я снова оказался с близким другом, который отвернулся от своих прежних убеждений. Какой в этом смысл? Зачем жизнь должна быть такой трудной? Может, мне тоже сдаться… Но я не хотел полностью отвергать Бога. Может, я найду церковь менее строгую. Опять я пришёл в себя и понял, что это не то, чего я действительно хочу. Это направление не приведёт меня туда, куда я хочу попасть. Поэтому снова, благодаря поощрению и регулярному общению с близким другом, молитвам других и Божьей верности, я продолжал бороться. Тогда было тяжело, но оглядываясь назад, я вижу, что многому научился благодаря пройденному.

Осенью 2015 года я уехал в штат Вашингтон по работе. В то время в моей церкви происходили вещи, с которыми мне было трудно мириться. Из‑за всего стресса я был довольно обескуражен церковной жизнью, христианством и жизнью вообще. Я не хотел отрекаться от своей христианской веры, но задавался вопросами: «Неужели вот в чём всё заключается?» «Почему люди не могут просто ладить?» «Разве это действительно то, что Бог задумал для Своего народа?» Если мы «маленькие Христосы», как мы себя называем, разве нам не следовало бы уметь ладить друг с другом? Разве мы не должны быть теми, кто радостен и полон жизни?

Я поехал в Вашингтон с такими мыслями. Там я посещал церковь, которая была и библейской, и духовно настроенной. Трудно объяснить всё, что происходило в моём уме, сердце и жизни в течение тех шести месяцев. Но я уехал оттуда и вернулся домой с обновлённой силой и видением.

Мы должны быть светом мира! Мы должны иметь что‑то, что можем предложить другим! Мы должны уметь ладить друг с другом! Да, по отдельности и всем нам как церкви приходят тяжёлые времена, но если мы бьёмся доброй битвой веры, если мы пройдём курс до конца, если мы храним веру, то нам уготована награда: для каждого из нас отложена венец праведности, который даст мне в тот день Господь, праведный Судия; и не только мне, но и всем, кто любит явление Его. Я сразился доброй битвой, я окончил путь, я сохранил веру: поэтому отложен мне венец праведности, который даст мне в тот день Господь, праведный Судия; и не только мне, но и всем, кто любит явление Его — 2 Тимофею 4:7-8.

* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

15 июня 2018 года в 16:40 крик пейджера экстренных служб разорвал спокойный полдень, когда он зашевелился. «Переворот одного автомобиля на улице Gingko Avenue, возможно, кто‑то зажат в салоне», — повторялся диспетчерский вызов. Когда мы подошли к месту происшествия, там сидела молодая женщина, которой, по‑видимому, было около двадцати пяти лет, и она была заметно побита. С кровью и слезами, струящимися по лицу, она повторяла фразы: «Я не хочу умирать… Я не готова умирать… Я может никогда больше не увижу своего ребёнка». По мере того как секунды превращались в минуты, парамедики пытались успокоить её встревоженные нервы. Мы обыскали покорёженный автомобиль и прилегающую территорию в поисках предполагаемого пропавшего ребёнка. Всё это время она сидела, с линиями тревоги и страха на лице. По её лицу текли слёзы и кровь, и она повторяла: «Я может никогда больше не увижу своего ребёнка… Я не готова умирать… Я не хочу умирать».

Как первые ответившие на вызов, мы нашли только автокресло, не пристёгнутое, без каких‑либо следов ребёнка где‑либо. Пока бригада скорой помощи укладывала её на носилки и грузила в машину, она всё ещё повторяла: «Где мой ребёнок…? Я не готова умирать… Я не хочу умирать… Я может никогда больше не увижу своего ребёнка».

Когда я уезжал с места происшествия тем вечером, с этим образом и этими фразами, крутящимися в моей голове, ко мне пришли две трезвые мысли. Если бы это была я, чудом пережившая аварию и сидящая рядом со своим автомобилем, едва связная, с кровью на лице, что бы я говорила? Чем бы запомнились меня парамедики и спасательная команда? Была бы я готова умереть? Была бы я ясна перед Богом?

* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

Как христиане, когда в последний раз мы помогали кому‑то подготовить душу к смерти? Как верующие, искупленные от бедствия и хаоса жизни во грехе (см. 1 Коринфянам 6:9-11), мы должны …всегда быть готовыми дать ответ каждому, кто спрашивает у вас отчет о надежде, которая в вас, с кротостью и страхом; — 1 Петра 3:15.

Осенью 2018 года Бог открыл дверь для моего переезда в церковь в другом штате, где я нашёл стабильность. Именно там Бог привёл в мою жизнь благочестивую молодую женщину, и мы поженились 30 ноября 2019 года. Быть женатым и иметь братьев, которые окружали меня ученичеством, состраданием и молитвенной поддержкой, помогло мне вырасти в Господе во многих отношениях.

Пребывание здесь пробудило во мне обновлённое видение быть светом мира. Сегодня я благодарен Богу за то, что Он не оставил меня. Пока я продолжал бороться духовную битву, Бог давал мне силу и мудрость делать следующее правильное дело. С каждой победой моя сила возрастала. Приблизьтесь к Богу, и Он приблизится к вам… — Иакова 4:8. Я благодарю Бога за то, что Он дал мне победу и помог найти мой высший источник любви, безопасности и цели — моего Господа и Спасителя, Иисуса Христа.

This hymn is generally thought to be one of the most loved hymns written during the latter part of the 19th century. The writing of this thoughtful and beautifully constructed text is even more amazing when we consider that its author was one who was almost completely blind and who describes the writing of this hymn as the “fruit of much mental suffering,” and “the quickest bit of work I ever did in my life.”

Born in Glasgow, Scotland, March 27, 1842, George Matheson had only partial vision as a boy, and, after entering Glasgow University, his eyesight continued to fail rapidly. Except for “moments of shadowy eyesight”, he was totally blind by the age of 18. This affliction of blindness seemed to be a tragedy since he was an eager and avid scholar, yet it caused him to trust in the Lord, and it strengthened his walk with God.

He entered the university at the early age of 15 and graduated with high honors in 1861 at the age of 19. He was a brilliant scholar, even spending four more years after graduation in more theological studies, all the while remaining single. After his graduation he became entirely dependent on others, relying much upon his two sisters, who were so dedicated that they learned Latin, Greek, and Hebrew since they thought it might aid him in his theological studies. One of them continued to be his faithful co-worker and helper throughout his life, assisting in his calling of being a pastor and other ministerial duties.

After completing his theological course, he became assistant pastor to the renowned Dr. Macduff, in whose church of thousands of members he had been brought up. Soon, however, he was chosen minister of the Church of Scotland in the seaport summer resort of Innellan. Here he stayed for eighteen years. Many families came to spend the summer there chiefly to be inspired by his preaching ministry.

Whenever he preached, the open Bible was before him as he stood in the pulpit, and to the congregation, he seemed to be reading from it. During the messages, his eyes looked straight at the congregation, and many went away with no clue that they just listened to a blind preacher. It was during this time that he made a practice of memorizing his sermons, as well as the passages of Scripture he used in his messages. His memory was so sharp that if someone read one of his prepared sermons to him twice, or whatever else he wanted to memorize, he could from then on repeat it perfectly. One Sunday, however, after doing this for 12 years, when in the middle of a powerful sermon his memory completely collapsed, and the topic on which he was preaching vanished from his mind. He sat down and commenced to request a psalm to be sung, and, after the song, with perfect calmness told the audience what had happened. With this done, he stood to his feet, gave out a new text, and preached an impromptu sermon of great power. After that experience George wrote little of his sermons, and finally prepared only an outline from which to preach.

Dr. Matheson’s final pastorate was taken up in 1886 at the age of 44 where he became pastor of the large St. Bernard’s Parish Church in Edinburgh, where his eloquent preaching consistently attracted large throngs of people to the services. Here he remained for 13 years, his church growing from 1,494 members to 1,703 in the first 5 years. He continued faithfully preaching the gospel and became well known as one of Scotland’s outstanding preachers and pastors and was greatly esteemed in Edinburgh where he resided.

Many speculations have been made regarding the cause of the mental distress which prompted the author to write this text. A very popular account, although never verified, is that this text was a result of the severe trial Matheson faced after his soon-to-be bride left him just before their marriage when she learned of his impending total blindness. Although this story cannot be documented, there are many significant hints in this hymn reflecting a saddened heart, such as the “flickering torch” and the “borrowed ray” in the second verse, the tracing of the “rainbow through the rain” in the third stanza, as well as the “cross” in the last verse.

Fortunately, Dr. Matheson did relate an account of his writing of this hymn:

“My hymn was composed in the manse of Innellan on the evening of June 6, 1882. I was at that time alone. It was the day of my sister’s wedding, and the rest of the family were staying overnight in Glasgow. Something happened to me, which was known only to myself, and which caused me the most severe mental suffering. The hymn was the fruit of that suffering and was the quickest bit of work I ever did in my life. A genuine inspiration, I had the impression rather of having it dictated to me by some inward voice than of working it out myself. I am quite sure that the whole work was completed in five minutes and equally sure it never received at my hands any retouching or correction. I have no natural gift of rhythm. All the other verses I have ever written are manufactured articles; this came like a dayspring from on high. I have never been able to gain once more the same fervor in verse.”

The hymn first appeared in the Church of Scotland monthly magazine, Life and Work, in January 1883. The tune was composed one year later by a prominent Scotch organist of his day, Albert L. Peace, who was asked to write a tune especially for Matheson’s text.

Peace’s own account of the writing of this fine tune is as follows, “After reading it over carefully, I wrote the music straight off, and may say that the ink of the first note was hardly dry when I had finished the tune.” The origin or the tune name, St. Margaret, is unknown except that it is a name much revered in Scotland, and certainly because of the beloved Queen Margaret of Scotland.

The later years of Matheson’s life from the age of 57 to his death at age 64 were spent in writing some of the finest devotional writings in the English tongue, including Moments on the Mount, Voice of the Spirit, and Rests by the River. Although this is his only hymn found in most hymnals, he did write a few other fine hymns, including “Make Me A Captive Lord”, and “Then I Shall Be Free.”

The four key words of “O Love, That Wilt Not Let Me Go” are: love, light, joy, and cross. These words have been described as the complete satisfaction for any believer whose life is totally surrendered to the will of God. It could take the rest of one’s life to completely discover the personal significance of these four expressions.

Αυτός ο ύμνος θεωρείται γενικά ένας από τους πιο αγαπημένους ύμνους που γράφτηκαν κατά το τελευταίο μέρος του 19th αιώνα. Η συγγραφή αυτού του στοχαστικού και όμορφα δομημένου κειμένου είναι ακόμη πιο αξιοσημείωτη αν λάβουμε υπόψη ότι ο συγγραφέας του ήταν σχεδόν εντελώς τυφλός και περιγράφει τη συγγραφή αυτού του ύμνου ως «καρπό πολλής πνευματικής οδύνης» και «το πιο γρήγορο κομμάτι δουλειάς που έχω κάνει ποτέ στη ζωή μου.»

Γεννημένος στη Γλασκώβη της Σκωτίας, στις 27 Μαρτίου 1842, ο George Matheson είχε μόνο μερική όραση ως παιδί και, αφού εισήλθε στο Πανεπιστήμιο της Γλασκώβης, η όρασή του συνέχισε να χειροτερεύει γρήγορα. Εκτός από «στιγμές σκιώδους όρασης», ήταν εντελώς τυφλός σε ηλικία 18 ετών. Αυτή η δοκιμασία της τύφλωσης φαινόταν καταστροφική αφού ήταν πρόθυμος και αδηφάγος μελετητής, ωστόσο τον οδήγησε να εμπιστευθεί τον Κύριο και ενίσχυσε τον πνευματικό του βίο.

Εισήλθε στο πανεπιστήμιο σε ηλικία 15 ετών και αποφοίτησε με άριστα το 1861 σε ηλικία 19 ετών. Ήταν λαμπρός μαθητής, περνώντας ακόμη τέσσερα χρόνια μετά την αποφοίτηση σε περαιτέρω θεολογικές σπουδές, παραμένοντας την ίδια περίοδο άγαμος. Μετά την αποφοίτησή του έγινε εντελώς εξαρτημένος από άλλους, στηριζόμενος σε μεγάλο βαθμό στις δύο αδελφές του, οι οποίες ήταν τόσο αφοσιωμένες που έμαθαν λατινικά, ελληνικά και εβραϊκά καθώς νόμιζαν ότι αυτό θα μπορούσε να τον βοηθήσει στις θεολογικές του σπουδές. Η μία από αυτές συνέχισε να είναι η πιστή συνεργάτιδα και βοηθός του σε όλη του τη ζωή, υποβοηθώντας τον στο κήρυγμα και σε άλλα υπηρεσιακά καθήκοντα.

Μετά την ολοκλήρωση του θεολογικού του κύκλου, έγινε βοηθός ποιμένα στον διαπρεπή Δρ. Macduff, στην εκκλησία του οποίου είχε μεγαλώσει. Σύντομα, όμως, επιλέχθηκε ως κληρικός της Εκκλησίας της Σκωτίας στο παραθαλάσσιο θερινό θέρετρο Innellan. Εκεί παρέμεινε δεκαοκτώ χρόνια. Πολλές οικογένειες ερχόταν να περάσουν το καλοκαίρι κυρίως για να εμπνευσθούν από το κηρυγματικό του έργο.

Όποτε κήρυττε, η ανοικτή Βίβλος βρισκόταν μπροστά του καθώς στεκόταν στο άμβωνα, και για την εκκλησία έδειχνε να διαβάζει από αυτήν. Κατά τη διάρκεια των κηρυγμάτων, τα μάτια του ήταν στραμμένα προς το ακροατήριο, και πολλοί έφευγαν χωρίς να έχουν την παραμικρή ιδέα ότι μόλις άκουσαν έναν τυφλό κήρυκα. Κατά την περίοδο αυτή συνήθιζε να απομνημονεύει τα κηρύγματά του, καθώς και τα χωρία της Γραφής που χρησιμοποιούσε στις ομιλίες του. Η μνήμη του ήταν τόσο κοφτερή που αν κάποιος του διάβαζε ένα από τα προετοιμασμένα κηρύγματά του δύο φορές, ή οτιδήποτε άλλο ήθελε να απομνημονεύσει, μπορούσε από τότε να το επαναλάβει τέλεια. Μια Κυριακή, όμως, μετά από αυτή τη συνήθεια για 12 χρόνια, στη μέση ενός δυνατού κηρύγματος η μνήμη του κατέρρευσε εντελώς και το θέμα στο οποίο κήρυττε εξαφανίστηκε από τη σκέψη του. Καθίστηκε και ζήτησε να ψαλεί ένας ψαλμός και, μετά το τραγούδι, με απόλυτη ηρεμία εξήγησε στο ακροατήριο τι είχε συμβεί. Μετά από αυτό στάθηκε, έδωσε ένα νέο κείμενο και κήρυξε ένα αυτοσχέδιο κήρυγμα μεγάλης δύναμης. Μετά από εκείνη την εμπειρία ο George έγραψε λίγα κηρύγματα και τελικά προετοίμαζε μόνο ένα περίγραμμα από το οποίο κήρυττε.

Η τελευταία ποιμαντορία του Δρ. Matheson άρχισε το 1886 σε ηλικία 44 ετών όταν έγινε πάστορας της μεγάλης ενορίας της St. Bernard’s στο Εδιμβούργο, όπου το εύγλωττο κήρυγμά του προσέλκυε σταθερά πλήθη ανθρώπων στις λειτουργίες. Εκεί παρέμεινε για 13 χρόνια, με την εκκλησία του να αυξάνεται από 1.494 μέλη σε 1.703 στα πρώτα 5 χρόνια. Συνέχισε πιστά να κηρύττει το ευαγγέλιο και έγινε ευρύτερα γνωστός ως ένας από τους διακεκριμένους κήρυκες και ποιμένες της Σκωτίας και ήταν πολύ εκτιμητός στο Εδιμβούργο όπου κατοικούσε.

Έχουν γίνει πολλές εικασίες σχετικά με την αιτία της ψυχικής δυσφορίας που ώθησε τον συγγραφέα να γράψει αυτό το κείμενο. Μια πολύ διαδεδομένη εξήγηση, αν και ποτέ μη επαληθευμένη, είναι ότι αυτό το κείμενο ήταν αποτέλεσμα της σκληρής δοκιμασίας που αντιμετώπισε ο Matheson αφού η μέλλουσα νύφη του τον εγκατέλειψε λίγο πριν από τον γάμο όταν έμαθε για την επικείμενη ολική τύφλωσή του. Αν και αυτή η ιστορία δεν μπορεί να τεκμηριωθεί, υπάρχουν πολλές σημαντικές νύξεις σε αυτόν τον ύμνο που αντανακλούν μια λυπημένη καρδιά, όπως η «φλεγμαίνουσα δάδα» και η «δανεική ακτίνα» στο δεύτερο στίχο, η ανίχνευση του «ουράνιου τόξου μέσα από τη βροχή» στην τρίτη στροφή, καθώς και ο «σταυρός» στον τελευταίο στίχο.

Ευτυχώς, ο Δρ. Matheson περιέγραψε ο ίδιος μια αφήγηση για τη συγγραφή αυτού του ύμνου:

«Ο ύμνος μου συντέθηκε στη μάνση του Innellan το βράδυ της 6ης Ιουνίου 1882. Ήμουν εκείνη την ώρα μόνος. Ήταν η μέρα του γάμου της αδελφής μου και τα υπόλοιπα μέλη της οικογένειας έμεναν για τη νύχτα στη Γλασκώβη. Κάτι συνέβη σε μένα, το οποίο ήταν γνωστό μόνο σε μένα, και το οποίο μου προκάλεσε την πιο έντονη πνευματική οδύνη. Ο ύμνος ήταν ο καρπός εκείνης της οδύνης και ήταν το πιο γρήγορο κομμάτι δουλειάς που έκανα ποτέ στη ζωή μου. Μια γνήσια έμπνευση, είχα περισσότερο την εντύπωση ότι μου υπαγορεύθηκε από κάποια εσωτερική φωνή παρά ότι το επεξεργάστηκα εγώ ο ίδιος. Είμαι απολύτως σίγουρος ότι όλο το έργο ολοκληρώθηκε σε πέντε λεπτά και εξίσου σίγουρος ότι ποτέ δεν υπέστη οποιαδήποτε επιμέλεια ή διόρθωση από μένα. Δεν έχω φυσικό χάρισμα ρυθμού. Όλοι οι άλλοι στίχοι που έχω γράψει είναι κατασκευασμένα προϊόντα· αυτός ήρθε σαν αυγή από τα ύψη. Δεν κατόρθωσα ποτέ να ξανακερδίσω την ίδια ζέση στο στίχο.»

Ο ύμνος εμφανίστηκε για πρώτη φορά στο μηνιαίο περιοδικό της Εκκλησίας της Σκωτίας, Life and Work, τον Ιανουάριο του 1883. Η μελωδία συντέθηκε ένα χρόνο αργότερα από έναν εξέχοντα σκωτσέζο οργανίστα της εποχής, τον Albert L. Peace, ο οποίος του ζητήθηκε να γράψει μια μελωδία ειδικά για το κείμενο του Matheson.

Η ίδιος ο Peace αφηγείται για τη σύνθεση αυτής της ωραίας μελωδίας ως εξής: «Αφού το διάβασα προσεκτικά, έγραψα τη μουσική αμέσως και μπορώ να πω ότι το μελάνι της πρώτης νότας μόλις είχε στεγνώσει όταν είχα τελειώσει τη μελωδία.» Η προέλευση ή το όνομα της μελωδίας, St. Margaret, είναι άγνωστα εκτός από το ότι είναι ένα όνομα πολύ σεβαστό στη Σκωτία, και βεβαίως λόγω της αγαπημένης βασίλισσας Margaret της Σκωτίας.

Τα τελευταία χρόνια της ζωής του Matheson, από την ηλικία των 57 έως τον θάνατό του σε ηλικία 64 ετών, αφιερώθηκαν στη συγγραφή κάποιων από τα καλύτερα πνευματικά κείμενα στην αγγλική γλώσσα, συμπεριλαμβανομένων των Moments on the Mount, Voice of the Spirit και Rests by the River. Αν και αυτός είναι ο μοναδικός του ύμνος που βρίσκεται στα περισσότερα υμνολόγια, έγραψε κι άλλους ωραίους ύμνους, συμπεριλαμβανομένων των «Make Me A Captive Lord» και «Then I Shall Be Free.»

Οι τέσσερις βασικές λέξεις του «O Love, That Wilt Not Let Me Go» είναι: αγάπη, φως, χαρά και σταυρός. Αυτές οι λέξεις έχουν περιγραφεί ως η πλήρης ικανοποίηση για κάθε πιστό του οποίου η ζωή είναι εντελώς παραδομένη στο θέλημα του Θεού. Μπορεί να χρειαστεί το υπόλοιπο της ζωής κάποιου για να ανακαλύψει πλήρως την προσωπική σημασία αυτών των τεσσάρων εκφράσεων.

For Christ sent me not to baptize, but to preach the gospel: not with wisdom of words, lest the cross of Christ should be made of none effect. For the preaching of the cross is to them that perish foolishness; but unto us which are saved it is the power of God. …it pleased God by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe –1 Corinthians –1:17-21.

The modern Christian world has duly accepted many of the lowly vehicles that God used to usher in the Kingdom. The virgin birth, the rough-hewn manger, and the swaddling clothes have become sovereign monuments that we could scarcely do without. Even the rude donkey is appreciated on Good Friday and the old, rugged cross has become a spiritual emblem nominally displayed on neck chains and ornate pulpit carvings. While man remains infatuated with the traditional symbols of the gospel, there remains an absurd avenue of God’s choosing that is becoming increasingly despised.

For centuries, the Gospel was heralded by foolish and unlearned men (according to their elite and intellectual counterparts). The biblical truth spoken in simplicity was sufficient of itself for God’s Holy Spirit to use to convert the sinner. While there is no lack for preaching in these days, it appears that much of it is of a different sort than the original form that Christ exemplified. If anyone was capable of articulating a flourish of orations in an accurate philosophical language it would have been the Apostle Paul. Yet, he refused to preach the gospel in this manner, …lest the cross of Christ should be made of none effect –1 Corinthians 1:17. He preached carefully, lest the success should be ascribed to the force of art, and not of truth itself.

Paul had been ingrained in Jewish learning at the feet of Gamaliel and was affluent in understanding both Hebrew and Greek, but in preaching the cross of Christ, he laid his learning aside. He spoke the words of the Gospel in a language void of human power lest the honor belonging to Christ be eclipsed by his own personal power. For his letters, say they, are weighty and powerful; but his bodily presence is weak, and his speech contemptible –2 Corinthians 10:10. It is here where the modern church has spurned the meager vehicles chosen by Christ and the Apostles while diverting to a route more acceptable to in our day. Modern day efficiency demands a more direct route to the end, and if the Bible doesn’t forbid it, we feel that it is our prerogative to employ it.

While evangelical films, music concerts, and a host of other questionable venues of ministry could be mentioned, I wish to speak primarily to the modern invitation system known as the “altar call”. While it is commonly associated with the “old fashioned meetings” of the past two centuries, it is indeed modern due to the fact that for nearly nineteen centuries no one had ever heard of the practice. Evangelists such as George Whitefield, Jonathan Edwards, and even John Wesley had never heard of such a custom. Even Charles Spurgeon (heralded as the “Prince of Preachers”) strongly criticized it and refused to adopt it.*

Thus, we observe, the practice was not born in the apostolic church. It is not found in the ministry of Jesus, His apostles, or even the church of the post-apostolic period. We do see Jesus and the apostles inviting men and women to come to Christ and to be saved, but never by means of this particular method. So why has this practice become such an essential tool in most evangelical and in many Anabaptist churches today? The answer—pragmatic results. Immediately following the sermon, the congregation will sing a hymn during which the preacher calls men and women to walk to the front of the auditorium (to the “altar”) to make a public decision for Christ. Salvation is offered to all who will but come to the front and receive it. Those who come often receive the personal attention of a counselor to pray with them and lead them through confession.

This practice was designed to encourage decisions and obtain results. So, it did. And with slight variations the new method spread with increasing popularity through Charles Finney, and later, Dwight L. Moody, and finally, into virtually all of nineteenth and twentieth century evangelicalism. Peter Cartwright, Sam Jones, R. A. Torrey, Billy Sunday, Bob Jones, Gipsy Smith, John R. Rice, Billy Graham, and George Brunk all employed the method with impressive success. Thus, the invitation system became the accepted normal practice and those who question it are often deemed spiritually eccentric.

Why should we take issue with the practice if the scripture doesn’t forbid it? The answer lies in the question of the propriety of the invitation system. Let us first note that the Scriptures abound with invitations to salvation. Such offers as, Come unto me, …and I will give you rest –Matthew 11:28, and, …If any man thirst, let him come unto me, and drink –John 7:37, are marvelous offers of life to those who will trust Christ. The apostles also did not hesitate to show forth Christ as Savior to all who would listen to their message.

They preached indiscriminately, Repent ye therefore, and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out… –Acts 3:19, and …we pray you in Christ›s stead, be ye reconciled to God –2 Corinthians 5:20. And they testified …to the Jews, and also to the Greeks, repentance toward God, and faith toward our Lord Jesus Christ –Acts 20:21. With all this, every Christian should not only agree but also rejoice.

Finally, …compel them to come in, that my house may be filled –Luke 14:23, is another Bible verse which could be used to lend support to the altar call method. Still, this says nothing to bolster the correctness of the altar call. As we examine the practice at its roots, we cannot help but observe a few deficiencies:

…Extra-Biblical

This is no reflection upon the multitudes who have found salvation at such an event. The angels in heaven rejoice at the repentance of every sinner no matter how he arrives there. We simply wish to hold forth the simplicity of the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe. The altar call is used as a specific addition to the sermon to bring to fruition what the foolishness of preaching itself could not do.

The altar call gained popularity in the 1830’s with the preaching of Charles G. Finney who wrote, “A revival is not a miracle, or dependent on a miracle, in any sense. It is a purely philosophical result of the right use of the constituted means.” ** We cannot accuse all who practice the altar call of believing this, but it is rather revealing that the preacher who brought it to popularity seemed to liken it more to a mathematical equation than to divine involvement.

When the truth falls on the soil of a good and honest heart, the seed veritably takes root and produces fruit. This seed of truth needs no artificial dress. It shines out with the greatest majesty in its own light and prevails in the world by its divine authority. It is a demonstration of the Spirit, without need of human invention or intervention. The plain preaching of a crucified Christ is more powerful than all the oratory, philosophical, and heart gripping modes of the world.

…Emotional Thrust

The altar call requires a seeker to leave his seat and walk to the forefront for pardon. These invitations are often preceded by fearfully moving accounts, sad stories, or testimonies that stir the emotions to fear, guilt, or regret. Flanked by a soft hymn sung by the congregation, the emotions are ripe to move forward. Those who choose to repent from their seat without responding are often esteemed as “missing an opportunity”.

And these are they likewise which are sown on stony ground; who, when they have heard the word, immediately receive it with gladness; And have no root in themselves, and so endure but for a time: afterward, when affliction or persecution ariseth for the word’s sake, immediately they are offended –Mark 4:16-17. We refuse to deduce that all who were converted under this type of ministry are stony ground hearers. Yet, the vast majority of those who receive it in such a charged emotional environment will often have a less than sincere conversion.

I once had an exuberant client in my shop who informed me that their church had sponsored a national evangelical ministry to preach at the public high school. “There were over 400 decisions for Christ!” While we all wish to rejoice with the angels, one cannot but question how many of them were still in church a year later. While the lack of true commitment may not fall upon the use of the altar call alone, we may be sure that the seed so quick to spring up will surely manifest itself at the moorings of an emotional invitation. Those that have no root would be better off never having responded prematurely.

Conversions wrought through emotional channels are often questionable and transient. Holy Spirit promptings do not need human strength, wisdom, or efforts to convey them forth. Revival methods such as shouting, overt weeping, emotion eliciting music, and the telling of sentimental stories is the man-made art of preaching. It is also found in many other public venues that are designed to elicit a specific predetermined response from the hearer. Each of these dimensions is quite natural to human behavior and, at times, there may be a fine line between what is acceptable and unacceptable in preaching. Great care should be taken that we do not create an emotional climax and eclipse the message in an inordinate manner lest the power be of men and not of Christ.

…Encroachment to Parental and Local Church Authority

Children are often a target at such a time. They may feel guilty for some childish misdeed, but a fiery message followed by emotional pleading can be very unsettling. These are times when a parent should speak to the heart of their child and connect in a spiritual way. Instead, often the child is moved to the front and given a church counselor for them to pour out their confession.

I know a woman whose father was an itinerant evangelical preacher. She claims that she responded “hundreds of times” to the altar call. A casual and honest appraisal would reveal that while the altar call may bring commencement to many sincere conversions, it also avails itself equally to a host of premature decisions and pressure-driven commitments. This often leaves many unstable souls wallowing in spiritual instability and struggling with a lack of assurance of salvation for years to come.

For though ye have ten thousand instructors in Christ, yet have ye not many fathers: for in Christ Jesus I have begotten you through the gospel. Wherefore I beseech you, be ye followers of me –1 Corinthians 4:15-16. God has ordained fathers and mothers to bring birth to their children, both physical and spiritual.

Be ye followers of me, even as I also am of Christ –1 Corinthians 11:1. The skilled itinerant evangelist has no intention of begetting spiritual children and making followers of himself. This he leaves to others, for he has found his gift in compelling people to make decisions.

And we beseech you, brethren, to know them which labour among you, and are over you in the Lord, and admonish you; And to esteem them very highly in love for their work’s sake… –1 Thessalonians 5:13. But there is to be a God-given loyalty to those spiritual fathers who labor over us and bring us to birth beyond the many instructors upon life’s pathway. The contemporary emergence of thousands of “hit and run” ministries should cause us concern.

While public confession of sin is obviously an important doctrine of Christ to accompany salvation, these confessions belong in the hands of the spiritual authorities who can discern the situation and help further the soul through tomorrow’s temptations. When those who know the convert are personally engaged, a more thorough and honest examination can be employed to bring about a sincere conversion. This will lay the groundwork for the deep digging required to lay the foundation upon the Rock and establish the soul, both in the home and in the church.

…Engineered Faith

When people are continually subject to revival scenes, there is often an unspoken expectation that the meetings are the place to do business with God. This has a tendency to confuse “saving faith” with a “saving act”. The emphasis on “coming forward to receive Christ” confuses the meaning of faith. Christ is the strong consolation, to whom we … have fled for refuge to lay hold upon the hope set before us: Which hope we have as an anchor of the soul, both sure and stedfast… –Hebrews 6:18-19.(emphasis mine)

The invitation of Christ to …Come unto me… Matthew 11:28, should never be confused with “coming to the altar” (walking to the front). The foolishness of preaching is the invitation, and “Christ” is the destination. The power of the oration shall not lie in the dynamics of the preacher but within the truth of the message. We become like paper figures, having no power at all in ourselves. All power must come from above; all methods used must also come from above. –Watchman Nee ***

The wind bloweth where it listeth… John 3:8, likewise the Holy Spirit, and the preacher must be content with that. I trust that many who give altar calls have the best of intentions and do not wish to circumvent the Spirit. But most works accomplished in the apex of emotion have a strong inclination to be fallacious. So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God –Romans 10:17.

Endnotes:

* “Charles Spurgeon, well known for his evangelistic abilities, firmly refused to adopt the practice of altar calls and he severely criticized it. He viewed the altar call as a method to force decisions as results, but he recognized its potential abuse and dangers.” Altar Calls – Bill Brenner

‘I should like to go into the enquiry-room.’ I dare say you would, but we are not willing to pander to popular superstition. We fear that in those rooms men are warmed into a fictitious confidence. Very few of the supposed converts of enquiry-rooms turn out well. Go to your God at once, even where you now are. Cast yourself on Christ, at once, ere you stir an inch!’ - Pleading and Encouragement – Charles Haddon Spurgeon – Aug 17, 1841

** What A Revival Of Religion Is – Charles Grandison Finney – The Belknap Press Of Harvard University A “Revival of Religion” presupposes a declension. Almost all the religion in the world has been produced by revivals. God has found it necessary to take advantage of the excitability there is in mankind, to produce powerful excitements among them, before he can lead them to obey. Men are so sluggish, there are so many things to lead their minds off from religion, and to oppose the influence of the gospel that it is necessary to raise an excitement among them, till the tide rises so high as to sweep away the opposing obstacles. They must be so excited that they will break over these counteracting influences, before they will obey God.

*** Spirit Force vs. Psychic Force – Watchman Nee

","section":"ISSUES AFFECTING THE CHURCH","subtitle":null,"title":"The Foolishness of Preaching"},"source_context":{"byline":{"authors":[{"location":"Athens, WI","name":"Lee Rufener"}],"raw":"by Lee Rufener Athens, WI"}},"target_language":"Portuguese","terminology_glossary":{},"translation":{"html":"

Porque Cristo não me enviou para batizar, mas para evangelizar; não em sabedoria de palavras, para que não seja anulada a cruz de Cristo. Porque a pregação da cruz é loucura para os que perecem; mas para nós, que somos salvos, é o poder de Deus. …agradou a Deus, pelo meio da loucura da pregação, salvar os que creem –1 Coríntios –1:17-21.

O mundo cristão moderno aceitou devidamente muitos dos veículos humildes que Deus usou para inaugurar o seu Reino. O nascimento virginal, o berço rude e a mortalha tornaram-se monumentos soberanos dos quais dificilmente podemos prescindir. Até o asno rude é apreciado na Sexta-feira Santa e a velha e rústica cruz tornou-se um emblema espiritual exibido nominalmente em correntes de pescoço e entalhes ornamentais de púlpitos. Enquanto o homem permanece fascinado pelos símbolos tradicionais do evangelho, há um caminho absurdo, escolhido por Deus, que está se tornando cada vez mais desprezado.

Durante séculos, o Evangelho foi proclamado por homens tontos e iletrados (segundo seus homólogos élite e intelectuais). A verdade bíblica falada em simplicidade era, por si só, suficiente para que o Espírito Santo de Deus a usasse para converter o pecador. Embora não falte pregação nos dias de hoje, parece que muito dela é de um tipo diferente da forma original que Cristo exemplificou. Se alguém fosse capaz de articular um floreio de oratórias numa linguagem filosófica acurada teria sido o apóstolo Paulo. Contudo, ele recusou-se a pregar o evangelho dessa maneira, …para que não seja anulada a cruz de Cristo –1 Coríntios 1:17. Pregou com cuidado, para que o sucesso não fosse atribuído à força da arte, e não à própria verdade.

Paulo havia sido instruído na aprendizagem judaica aos pés de Gamaliel e era abundante no entendimento tanto do hebraico quanto do grego, mas ao pregar a cruz de Cristo, deixou de lado seu aprendizado. Falou as palavras do Evangelho numa linguagem desprovida de poder humano, para que a honra pertencente a Cristo não fosse eclipsada pelo seu próprio poder pessoal. Porque dizem as suas cartas que são graves e fortes, mas que a sua presença corporal é fraca, e a sua palavra desprezível –2 Coríntios 10:10. É aqui que a igreja moderna tem desprezado os veículos modestos escolhidos por Cristo e pelos apóstolos, desviando-se para uma rota mais aceitável em nosso tempo. A eficiência contemporânea exige um caminho mais direto até o fim, e se a Bíblia não o proíbe, sentimos que é nossa prerrogativa empregá-lo.

Embora filmes evangélicos, concertos de música, e uma série de outros locais duvidosos de ministério possam ser mencionados, desejo falar principalmente sobre o sistema moderno de convite conhecido como “apelo ao altar”. Embora seja comumente associado às “reuniões à moda antiga” dos últimos dois séculos, é de fato moderno pelo fato de que por quase dezenove séculos ninguém ouvira falar da prática. Evangelistas como George Whitefield, Jonathan Edwards e até John Wesley nunca tinham ouvido falar de tal costume. Mesmo Charles Spurgeon (venerado como o “Príncipe dos Pregadores”) criticou-o fortemente e recusou-se a adotá-lo.*

Assim, observamos que a prática não nasceu na igreja apostólica. Não se encontra no ministério de Jesus, nem de seus apóstolos, nem mesmo na igreja do período pós-apostólico. Vemos Jesus e os apóstolos convidando homens e mulheres a virem a Cristo e serem salvos, mas nunca por meio deste método particular. Então, por que essa prática tornou-se uma ferramenta tão essencial em muitas igrejas evangélicas e em muitas igrejas anabatistas hoje? A resposta—resultados pragmáticos. Imediatamente após o sermão, a congregação canta um hino durante o qual o pregador chama homens e mulheres a caminhar até a frente do auditório (ao “altar”) para tomar uma decisão pública por Cristo. A salvação é oferecida a todos os que apenas forem à frente e a receberem. Aqueles que vêm frequentemente recebem a atenção pessoal de um conselheiro para orar com eles e conduzi-los através da confissão.

Essa prática foi projetada para encorajar decisões e obter resultados. E assim o fez. E com pequenas variações o novo método espalhou-se com crescente popularidade por Charles Finney, e mais tarde, Dwight L. Moody, e finalmente, para praticamente todo o evangelismo dos séculos XIX e XX. Peter Cartwright, Sam Jones, R. A. Torrey, Billy Sunday, Bob Jones, Gipsy Smith, John R. Rice, Billy Graham e George Brunk todos empregaram o método com impressionante sucesso. Assim, o sistema de convite tornou-se a prática normal aceita e aqueles que o questionam são frequentemente tidos como espiritualmente excêntricos.

Por que deveríamos contestar a prática se as Escrituras não a proíbem? A resposta reside na questão da propriedade do sistema de convite. Notemos primeiro que as Escrituras abundam em convites à salvação. Ofertas tais como, Vinde a mim, …e eu vos aliviarei –Mateus 11:28, e, …Se alguém tem sede, venha a mim e beba –João 7:37, são ofertas maravilhosas de vida para aqueles que confiarem em Cristo. Os apóstolos também não hesitaram em apresentar Cristo como Salvador a todos os que quisessem ouvir sua mensagem.

Pregaram indiscriminadamente, Arrependei-vos, pois, e convertei-vos, para que sejam apagados os vossos pecados… –Atos 3:19, e …rogamos-vos por Cristo: sede reconciliados com Deus –2 Coríntios 5:20. E testificaram …aos judeus, e também aos gregos, arrependimento para com Deus, e fé em nosso Senhor Jesus Cristo –Atos 20:21. Com tudo isso, todo cristão não apenas deveria concordar como também alegrar-se.

Finalmente, …compeli-os a entrarem, para que a minha casa se encha –Lucas 14:23, é outro versículo bíblico que poderia ser usado para apoiar o método do apelo ao altar. Ainda assim, isso nada diz para fortalecer a correção do apelo ao altar. Ao examinarmos a prática em suas raízes, não podemos deixar de observar algumas deficiências:

…Extrabíblico

Isto não é uma crítica às multidões que encontraram salvação em tal evento. Os anjos no céu regozijam-se com o arrependimento de todo pecador, não importa como ele chegue lá. Desejamos simplesmente manter à vista a simplicidade da loucura da pregação para salvar os que creem. O apelo ao altar é usado como um acréscimo específico ao sermão para trazer à fruição aquilo que a loucura da pregação em si não poderia fazer.

O apelo ao altar ganhou popularidade na década de 1830 com a pregação de Charles G. Finney, que escreveu: “Um avivamento não é um milagre, nem dependente de um milagre, em nenhum sentido. É um resultado puramente filosófico do uso correto dos meios constituídos.” ** Não podemos acusar todos os que praticam o apelo ao altar de crerem nisso, mas é revelador que o pregador que o popularizou parecesse compará-lo mais a uma equação matemática do que a um envolvimento divino.

Quando a verdade cai no solo de um coração bom e honesto, a semente verdadeiramente cria raízes e produz fruto. Essa semente da verdade não precisa de traje artificial. Brilha com a maior majestade à sua própria luz e prevalece no mundo por sua autoridade divina. É uma demonstração do Espírito, sem necessidade de invenção ou intervenção humana. A pregação simples de um Cristo crucificado é mais poderosa do que toda a oratória, filosófica e modos comoventes do mundo.

…Impulso Emocional

O apelo ao altar exige que o buscador deixe seu assento e caminhe até a frente em busca de perdão. Esses convites são frequentemente precedidos por relatos comoventes, histórias tristes ou testemunhos que agitam as emoções em medo, culpa ou arrependimento. Amparadas por um hino suave cantado pela congregação, as emoções estão maduras para avançar. Aqueles que escolhem arrepender-se em seu assento sem responder são frequentemente considerados como “perdendo uma oportunidade”.

E estes são os que foram semeados em terreno pedregoso; os quais, quando ouviram a palavra, logo a recebem com alegria; e não têm raiz em si mesmos, e duram apenas por algum tempo: depois, quando surge alguma tribulação ou perseguição por causa da palavra, logo se escandalizam –Marcos 4:16-17. Recusamo-nos a deduzir que todos os que se converteram sob esse tipo de ministério são ouvintes de solo pedregoso. Contudo, a vasta maioria dos que a recebem num ambiente emocionalmente carregado muitas vezes terá uma conversão menos que sincera.

Certa vez tive um cliente exuberante na minha loja que me informou que sua igreja havia patrocinado um ministério evangélico nacional para pregar na escola pública secundária. “Houve mais de 400 decisões por Cristo!” Embora todos desejemos regozijar-nos com os anjos, não se pode deixar de questionar quantos deles ainda estariam na igreja um ano depois. Embora a falta de verdadeiro compromisso possa não recair apenas sobre o uso do apelo ao altar, podemos ter certeza de que a semente tão rápida em brotar manifestar-se-á nos atalhos de um convite emocional. Aqueles que não têm raiz fariam melhor em nunca terem respondido prematuramente.

Conversões produzidas por canais emocionais são frequentemente questionáveis e transitórias. Impulsos do Espírito Santo não necessitam de força, sabedoria ou esforços humanos para se manifestarem. Métodos de avivamento tais como gritos, choro ostensivo, música que provoca emoção e a narração de histórias sentimentais são a arte feita pelo homem de pregar. Também se encontram em muitos outros lugares públicos projetados para evocar uma resposta predeterminada do ouvinte. Cada uma dessas dimensões é bastante natural ao comportamento humano e, por vezes, pode haver uma linha tênue entre o que é aceitável e inaceitável na pregação. Deve-se ter grande cuidado para que não criemos um clímax emocional e eclipse a mensagem de maneira desordenada para que o poder não seja dos homens e sim de Cristo.

…Apropriação da Autoridade Parental e da Igreja Local

Crianças são frequentemente alvos nesse momento. Podem sentir-se culpadas por alguma travessura infantil, mas uma mensagem inflamável seguida de súplicas emocionais pode ser muito perturbadora. São ocasiões em que um pai deveria falar ao coração de seu filho e conectar-se de maneira espiritual. Em vez disso, muitas vezes a criança é levada à frente e entregue a um conselheiro da igreja para desabafar sua confissão.

Conheço uma mulher cujo pai era um pregador itinerante evangélico. Ela afirma que respondeu “centenas de vezes” ao apelo ao altar. Uma avaliação casual e honesta revelaria que, embora o apelo ao altar possa iniciar muitas conversões sinceras, ele também se presta igualmente a uma série de decisões prematuras e compromissos impulsionados por pressão. Isso frequentemente deixa muitas almas instáveis rebolando em instabilidade espiritual e lutando com a falta de certeza da salvação por anos a fio.

Porque, ainda que tenhais milhares de mestres em Cristo, não tendes muitos pais: porque em Cristo Jesus eu vos gerei pelo evangelho. Por isso vos rogo que sejais meus imitadores –1 Coríntios 4:15-16. Deus ordenou pais e mães para gerar seus filhos, tanto físicos quanto espirituais.

Sede meus imitadores, como também eu sou de Cristo –1 Coríntios 11:1. O itinerante evangelista habilidoso não tem intenção de gerar filhos espirituais e fazer seguidores de si mesmo. Isso ele deixa para outros, pois encontrou seu dom em compelir pessoas a tomar decisões.

E rogamos-vos, irmãos, que conheçais os que trabalham entre vós, e que presidem sobre vós no Senhor, e que vos aconselham; e que os tenhais em grande estima e amor por causa do seu trabalho… –1 Tessalonicenses 5:13. Mas deve haver uma lealdade dada por Deus àqueles pais espirituais que trabalham sobre nós e nos geram além dos muitos instrutores no caminho da vida. O surgimento contemporâneo de milhares de ministérios “pá e corra” deveria nos causar preocupação.

Embora a confissão pública do pecado seja obviamente uma doutrina importante de Cristo a acompanhar a salvação, essas confissões pertencem às mãos das autoridades espirituais que podem discernir a situação e ajudar a encaminhar a alma diante das tentações de amanhã. Quando aqueles que conhecem o convertido estão pessoalmente envolvidos, pode-se empregar um exame mais completo e honesto para efetivar uma conversão sincera. Isso lançará a base para a escavação profunda necessária para estabelecer o fundamento sobre a Rocha e firmar a alma, tanto no lar quanto na igreja.

…Fé Engendrada

Quando as pessoas estão continuamente sujeitas a cenas de avivamento, há frequentemente uma expectativa tácita de que as reuniões sejam o lugar para tratar os assuntos com Deus. Isso tende a confundir “fé salvadora” com um “ato salvador”. A ênfase em “vir à frente para receber Cristo” confunde o significado da fé. Cristo é a forte consolação, para quem nós …fugimos para nos apegar à esperança que nos está proposta: a qual temos como âncora da alma, tanto segura quanto firme… –Hebreus 6:18-19. (ênfase minha)

O convite de Cristo para …Vinde a mim… Mateus 11:28, nunca deve ser confundido com “vir ao altar” (caminhar até a frente). A loucura da pregação é o convite, e “Cristo” é o destino. O poder da oratória não deverá residir na dinâmica do pregador, mas na verdade da mensagem. Tornamo-nos como figuras de papel, não tendo nenhum poder em nós mesmos. Todo o poder deve vir do alto; todos os métodos usados também devem vir do alto. –Watchman Nee ***

O vento sopra onde quer, …João 3:8, assim também o Espírito Santo, e o pregador deve contentar-se com isso. Confio que muitos que fazem apelos ao altar têm as melhores intenções e não desejam contornar o Espírito. Mas a maioria das obras realizadas no ápice da emoção tende a ser falaciosa. Então a fé vem pelo ouvir, e o ouvir pela palavra de Deus –Romanos 10:17.

Notas finais:

* “Charles Spurgeon, bem conhecido por suas habilidades evangelísticas, recusou firmemente adotar a prática dos apelos ao altar e a criticou severamente. Via o apelo ao altar como um método para forçar decisões como resultados, mas reconhecia seu potencial de abuso e perigos.” Apelos ao Altar – Bill Brenner

‘Eu gostaria de ir à sala de inquirição.’ Eu arriscaria dizer que sim, mas não estamos dispostos a alimentar a superstição popular. Tememos que nessas salas os homens sejam aquecidos em uma confiança fictícia. Muito poucos dos supostos convertidos das salas de inquirição saem-se bem. Vá ao seu Deus agora mesmo, mesmo onde você está. Lança-te sobre Cristo, agora, antes que te movas sequer um centímetro!’ - Pleading and Encouragement – Charles Haddon Spurgeon – 17 de ago. de 1841

** O Que É Um Avivamento Religioso – Charles Grandison Finney – The Belknap Press Of Harvard University Um “Avivamento da Religião” pressupõe um declínio. Quase toda a religião no mundo foi produzida por avivamentos. Deus achou necessário aproveitar a excitabilidade que há na humanidade, para produzir poderosas excitações entre eles, antes que possa levá-los a obedecer. Os homens são tão lentos, há tantas coisas para desviar suas mentes da religião, e para opor-se à influência do evangelho que é necessário levantar uma excitação entre eles, até que a maré suba tanto a ponto de varrer os obstáculos opostos. Eles devem ficar tão excitados que ultrapassarão essas influências contrárias, antes de obedecerem a Deus.

*** Força do Espírito versus Força Psíquica – Watchman Nee
